title: Functional Genomics Scientist
description:
The opportunity

Substrate is building a network of fully autonomous wet labs, cloud-based data production facilities for AI biology, integrated with foundation models to become the critical infrastructure layer for AI-driven biological discovery. Our first node opens in King’s Cross, London, with several integrated workcells and two scientific verticals online by mid-2027. Our customers range from foundation model labs to global pharma.

We are hiring across three tiers — Lab Technician, Scientist, and Principal Scientist in functional genomics. This is the second scientific vertical we are bringing online, alongside protein science. The vertical covers cell line engineering, perturbation library design, screen execution, and bulk and single-cell sequencing readouts, with the resulting data feeding customer pipelines that include foundation model training for virtual cell models. Manual development of the day-1 screening workflow is starting now, and full autonomous execution on workcells is targeted for mid-to-late 2027. You will be the bench scientists who develop, validate, and operate the screens through that transition: running them by hand, setting reproducibility and quality thresholds, working alongside automation engineers as the screens move onto instrumentation, and validating equivalence at every step. The Head of Functional Genomics you will work under is being hired alongside you.

About Substrate

Substrate is spinning out of Automata, the UK lab automation company that has built the workcell platform our labs run on. Our four co-founders are Mostafa ElSayed (CEO and founder of Automata), Oli Hoy (formerly VP Customer Experience at Automata), Alexey Morgunov (AI Scientist co-founder, leading the intelligence software product), and a Founding Biology Lead joining shortly. We are aiming to have ramped up to 32 people by the end of Q1 2027.

We are funded in parallel by a combination of venture funding and government grants. We are not a cloud lab and we are not a CRO. We are an autonomous lab platform with closed-loop integration available as one operating mode for foundation model partners.

The role

You will be at the bench. The work is to develop, validate, and operate the screens that will eventually run autonomously on Substrate’s workcells. In the first phase, that means manual screen development: cell line preparation, library cloning and QC, lentivirus production, screen execution, sequencing sample prep, and the readout pipeline — all by hand, setting reproducibility and quality thresholds, and proving each step out before it moves onto instrumentation. As the workcells arrive, the work shifts toward instrumented execution, equivalence validation, and the engineering judgement calls that decide which manual steps get automated and which stay in human hands.

We are hiring across three levels:

  • Principal Scientists own a slice of the screening workflow end to end: scoping it with the Head, designing the manual protocol, validating it to acceptance thresholds, authoring the SOPs that translate to workcell design, and seeing it through to automated execution.

  • Scientists work alongside Principal Scientists at the bench, executing the experiments, contributing to validation work, and growing into protocol authorship over the first year.

  • Lab Technicians are the hands-on execution layer: following established SOPs, preparing reagents and consumables, maintaining equipment, and running routine steps of validated protocols so that Scientists and Principal Scientists can focus on design and troubleshooting decisions.

All three tiers work directly with our automation engineering and software teams on the boundary between scientific protocols and autonomous execution.

What is unusual about the work is that no screen in this vertical is being retrofitted onto automation. Every protocol is designed for AI-in-the-loop execution from the first manual run. The data each screen produces — cell line provenance, library composition, perturbation metadata, sequencing QC, consistency across runs — is treated as a first-class scientific constraint, because that data feeds directly into foundation model training pipelines for our customers. Your decisions at the bench affect what the orchestrator has to do and what data flows back to model partners.

What you will do in your first twelve months

PHASE 0: NOW TO AUG 2026

  • Land in the lab. Set up your bench at our King’s Cross site and start manual screen development alongside the Head of Functional Genomics.

  • Get hands on the day-1 wedge as the Head scopes it: which cell line, which library, which sequencing readout. Run the early steps by hand and capture the data structure and metadata decisions that will translate to workcell design.

  • For Principal Scientists: contribute to the day-1 wedge decisions and begin authoring SOPs for your slice of the screening workflow. Help interview the Scientists and Lab Technicians joining alongside.

PHASE 1: SEP TO DEC 2026

  • Develop and validate the first screens manually. Set the reproducibility and quality thresholds that will serve as acceptance criteria for the moves to instrumented and to fully autonomous execution.

  • Co-design protocols with the software and automation engineering teams so that the manual versions you validate are automation-ready by design. Decide which manual judgement calls have to be engineered out before they hit a workcell.

  • Contribute to co-design conversations with the first commercial customers, including the foundation model partners coming online from 2027.

PHASE 2: JAN TO MAR 2027

  • Workcells arrive in the lab. Move the validated screens onto them, running with instrumentation and human intervention in the loop. Validate equivalence against your manual baselines and triage failures.

  • Open the screening menu to customers via manual and semi-automated services. Run real experiments for real customers.

  • Help bring on the next Scientists and Lab Technicians as the vertical grows.

Who you are

You are a functional genomics scientist who is excited about doing the actual work — designing, running, validating, and iterating on screens at the bench. You are comfortable in the detail. You have done at least one screening modality end to end. The shape of the problem is what attracts you: screens that have to be designed for autonomous execution from day one, in a business where the data the lab produces is itself part of the product.

You write good SOPs. You hold yourself and your colleagues to clear reproducibility thresholds. You are pragmatic about being hands-on in the early phase, with cadence that will be heavy in the manual development phase and ease as protocols move onto instrumentation. You enjoy working at the boundary with non-biologist colleagues — automation engineers, software engineers, AI researchers — and you do not require them to be scientifically fluent before you will collaborate with them.

We are hiring across three tiers — Lab Technician, Scientist, and Principal Scientist. The shape of the work is hands-on bench science at all levels, with collaboration into automation and software. The difference is depth of ownership, design authority, and team responsibility.

MUST HAVE for all three tiers

  • Hands-on cell culture experience, including CL2 wet-lab work with mammalian cell lines.

  • Hands-on experience in at least one component of pooled screening: cell line preparation, library cloning and QC, lentivirus production, screen execution, or sequencing sample prep.

  • Comfortable executing protocols at the bench through manual, semi-automated, and instrumented phases.

  • Track record of working alongside non-scientist colleagues (automation, software, computational) on a shared workflow.

MUST HAVE – Lab Technician

  • Relevant hands-on lab experience (including A-level lab work, apprenticeships, or technician roles) is the primary consideration.

  • Comfortable following written SOPs precisely and flagging deviations. You do not need to design experiments, but you do need to execute them reliably and communicate clearly when something looks off.

  • Hands-on familiarity with basic wet lab techniques: pipetting, buffer preparation, sample handling, and equipment maintenance. Experience in a cell biology, genomics, or molecular biology lab setting is helpful but not required.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, early-stage environment where protocols are still being written. You are methodical, safety-conscious, and do not take shortcuts.

MUST HAVE – Scientist

  • Three or more years of post-PhD or equivalent industry experience in functional genomics, cell biology, or molecular biology with a screening-adjacent focus.

  • Strong hands-on competence in cell culture and in at least one of: library cloning, lentivirus production, single-cell capture, or NGS sample prep.

  • Ready to grow into protocol authorship and SOP ownership over the first 12 months.

MUST HAVE – Principal Scientist

  • Seven or more years of experience in functional genomics or related disciplines (target validation, perturbation screening), with at least one screening modality (CRISPR knockout, CRISPRi knockdown, or analogous) run end to end: cell line preparation, library design, screen execution, sequencing readout, and hit calling.

  • SOP and protocol authorship that other scientists have run successfully.

  • Has supervised at least one junior scientist or technician.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Hands-on experience in cell line engineering, particularly iPSC differentiation or CRISPR-edited stable cell line generation.

  • Direct experience moving screens from manual workflows onto lab automation platforms.

  • Familiarity with structured experimental data capture, LIMS, ELN, or analogous data infrastructure.

  • Experience working with computational or AI/ML colleagues on closed-loop perturbation programmes.

  • Background at an AI-native biotech or foundation model company.

Why this is unusual

Most functional genomics bench roles in industry sit either inside a pharma R&D group (slow iteration, internal customers only), inside a CRO (external customers, faster iteration, but optimised for service throughput rather than scientific decisions about screen design), or inside an AI-native biotech (fast iteration, but a single internal customer in the company’s own pipeline). This is none of the three. You will be developing screens that have to be automation-ready from the first manual experiment, working alongside foundation model labs on closed-loop programmes that do not have a precedent in any of those settings, and contributing to the proprietary dataset programme that turns the lab itself into a commercial asset.

It is also a functional genomics role with significant software and AI surface area. The way you design and run screens affects what the orchestrator has to do, what data flows back to model partners, and which manual judgements get re-engineered out of the workflow. Some scientists find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are.

Compensation and equity

We pay competitively against the London market for functional genomics scientists at venture-backed companies, with bands calibrated to seniority and to the specific scope of the role. We will discuss numbers with serious candidates after first conversations.

Options on the standard four-year vest with a one-year cliff. The specific quantum varies by seniority and we will discuss it with serious candidates.

How we work

Working pattern is in-person and lab-based. You will be at our King’s Cross site most days; that’s where the experiments are. Some flexibility for desk-based work — protocol writing, data analysis, reading — but the cadence is set by the science.

30 days annual leave. A learning budget you can use for conferences, courses, books, and time. The founding team operates on a weekly cadence with a Monday planning meeting and a Friday close, and a quarterly offsite. We are direct with each other, we write things down, and we expect to be challenged.

The team you will join

You will report to the Head of Functional Genomics, who is being hired alongside this team. Until they are in seat, your interim manager is Alexey Morgunov, our science and AI focused co-founder. You will work most closely with the other functional genomics scientists at the bench, with the Lab Technicians who execute alongside you, with the protein science team across the other vertical, and with the software and automation engineering teams on the boundary between scientific protocols and autonomous execution.

You are joining a vertical that is being built from scratch. Substrate is currently three co-founders growing to roughly 32 people by the end of Q1 2027.

How to apply

Apply via Ashby with whatever you think shows your work best: a CV, a published paper or technical report you are proud of, a protocol you have written, a problem you fixed at the bench that you think makes the point. We read everything that comes in.

LAB TECHNICIAN

Our process is two stages. A short initial conversation with the hiring manager (Alexey, or the Head of Functional Genomics once in seat) to understand your background and what you are looking for. Followed by an in-person lab visit at our King’s Cross site, where we will walk through some practical bench scenarios, final questions and introduce you to the team.

SCIENTIST

Our process is two stages. An initial conversation with the hiring manager (Alexey, or the Head of Functional Genomics once in seat) to understand what you want from the role and what we want from it. Followed by an in-person lab visit and meet-the-team session at our King’s Cross site, covering your scientific background, bench skills, scope, and any final questions.

PRINCIPAL SCIENTIST

Our process is four stages. An initial conversation with the hiring manager. Followed by a short technical design exercise: a 2–4 hour take-home testing your design judgment on running a functional genomics campaign end to end. We send the brief after the first conversation. Followed by a technical session walking through your exercise, your scientific track record, and how you have built and led a small bench team. Finally, an in-person founder-team session at our King’s Cross site covering scope, terms, and any final questions.

We aim to move fast on candidates we are excited about; expect roughly two to three weeks end to end.

If you are not sure whether you are a fit, send a note anyway. The most useful conversations we have had so far have been with people who were not sure.

Substrate is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background.

title: Hardware Systems Architect
location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic trains and serves frontier AI models on some of the largest and most diverse accelerator fleets in the world, and the hardware those models run on is one of the most direct levers we have on capability, cost, and reliability. Our Hardware Systems team owns the system-level architecture of that compute — from the package boundary out through boards, racks, interconnect, power, cooling, and the datacenter interface.

We're hiring senior hardware systems architects and technical leads who can work broadly across the hardware stack and go deep where it's needed, and who have the judgment to make and own directional calls — what to build, what to buy, what to co-design with a partner. You'll set architecture, write the specs that partners and internal teams build against, and own the validation and qualification strategy that proves the result.

The skillsets we need span power, cooling, mechanical, interconnect, signal integrity, data and control plane, system management, reliability and serviceability — applied across networking, compute, storage, and accelerator systems.

You'll work closely with our ML performance, infrastructure software, supply chain, and datacenter teams, and directly with hardware vendors and partners across the stack. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a genuine collaborator — we expect this team to push on what AI-assisted hardware design and review can look like.

Key responsibilities

  • Own system path-finding and architecture for your domain across the breadth of compute Anthropic deploys — from concept and requirements through spec, design review, and deployment — and act as a reviewer and thought partner across the others.
  • Write and own high-level requirements and specifications — system, board, interface, rack — that partners and internal teams build against.
  • Review partner and vendor designs against our requirements, make the build / buy / co-design calls with supply chain and partnership teams, and surface misalignment or schedule risk early enough to act on it.
  • Drive the interconnect and networking architecture that ties our systems together — scale-up and scale-out fabrics, NICs and switches, optics, and topology.
  • Drive board-, chassis-, and system-level architecture with our partners — major component placement, PCB architecture, connector and cable design, and power and thermal budgeting — at the chassis, rack, and data-hall level.
  • Develop performance simulations, hardware models, and "what-if" scenarios to evaluate and choose between candidate hardware architectures.
  • Define validation, bring-up, and qualification strategy for new platforms — including the telemetry and reliability targets they need to hit in the fleet — and track the technology roadmaps and vendor landscape that shape what we deploy in the short and long term.
  • Partner with ML performance and infrastructure software teams so hardware decisions land well for the workloads that actually run on them.
  • Help shape how hardware engineering operates at Anthropic — develop and apply AI-assisted approaches to design, spec review, and validation; establish review forums, spec standards, and partner engagement.

Minimum qualifications

  • Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one core hardware-systems domain (e.g., interconnect, power, thermal) for large-scale compute or networking systems.
  • Experience owning hardware system architecture at scale — machine, rack, row, and cluster — and authoring specifications and requirements.
  • Experience taking hardware from architecture through bring-up and high-volume production deployment.
  • Experience working with external hardware vendors and partners — reviewing their designs and holding them to a specification.
  • Ability to reason about trade-offs across adjacent hardware domains (e.g., interconnect ↔ power ↔ thermal ↔ mechanical) rather than within a single one.
  • Track record of technical leadership — owning directional decisions and their consequences, and driving alignment across teams and partners.
  • Comfort operating with high autonomy and limited process in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.
  • Strong written communication — you'll write specs and reviews that many teams depend on.

Preferred qualifications

  • 8+ years in hardware systems architecture or engineering for hyperscale, HPC, AI/ML, or high-end networking platforms.
  • Experience with AI accelerator systems (GPU, TPU, or other custom ASIC platforms) and their scale-up / scale-out fabrics.
  • Familiarity with the chip-package-system interface and co-design.
  • Experience establishing a new function, program, or engineering practice.
  • Comfort working with — and curiosity about pushing — AI tools as part of an engineering workflow.
  • Degree in EE, CE, ME, CS, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Depth in one or more of:
    • High-speed SerDes, PCIe/CXL, Ethernet/InfiniBand, and optical interconnect.
    • BMC and platform firmware, hardware root of trust, and secure boot.
    • 48V/HVDC power delivery and direct liquid cooling.
    • Fleet-scale reliability engineering and RAS architecture.
    • Signal and power integrity.

Representative projects

  • Define the scale-up and scale-out interconnect architecture for a next-generation training platform, from link budget and topology through switch / NIC / optics selection and the bring-up and validation plan.
  • Architect the management and control plane for a new hardware system: BMC and host control, power / reset sequencing, secure boot and attestation, and the telemetry surface the fleet needs.
  • Own the rack-level power and thermal architecture for a liquid-cooled accelerator rack, and the interface spec between that rack and the datacenter that hosts it.
  • Build the reliability model and RAS strategy for a multi-thousand-node fleet — failure budgets, derating policy, telemetry requirements, and serviceability targets — and drive the design changes that hit them.
  • Run the technical evaluation of a partner's proposed system design against our requirements, write up where it falls short, and drive the changes end to end.
  • Prototype an AI-assisted workflow for partner design review and spec consistency checking, and put it to work on a live platform.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$320,000—$485,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. title: Systems Specialist II

Systems Specialist II


The Department of Protein Sciences at Genentech is seeking a talented, high-spirited automation specialist to join a world-class team focused on generating target proteins that support small- and large-molecule drug discovery.


This highly collaborative role sits at the interface of protein expression, cell engineering, research biology, and other groups. You will work closely with scientists and group leaders across and beyond the Drug Discovery organization to enhance protein production, nucleic acid library generation, cell line development, and the exploration of new therapeutic modalities.

This position is based in South San Francisco, on site.

The Opportunity

  • Engage closely with scientists and automation specialists to implement and support automated workflows for molecular biology, cell culture, purification, screening, and characterization.

  • Operate and troubleshoot key instruments, integrated systems, and automated workflows.

  • Train and provide ongoing support to end users of automated workflows in the department, helping drive adoption and best practices.

  • Perform routine precision/accuracy assessments and coordinate instrument maintenance as needed.

  • Identify and drive improvements to increase throughput, robustness, and operational efficiency.


Who You Are (Required)

  • Master’s degree in Biology or a closely related field (e.g., Biochemistry, Engineering) and 1-2 years of related work experience.

  • Operational expertise in laboratory automation, programming, data management, and/or process management.

  • Knowledge of one or more scripting/programming languages (e.g., Java, C#, Python).

  • Experience integrating liquid handlers, robotic arms, automated incubators, plate readers, and/or plate washers into fully automated systems.

  • Experience integrating laboratory equipment with Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS).

  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot and resolve issues in automated processes.

  • A mindset for guiding and supporting users to enable broader adoption of automation in their workflows.

  • Experience converting bench-top or manually conducted assays/protocols into robust, fully automated routines.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Knowledge of basic scientific principles in biology, chemistry, biochemistry, and/or protein engineering is a plus.

Preferred experience

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. title: People Business Partner
description:
People Business Partner

The People Business Partner (PBP) serves as a strategic advisor to leaders and a trusted partner to employees, helping the organization achieve business objectives through effective people strategies. This role is responsible for partnering with operational, clinical, and functional leaders to drive organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, talent development, employee engagement, performance management, change management, and employee relations.

The PBP operates at both a strategic and executional level—helping leaders solve complex people challenges while also designing and implementing scalable programs, processes, and solutions that support organizational growth. The successful candidate combines strong business acumen, sound judgment, data-driven decision making, and exceptional relationship-building skills to influence outcomes and improve organizational performance.

This position is hybrid, with three days a week working at our headquarters in Scottsdale, Arizona, and two days a week working remotely.

Compensation

  • First-year compensation $90,000 - $120,000 annually (DOE)
  • Bonuses driven by self-care, professional development, and individual KPIs
  • $1,200 annual technology allowance
  • 401(k) company match up to 3%
  • Competitive Benefits – We offer competitive benefits including medical, dental, vision, EAP, life insurance, voluntary short-term, and employer-paid long-term disability. Generous PTO which includes 80 hours of vacation, 40 hours of sick leave, seven holidays, PLUS Winter Break (the last week of December). For those in the military reserves we offer 80 hours of paid military leave, and after one year of employment we offer 80 hours of Parental Leave for each birth/adoption.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, or related field.
  • Minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible HR experience, including business partnership responsibilities.
  • Strong knowledge of employee relations, performance management, talent management, workforce planning, and employment law.
  • Experience conducting workplace investigations and managing sensitive employee matters.
  • Demonstrated success influencing leaders and driving organizational change.
  • Experience using HR metrics and workforce analytics to support business decisions.
  • Ability to build credibility and trust across all levels of the organization.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, coaching, and consulting skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • PHR, SPHR, SHRM-CP, or SHRM-SCP certification.
  • Experience supporting healthcare, multi-site operations, or high-growth organizations.
  • Experience in private equity-backed or high-growth environments.
  • Experience with HRIS, workforce analytics, and reporting tools.
  • Strong project management and process improvement capabilities.

Core Competencies

Business Acumen

Leadership Coaching

Workforce Planning

Organizational Effectiveness

Change Management

Data Analysis & Analytics

Employee Relations Expertise

Critical Thinking

Project Management

Communication & Influence

Relationship Building

Conflict Resolution

Judgement & Decisiveness

Adaptability & Resilience

Roles & Responsibilities

Strategic Business Partnership

  • Serve as the primary People Team advisor to assigned business units and leaders.
  • Develop a deep understanding of operational priorities, workforce challenges, and organizational objectives.
  • Partner with leaders to align people strategies with business goals.
  • Provide proactive consultation on workforce planning, organizational design, team effectiveness, and talent optimization.
  • Coach leaders on leadership effectiveness, employee development, accountability, and team performance.
  • Build trusted relationships that enable candid conversations and effective problem-solving.

Organizational Effectiveness & Workforce Planning

  • Partner with leaders to assess workforce needs and develop staffing strategies that support organizational growth.
  • Facilitate talent reviews, succession planning discussions, and workforce planning exercises.
  • Identify talent risks and organizational capability gaps and develop actionable mitigation plans.
  • Support organizational restructuring, team design, role clarity, and workforce optimization initiatives.
  • Analyze organizational trends and recommend solutions that improve performance and scalability.

Talent Management & Leadership Development

  • Lead talent planning initiatives that identify high-potential employees and future leaders.
  • Partner with Learning & Development to support leadership capability building and career development programs.
  • Facilitate development planning conversations and talent calibration processes.
  • Support leaders with coaching, performance feedback, and employee development strategies.
  • Promote internal mobility and succession planning efforts throughout the organization.

Performance Management

  • Guide leaders through the performance management process from goal setting through annual reviews.
  • Support calibration discussions and performance evaluations to ensure consistency and fairness.
  • Partner with leaders to address performance concerns and accountability challenges.
  • Coach leaders on delivering effective feedback and conducting difficult performance conversations.
  • Support the development and execution of performance improvement plans and other corrective action processes.

Employee Relations & Investigations

  • Serve as a trusted resource for leaders navigating employee relations concerns.
  • Conduct workplace investigations related to policy violations, employee complaints, and workplace conflicts.
  • Assess risk and provide recommendations that are legally compliant, consistent, and aligned with company values.
  • Facilitate conflict resolution and mediation efforts when appropriate.
  • Partner with leadership and legal counsel on complex employee relations matters when necessary.

Change Management

  • Lead and support organizational change initiatives that impact employees, leaders, and business operations.
  • Develop change management strategies, communication plans, leader toolkits, and implementation plans.
  • Help leaders anticipate resistance and navigate employee concerns through periods of transition.
  • Monitor change effectiveness and recommend adjustments to improve adoption and outcomes.
  • Serve as a cultural steward during organizational transformation efforts.

Employee Experience & Engagement

  • Partner with leaders to foster highly engaged, productive, and inclusive teams.
  • Analyze engagement data and recommend strategies to improve employee retention and experience.
  • Support action planning efforts following engagement surveys and organizational assessments.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen culture, improve communication, and enhance employee satisfaction.
  • Monitor workforce trends and proactively address retention risks.

Policy, Compliance & Risk Management

  • Ensure leaders understand and apply company policies consistently and appropriately.
  • Partner with People Operations to maintain compliance with federal, state, and local employment regulations.
  • Advise leaders on leave administration, accommodations, workplace policies, and employment related risk mitigation.
  • Support audits, compliance initiatives, and regulatory reporting efforts.
  • Assist in the development and maintenance of People Team policies, procedures, and best practices.

People Analytics & Business Insights

  • Utilize workforce data, metrics, and trends to identify business opportunities and organizational risks.
  • Analyze turnover, retention, engagement, hiring, performance, and workforce planning metrics.
  • Translate complex data into actionable recommendations for leaders.
  • Develop and present workforce insights to support strategic decision-making.
  • Measure effectiveness of People Team initiatives and recommend continuous improvements.

Process Improvement & Program Implementation

  • Design, implement, and continuously improve people programs, workflows, and processes.
  • Partner with People Operations, Talent Acquisition, Learning & Development, and Finance to ensure coordinated execution.
  • Lead cross-functional projects that improve scalability, consistency, efficiency, and employee experience.
  • Create tools, resources, leader guides, and communication materials that improve manager capability and process adoption.
  • Identify opportunities for automation and standardization across the employee lifecycle.

About Us

At evolvedMD, we are leading the integration of behavioral health services in modern primary care. How? We use a uniquely upfront, innovative, and ongoing approach that places our clinicians on site and in person at each of the practices we serve. As one of America’s largest and most seasoned companies dedicated to integration, we fully embed behavioral health managers into a collaborative team. evolvedMD is committed to meeting patients where they are most comfortable: whether that is in person and on site at your practice location or virtual. We offer early, comprehensive, and dedicated care to help patients achieve the best possible behavioral health outcomes.

To find out more about what it’s like to work at evolvedMD, visit our Resources and News page at where you can learn about our culture, leaders, innovations, and impact in the community.

title: Lead Scientist II
description:
Are you looking to power the next leap in the exciting world of advanced electronics? Do you want to help solve problems that drive success in the rapidly evolving technology and connectivity landscape? Then bring your problem-solving, passion, and creativity to help us power the next leap in electronics.

At Qnity, we’re more than a global leader in materials and solutions for advanced electronics and high-tech industries – we’re a tight-knit team that is motivated by new possibilities, and always up for a challenge. All our dedicated teams contribute to making cutting-edge technology possible. We value forward-thinking challengers, boundary-pushers, and diverse perspectives across all our departments, because we know we play a critical role in the world enabling faster progress for all. Learn how you can start or jumpstart your career with us.

Position Summary

The Lead Scientist II / Technology Manager will provide technical and organizational leadership for the development of next-generation thermal management materials and technologies. This role combines deep scientific expertise with people, project, and portfolio leadership. The successful candidate will drive innovation from concept through commercialization while managing a team of scientists and engineers focused on advanced thermal interface materials (TIMs), EMI materials, and emerging thermal and EMI solutions for AI datacenters, advanced packaging, automotive electronics, telecommunications, and high-performance computing applications.

The position requires a strong technology vision, the ability to translate market needs into innovation roadmaps, and demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary teams through complex product development programs.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Leadership

  • Define and execute technology roadmaps aligned with business strategy and customer needs.
  • Lead development of next-generation thermal management materials, including TIM1, TIM1.5, TIM2, liquid metal systems, phase change materials, lid seals, and adjacent technologies.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies, competitive landscapes, and intellectual property opportunities.
  • Drive innovation through invention disclosures, patents, publications, and strategic collaborations.
  • Serve as a technical authority for customers, business leaders, sales teams, and executive stakeholders.

Team Leadership & People Development

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a team of scientists, engineers, and technologists.
  • Establish technical priorities, resource allocation, and project staffing plans.
  • Foster a culture of innovation, scientific rigor, collaboration, and accountability.
  • Support recruitment, succession planning, and technical career development.
  • Build strong cross-functional relationships across R&D, Operations, Product Management, Marketing, Quality, and Manufacturing.

Product & Project Leadership

  • Lead strategic product development programs from concept through commercialization.
  • Drive stage-gate execution, technical risk reduction, and development planning.
  • Coordinate global project activities across multiple sites and disciplines.
  • Ensure projects meet technical, timing, cost, quality, and customer objectives.
  • Partner with PMO and business stakeholders to prioritize resources and maximize return on innovation investments.

Customer & Market Engagement

  • Engage directly with key customers to understand system-level challenges and future technology needs.
  • Support design-in activities, technical reviews, and strategic customer engagements.
  • Translate application requirements into differentiated technology and product solutions.
  • Represent the company at industry conferences, consortiums, and technical forums.

Operational Excellence

  • Establish best practices for experimentation, characterization, data analysis, and documentation.
  • Drive continuous improvement in laboratory capabilities and technology development processes.
  • Support manufacturing scale-up, technology transfer, and commercialization efforts.
  • Ensure compliance with safety, quality, and regulatory requirements.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelors’ required, master’s or Ph.D. preferred in Materials Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or related technical field.
  • 10+ years of industrial R&D experience in advanced materials or thermal management technologies.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex technology development programs.
  • Experience managing scientists, engineers, or cross-functional technical teams.
  • Strong understanding of product development, commercialization, and manufacturing scale-up.
  • Proven record of innovation, patents, product launches, or significant technical contributions.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred

  • Expertise in thermal interface materials, liquid metals, phase change materials, advanced polymer composites, fillers, or semiconductor packaging materials.
  • Knowledge on EMI (ELECTRO MAGNETIC INTERFERANCE) material is a plus.
  • Experience supporting AI/datacenter, semiconductor, telecommunications, automotive, aerospace, or electronics markets.
  • Knowledge of thermal modeling, reliability testing, and advanced characterization techniques.
  • Experience managing global teams and multi-site development programs.
  • MBA or formal project/program management training is a plus.

Success Measures

In the first 12-24 months, the successful candidate will:

  • Deliver high-impact technology platforms that support strategic growth objectives.
  • Build and develop a high-performing technical team.
  • Accelerate commercialization of advanced thermal solutions.
  • Generate meaningful intellectual property and competitive differentiation.
  • Improve project execution, resource utilization, and cross-functional alignment.

title: Remote Industrial Engineering SME (FlexSim Expert)
description:
At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe.

The Industrial Engineer SME II serves as a strategic Industrial Engineering leader responsible for planning, designing, implementing, and optimizing integrated manufacturing and service delivery systems that drive performance, reliability, maintainability, schedule adherence, scalability, and cost effectiveness. This role supports regional and global operations, including new manufacturing site development, capacity expansion, factory design, and complex operational transformation initiatives. The successful candidate will leverage advanced industrial engineering methodologies, simulation tools, and data-driven decision making to support business growth and continuous improvement.

How will you make an impact?

As an Industrial Engineering Subject Matter Expert, you will influence strategic manufacturing decisions by developing innovative solutions that improve productivity, reduce costs, optimize facility utilization, and support operational excellence. You will play a critical role in designing and launching new manufacturing operations, leading large-scale industrial engineering projects, and utilizing advanced simulation and analytical tools, including FlexSim, to model, validate, and optimize manufacturing systems.

What will you do?

  • Lead and implement complex industrial engineering projects across site, regional, and global operations.
  • Drive waste elimination and operational excellence through application of Industrial Engineering principles and Lean methodologies.
  • Develop and execute advanced manufacturing models utilizing FlexSim and other simulation tools to evaluate production flows, capacity requirements, labor utilization, material movement, and facility layouts.
  • Lead greenfield and brownfield manufacturing site development projects, including facility planning, line design, equipment layout, staffing models, infrastructure requirements, and operational readiness activities.
  • Critically evaluate workforce utilization, facility layouts, production costs, process flow analysis, and end-to-end value streams to determine optimal operational performance.
  • Conduct complex process simulations, operations research studies, and business case analyses to support strategic decision-making.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert for Industrial Engineering systems, tools, methodologies, and best practices.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives involving Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, Facilities, Quality, and Program Management teams.
  • Prepare complex manufacturing quotations and operational models for new business opportunities, including:
    • End-to-end line design
    • Direct labor and value-add labor planning
    • Equipment and automation sizing
    • Capital investment requirements
    • Facility and infrastructure expansion needs
  • Define and standardize SAP and Manufacturing Execution System (MES) configurations supporting operational excellence.
  • Support business unit and site leadership by evaluating process reliability, profitability, and assumptions related to new programs and manufacturing strategies.
  • Lead Industrial Engineering support for New Product Introduction (NPI) initiatives.
  • Develop and communicate key Industrial Engineering metrics to regional and global stakeholders.
  • Coach, mentor, and develop Industrial Engineers and cross-functional team members.
  • Create and implement new Industrial Engineering best practices and share learnings across regional and global teams.
  • Support Lean transformation initiatives through strong process discipline, data integrity, and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure compliance with all company policies, procedures, security requirements, and safety standards.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

How will you get here?

Education:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related engineering discipline required.
  • Master's Degree in Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business Administration (MBA), or related field preferred.
  • Lean Master Certification, Six Sigma Certification, or equivalent continuous improvement certification preferred.

Experience:

  • Minimum of 12 years of professional experience, including at least 7 years of Industrial Engineering or closely related manufacturing engineering experience.
  • Proven experience leading large-scale manufacturing optimization and operational improvement initiatives.
  • Demonstrated experience in new manufacturing site development, factory launches, facility expansions, capacity planning, and production system design.
  • Significant experience utilizing FlexSim software for manufacturing simulation, capacity analysis, production flow optimization, and network modeling preferred.
  • Experience supporting global manufacturing operations and cross-functional projects in a complex industrial environment.
  • Equivalent combinations of education, training, and experience may be considered.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:

  • Advanced knowledge and practical application of Industrial Engineering methodologies, including:
    • Work measurement
    • Capacity planning
    • Process mapping
    • Facility and workstation design
    • Discrete event simulation
    • Operations research
    • Value stream mapping
    • Labor modeling and optimization
  • Expert-level proficiency with FlexSim simulation software and the use of digital models to optimize manufacturing performance and support investment decisions.
  • Strong understanding of manufacturing site development, production system design, facility planning, and manufacturing startup execution.
  • Knowledge of global manufacturing strategies and operational best practices.
  • Data science, statistical analysis, and advanced analytics skills preferred.
  • Strong financial acumen, including:
    • P&L analysis
    • Capital planning
    • Cost modeling
    • Return on investment analysis
    • Operational budgeting
  • Proven track record of successful change management and continuous improvement implementation.
  • Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Knowledge of health, safety, and environmental standards within manufacturing environments.
  • Understanding of quality systems and manufacturing process controls.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Microsoft Project, Microsoft Visio, AutoCAD, SAP, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and related engineering tools.

title: Research Associate, Molecular Biology
description:
An affiliate of Colossal is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Research Associate to join our interdisciplinary team at the intersection of molecular and developmental biology. This role offers the opportunity to work closely with scientists developing cutting-edge approaches to drive novel applications in the modification of phenotypes in avians. The successful candidate will support ongoing research projects by performing a range of cellular and tissue-based assays, including in situ hybridization, flow cytometry, histology, and immunofluorescence staining.

This role is based in Dallas, TX. Relocation assistance is available.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with developmental biologists to analyze gene expression and function across different developmental stages.
  • Perform in situ hybridization (ISH) to localize and quantify RNA/DNA targets in tissue and whole embryo samples
  • Prepare and process tissue samples for histology, including sectioning, fixation, and staining (H&E and special stains)
  • Perform immunofluorescence (IF) staining and support imaging/microscopy workflows
  • Conduct flow cytometry experiments, including sample preparation, staining panel setup, data acquisition, and basic analysis
  • Screen constructs in developing avian embryos to quantify expression patterns.
  • Produce transfection reagents to aid experimental workflows.
  • Analyze and interpret experimental data, providing recommendations to guide project direction.
  • Participate in meetings, generate reports, and present findings to ensure alignment with project milestones.
  • Maintain accurate, detailed laboratory records and demonstrate strong organizational skills.

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree (B.S./B.A.) in molecular biology, or a related life science field with 1 or more years of hands-on research experience in industry or academic research labs.
  • Hands-on experience in molecular cloning, plasmid construction, and plasmid preparation (mini-, midi-, and maxi-prep).
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience with at least two of the following: microscopy (confocal and/or lightsheet), in situ hybridization, flow cytometry, histology, immunofluorescence staining, (experience with all four strongly preferred)
  • Skilled in PCR primer design and PCR optimization/troubleshooting.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and meet deadlines.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, with demonstrated problem-solving abilities.

Preferred Skills and Abilities

  • Experience handling vertebrate embryos.
  • Familiarity with microscopy/imaging software (e.g., Imaris, ImageJ or similar)
  • Experience with transfection reagents (i.e. lipofectamine or electroporation)
  • Familiarity with high-throughput automation platforms for molecular biology workflows.

title: Director, Linear Product Management for Process Systems & Training
description:
OVERVIEW OF THE COMPANY

Fox Corporation

Under the FOX banner, we produce and distribute content through some of the world’s leading and most valued brands, including: FOX News Media, FOX Sports, FOX Entertainment, FOX Television Stations and Tubi Media Group. We empower a diverse range of creators to imagine and develop culturally significant content, while building an organization that thrives on creative ideas, operational expertise and strategic thinking.

JOB DESCRIPTION

We are seeking a seasoned Director, Linear Product Management to join our Revenue Operations organization. In this role, you will act as the crucial bridge between our organization and our Engineering teams, serving as the ultimate "voice of the customer" in the design and deployment of next-generation linear advertising systems and solutions.

This role requires a deeply experienced professional with a comprehensive understanding of the media buying ecosystem, linear advertising sales, operations, and reporting. You will dive deep into current workflows, pinpoint operational friction, and partner with engineering to architect and deploy automated, scalable solutions. Your responsibility doesn't end at deployment; you will own the entire lifecycle of these tools—from co-designing training and rollout programs to driving end-user adoption and establishing a feedback loop for continuous, iterative improvement.

A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITES

  • Voice of Revenue Operations: Represent the unique needs, pain points, and workflows of the Revenue Operations team to the Engineering organization by turning those prioritized opportunities into end user facing solutions.

  • Workflow Optimization & Automation: Analyze current operational systems and processes to identify inefficiencies, draft clear problem statements, and ideate on automated product solutions.

  • Feature and Release Testing: In partnership with business leads within Revenue Operations, validate the desirability, usability, feasibility & quality of product releases against stated business goals.

  • System Rollout & Training Partnership: Champion the launch of new tools and features by designing comprehensive rollout programs and partnering closely with the Training team to ensure smooth onboarding and high adoption rates.

  • Adoption & Change Management: Drive the end-to-end adoption strategy within Revenue Operations, gathering post-launch feedback via user forums to feed into a continuous cycle of tool optimization and iteration with our Engineering partners.

  • Efficiency Measurement: In partnership with Engineering, define, track, and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure and quantify the operational and workflow efficiencies gained through new tool deployments.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner across teams and organizations to continuously align business strategy with technical execution and end-user rollout.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • Experience in linear advertising operations, with a distinct and heavy focus on ad sales support, client services, master data management, pricing and traffic workflows.

    • Deep, comprehensive knowledge of linear advertising sales end-to-end cross-functional workflows and systems, including OMS and CRM applications

    • Thorough understanding of the agency/advertiser media buying process, from RFPs and proposals to order management and billing reconciliation.

  • Proven capability to map complex operational workflows, identify bottlenecks, and quantify time/cost efficiencies gained through automation.

  • Ability to translate abstract, real-world operational issues into problem statements, goals, and user stories for engineering product teams.

  • Proven track record of successfully implementing, rolling out, and driving adoption for enterprise-level ad tech:

    • Strong background in change management, product adoption strategies, and establishing iterative feedback mechanisms.

    • Experience partnering with training or enablement teams to build learning modules, documentation, and release notes for non-technical users.

  • Proven ability to collaborate with and influence diverse stakeholders across technical and business teams.

  • Exceptional organizational skills with a meticulous eye for detail, particularly in workflow mapping and documentation.

  • Exceptional communication and empathy skills—equally comfortable presenting to leadership, whiteboarding with engineers, and soliciting feedback from end users with varying degrees of industry experience.

title: Campus Safety Officer
description:
St. Norbert College, a nationally ranked, private, Catholic liberal arts college, is seeking a Campus Safety Officer.

This position promotes a safe and secure campus environment by maintaining a visible, uniformed presence and protecting the welfare of students, faculty, staff, and visitors. Campus Safety operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, providing safety and security for the campus community, conference attendees, church members, guests of the Kress Inn, and other visitors.

Campus Safety Officers monitor the safety and security of campus buildings and grounds by locking and unlocking facilities, conducting foot and vehicle patrols, monitoring surveillance cameras, managing alarm and fire systems, responding to suspicious activity, and coordinating with local law enforcement when appropriate. Officers also investigate disturbances, secure campus property, maintain order during campus events, and enforce College policies and regulations.

The regular schedule for this position is 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with every other weekend required. The weekday schedule will adjust based on the assigned weekend rotation.

Specific responsibilities:

  • Patrol campus buildings and grounds on foot and by vehicle to maintain a safe and secure environment, enforce College policies, and monitor security systems.

  • Respond to emergencies, including medical, mental health, fire, and security incidents, providing first aid, CPR/AED, Narcan administration, and coordinating with emergency responders and local law enforcement as needed.

  • Investigate incidents and policy violations by gathering information, reviewing surveillance footage, interviewing witnesses, and preparing detailed reports, including Title IX documentation.

  • Build positive relationships with students, faculty, staff, and visitors by providing assistance, addressing safety concerns, and supporting Residential Education and Housing in enforcing campus regulations.

  • Monitor campus safety systems, identify and report security or facility hazards, respond to alarms, and ensure the proper operation of security and fire protection equipment.

  • Conduct campus safety education and training, including fire drills, emergency preparedness, evacuation procedures, and active threat response training.

  • Assist with traffic and parking management, provide directions and information to campus visitors, and perform other duties as assigned.


Required Minimum Qualifications:

  • Associate degree in public safety services or related field, or enrolled in and have completed at least one year of a relevant Associate Degree program.

  • 1-2 years of experience in Campus Safety, Security, Law Enforcement, or equivalent Military experience.

  • Valid driver’s license.

  • Current first aid/CPR/AED certifications preferred or the ability to obtain.

  • Ability to learn and apply campus safety and security policies, procedures, and emergency response protocols.

  • Strong interpersonal and customer service skills, with the ability to build positive working relationships with students, faculty, staff, visitors, and community partners.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to prepare reports and other documentation.

  • Strong organizational, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to remain calm and exercise sound judgment in stressful situations.

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.

  • Proficiency with computer applications, including Google Workspace and other department-related software.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain certifications for pepper spray and Electronic Control Device (Taser) use.

  • Ability to operate department vehicles and utilize campus safety systems, including the Campus Notification System (CNS).

The College may consider any equivalent amount of credentials, licensures, training, or experience that provides the necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties and responsibilities of this job.

Benefits package:

The College offers an outstanding benefits package including health, dental, vision, and life insurance; retirement plan; paid time-off and tuition waiver.

Application instructions:

This position will be posted for a minimum of five business days, and applications will be reviewed upon receipt until the position is filled.

As the only Norbertine institution of higher learning in the world, our roots, traditions, and commitments create a unique and enriching educational experience for our students.

As a US Compensation & Benefits Partner, you will be a subject matter expert within the global Reward team, responsible for the design, implementation, governance and continuous improvement of compensation and benefits programmes across the Hiscox US Business. You will partner closely with People Leaders, Business Leaders, Finance, Legal, Talent Acquisition and External Advisers to ensure Hiscox maintains competitive, compliant and commercially effective reward programmes that support business objectives and enhance the employee experience.

Your key role will be to act as the US Reward specialist within the Group Reward function, ensuring alignment with global reward strategy, policies and governance whilst partnering closely with US stakeholders to deliver market-relevant compensation and benefits solutions

Operating with significant autonomy, you will provide expert advice on compensation strategy, market positioning, benefit design, regulatory compliance and reward governance. You will leverage data, market insight and stakeholder feedback to make recommendations that drive employee engagement, support talent outcomes and ensure regulatory compliance.

This role requires strong organizational and analytical skills, a customer-focused mindset, and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Act as the primary Compensation & Benefits partner to the US business, providing expert advice and guidance on reward matters including hiring, promotions, organisational design, talent retention and employee pay decisions.

  • Lead the delivery of annual reward activities for the US business, including salary reviews, incentive planning and benefits enrolment, ensuring programmes are competitive, cost-effective and aligned to business strategy.

  • Own and continuously enhance US compensation and benefits programmes, using market intelligence, employee feedback and business insight to ensure Hiscox remains competitive in attracting and retaining talent.

title: Senior Software Development Engineer 5
description:
Overview

Join Adobe’s Experience Platform (AEP) team as a Senior Software Engineer 5 focused on backend systems. You will architect and deliver scalable, high-performance backend solutions powering AI-native applications in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Multi-Agent Collaboration Platform (MCP) environments. This role requires deep technical expertise, leadership in engineering, and a passion for innovation at scale.

Key Responsibilities

Architect and Develop Backend Systems

  • Lead the design and implementation of robust, scalable backend services using Java and Python.

  • Own end-to-end system architecture for AI-native applications, including RAG/MCP multi-agent environments.

  • Define and enforce code standards, guidelines, and architectural patterns for the team.

AI-Native Application Engineering

  • Build and optimize backend components that support AI/ML workflows, including data ingestion, orchestration, and inference pipelines.

  • Collaborate with data scientists and AI engineers to integrate advanced models and agents into production systems.

title: Sr Staff Product Designer, Emerging Agents
description:
The opportunity

We are seeking a Senior Staff Designer to lead the design and delivery of intelligent agentic systems across complex creative and enterprise workflows. This role focuses on building and shipping AI-native capabilities that enable users to delegate, steer, and evaluate intelligent systems with confidence.

This is a systems design role focused on AI behavior, orchestration, and adaptive interfaces. We are looking for a designer who works directly with models, prototypes in code, and treats AI systems as a design material.

What you’ll do

You will lead major initiatives within our agentic systems work, translating emerging AI capabilities into production-ready interaction patterns and driving a coherent vision across research, engineering, and product.

Design and Ship Agentic Interaction Systems

  • Establish mental models for delegation, collaboration, and control between humans and AI agents.

  • Design interaction frameworks for multi-step workflows and tool-using skills.

  • Design mechanisms that make reasoning legible, including confidence indicators, provenance, and evaluation UX.

  • Build patterns that balance prompt-based and structured interaction.

Prototype and Deliver AI-Native Capabilities

  • Work directly with large language models and agent frameworks.

  • Write and refine prompts, skills, system instructions, and behavioral constraints.

  • Prototype in code and contribute to production implementations alongside engineering.

  • Rapidly iterate through build → test → refine cycles in close partnership with research and engineering.

Adapt AI Systems to Creative Contexts

  • Design systems that understand creative workflows, enterprise constraints, memory, and personalization.

  • Ensure agent behaviors align with real creative processes and tooling needs.

  • Contribute to the evolution of AI-native components within Adobe’s design system.

Drive Cross-Functional Execution

  • Partner closely with engineering, research, and product to deliver production systems.

  • Influence stakeholders through working prototypes and clear system articulation.

  • Contribute to shared best practices for AI interaction and behavior design.

What you bring

We are redefining what it means to be a designer in the age of AI.

Core Experience

  • 8+ years of experience in product, systems, or interaction design.

  • Demonstrated experience designing and shipping AI-assisted or agent-based systems.

  • Experience designing for creative tools or deep familiarity with creative workflows.

  • Hands-on experience working with large language models and designing adaptive or generative interfaces.

  • Comfort prototyping in code and contributing production-quality implementations alongside engineering teams.

  • Strong systems thinking and experience working within complex, cross-functional environments.

Additional Depth

  • Experience designing enterprise AI workflows.

  • Familiarity with multi-agent orchestration patterns.

  • Experience integrating first- and third-party AI systems.

  • Background in automation design, developer tooling, or platform ecosystems.

  • Accessibility expertise in AI-driven interfaces.

Preferred Accessibility Design Skills:

  • Experience designing accessible and inclusive interfaces for people with disabilities.

  • Understanding of applying WCAG conformance criteria in design, specifically testing comps, wireframes, and prototypes for accessibility standards.

  • Accessibility certifications CPACC, WAS, CPWA, or ADS from the IAAP preferred.

You think in behaviors, systems, and capabilities, not just screens, flows, and features.

You treat AI systems as a design material and have built workflows or prototypes that explore model behavior under real constraints.

You are energized by ambiguity and motivated to shape how AI becomes a practical, trusted collaborator in creative work.

Most importantly, you believe AI should expand human creativity and capability, not replace it.


To be considered for this role, please submit your resume and portfolio. We’re especially interested in systems you’ve defined, AI workflows you’ve built, and evidence of working directly with intelligent systems.

Utilizing leadership, advocacy and collaboration the School Counselor promotes student success by providing preventive services and responding to identified needs through implementation of a comprehensive school counseling program that helps guide all learners in their academic success, social and emotional development, and career and college planning and readiness.

K12, a Stride Company, believes in Education for ANYONE. We provide families with an online option for a high-quality, personalized education experience. Students can thrive, find their passion, and learn in an environment that encourages discovery at their own pace.

Student success will be measured by valid and reliable assessment data, parent and student satisfaction, and continued institutional growth within the academic community. Join us!

title: Senior Executive, Facilities and Operations
description:
The School of Chemistry, Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology (CCEB) hosts world-class education and research programmes in organic and inorganic chemistry, physical chemistry, chemical engineering, bioengineering and process engineering and synthetic chemistry. We aim to nurture future-ready graduates with the ability to tackle new challenges in chemicals manufacturing, healthcare, energy, food, and other important sectors.

We are seeking a Senior Executive, Facilities and Operations to support the effective running of its facilities, infrastructure and operational functions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate and monitor routine and ad-hoc facilities maintenance works, liaising with vendors and contractors to ensure issues are resolved promptly and service standards are met.

  • Coordinate infrastructure-related improvement projects and renovations, including space-related modifications, to minimise disruption to staff and students.

  • Plan and manage office and cubicle space allocation, analyse space utilisation, and recommend optimisation measures to meet growing demand from faculty and postgraduate students.

  • Support safety-related initiatives, including emergency coordination and contractor management, to maintain a safe and compliant working environment.

  • Identify opportunities to improve existing processes and digitalise workflows, and recommend cost-effective solutions for facilities operations.

title: Senior Systems Engineer - Spaceplane
description:
Join us in developing a remotely operated reusable spaceplane that combines the demanding performance of a rocket with the operational discipline of an aircraft.

We're looking for an experienced Systems Engineer who enjoys taking ownership, solving complex technical problems, and driving engineering decisions across multidisciplinary teams. This is a hands-on technical role for someone who can lead from the front and help shape both the vehicle and the way we engineer it.

If you want a narrow, heavily structured role, this is probably not for you. We are looking for someone practical, organised, and capable of taking ownership in a fast-moving environment.

What You'll Do

Take Ownership of Vehicle Functions

  • Take end-to-end ownership of one or more vehicle functions or systems.
  • Define functional behaviour, requirements, architecture, interfaces, and verification approaches.
  • Drive technical decisions and work closely with propulsion, structures, avionics, GNC, software, operations, and certification teams.
  • Establish verification plans and support execution throughout the development lifecycle to deliver integrated vehicle capabilities.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to engineers working within your functional areas.

Lead Aircraft System Safety

  • Lead Functional Hazard Assessments (FHA) for your assigned functional areas.
  • Develop system-level safety requirements and ensure hazards are effectively mitigated.
  • Perform or contribute to Fault Tree Analysis (FTA), Common Cause Analysis (CCA), and other system safety activities.
  • Support the development of safety cases and certification evidence where required.

Demonstrate System Reliability and Assurance

A key responsibility of this role is ensuring that the reliability statements identified through Functional Hazard Assessments (FHA) are supported by credible engineering evidence.

  • Translate reliability allocations and safety objectives from FHA and other safety analyses into practical verification and qualification activities.
  • Define appropriate combinations of testing, analysis, inspection, similarity, and operational evidence to support reliability claims.
  • Develop qualification and environmental test programmes by deriving realistic vibration, shock, thermal, pressure, and other environmental conditions from expected operational use.
  • Lead qualification and reliability demonstration activities, turning certification and safety objectives into practical engineering programmes.
  • Work closely with design engineers to ensure reliability is designed into systems from the outset and demonstrated through robust engineering evidence.
  • Help establish effective approaches for qualification, reliability demonstration, and engineering assurance across the spaceplane programme.
  • Provide technical justification to support high-confidence reliability claims for critical vehicle functions.

What We're Looking For

You are an experienced engineer who takes ownership, enjoys working across disciplines, and is comfortable making sound technical decisions in complex environments.

We expect applicants to bring strong experience in at least two or three of the following areas:

  • Systems engineering for complex aerospace or other safety-critical systems.
  • Ownership of system functions, including requirements, architecture, interfaces, and verification.
  • Practical qualification and reliability demonstration of structural, mechanical, electrical, or avionics systems.
  • Functional Hazard Assessment (FHA). Fault Tree Analysis (FTA), Common Cause Analysis (CCA), or reliability engineering.
  • Environmental qualification testing, including development of test requirements and profiles.
  • Flight test, vehicle integration, verification, and validation.
  • Aircraft, spacecraft, launch vehicle, advanced unmanned aircraft, or other highly integrated safety-critical systems.

What Makes You Successful

  • You quickly understand the strengths and capabilities of a team, adapt your approach accordingly, and raise the technical standard by leading through example.
  • You naturally take ownership and drive work through to completion.
  • You can understand complex systems and make pragmatic engineering decisions.
  • You enjoy building practical engineering solutions rather than simply following process.
  • You communicate clearly and influence technical direction through sound engineering judgement.
  • You enjoy mentoring others and helping teams deliver higher-quality engineering outcomes.

Why Join Us?

This is an opportunity to help develop a first-of-its-kind aerospace vehicle operating at the intersection of aviation and spaceflight.

You'll have genuine ownership of critical vehicle functions, work alongside highly capable engineers, and help solve technical challenges that don't exist anywhere else in the industry. Your work will directly influence how we demonstrate safety, reliability, and operational readiness as we take the vehicle from development into routine operations.

Diversity & Inclusion

At Dawn Aerospace, we believe that diverse teams build better solutions. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences are valued and supported to do their best work.

About Dawn Aerospace

Dawn Aerospace is a space transportation company with a purpose.
Our mission is to enable the next generation of space users by providing more sustainable and scalable ways to access and move around in space. We believe this access, in the form of a transportation network, will fundamentally change what’s possible from space. We currently focus on three areas of space transportation:

  • In-space propulsion
    We're a leading supplier of turnkey green propulsion systems for various classes of satellites. Our systems utilise safe, accessible propellants and we have over 170 of these propulsion units on more than 40 operational satellites already. A further 200 units are in production.
  • In-space servicing
    Coupled with our propulsion expertise, we are ensuring that our customers' satellites are refuellable. In the coming years, Dawn will offer a refueling service to enable life extension of customer satellites. This new market is aligned with our sustainability goal to ensue a clean and safe space for everyone!
  • Spaceplane
    We are developing the fastest and highest-flying aircraft ever to take off from a runway, combining the extreme performance of rocket propulsion with the reusability of conventional airplanes to enable high-frequency, low-cost access to sub-orbital space.

Our international teams are distributed across four locations: the Netherlands, France, New Zealand, and the USA.
