If you think you have what it takes but are unsure that you check every box, we still want to hear from you.

title: Reliability Engineer
description:
Company Description

About AbbVie

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at . Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.


Job Description

The Reliability Engineer is responsible for driving continuous equipment and Utilities systems reliability improvements by providing and coordinating technical support, and by managing the reliability improvement processes for the site, with the aim of reducing risk levels to the business.

The Reliability Engineer will lead the Maintenance Excellence Program (MEP), driving strategic vision and execution of Maintenance Excellence Program in BLI, collaborating with Facilities, Engineering and Maintenance Planner to enhance reliability by implementing best practices to achieve superior operational efficiency and asset management.

The Reliability Engineer will provide expertise to ensure asset reliability is maintained at the highest levels, and will drive for reliability of work processes, job plans, procedures and operating practices. The Reliability Engineer will define, design, develop, and monitor the site’s critical asset register to provide standardized processes and procedures for the proper operation and care of key production, utility and supporting assets.

Responsibilities:

  • Responsible of BLI Maintenance Excellence Program (MEP) by targeting critical equipment assets for optimization and Continuous Improvement activities, train personnel on reliability processes.
  • Guide efforts to ensure reliability and maintainability of equipment, processes, utilities, facilities, controls and safety systems.
  • Develop engineering solutions to repetitive failures, and apply knowledge in methods and processes to prevent, or reduce the likelihood or frequency of failures in site systems.
  • Analyze failure history to determine the reliability characteristics of key systems, and from this analysis, develop long term solutions to recurring issues.
  • Develop and enforce an Asset Operations Plan that will ensure optimum utilization and operating efficiency of facility’s assets, and development of an Asset Maintenance Plan to ensure adequate levels of sustaining effective maintenance for each plant asset on the asset register.
  • Responsible for adherence to Life Cycle Asset Management (LCAM) process throughout the entire life cycle of new assets.
  • Conduct root cause failure analysis (RCFA) by understanding and applying failure data analysis techniques, perform analyses of asset and production equipment performance to include asset utilization, overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) and remaining useful life as guiding parameters.
  • Generate asset management plan that includes creation of value-added preventative maintenance tasks and determine the most effective utilization of predictive and other nondestructive testing methods to identify inherent reliability problems.
  • Work with Facilities and Engineering to review maintenance and installation plans for new equipment, and provide reliability and maintainability specifications for changes, to ensure the reliability and maintainability of new and modified installations. Participate in design and installation specifications, factory and site acceptance testing, and commissioning plans to assure adherence to functional specifications.
  • Apply AbbVie MEP best practices for example predictive maintenance program and telemetry sensor technology, and influence BLI equipment/system/facilities capital planning and LRP.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Science degree in Chemical or Mechanical Engineering
  • Five (5)+ years of relevant work experience in Reliability Engineering field, preferably in the cGMP / pharmaceutical Industry.
  • Proficient in Computer-based Maintenance Management systems (CMMS, example MAXIMO or similar)
  • Previous demonstrated experience of six sigma methodology would be beneficial.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, verbal and written; proven problem-solving skills, innovative thinking, attention to detail to ensure accuracy and compliance with procedures
  • Results driven, striving to meet targets and metrics as set by site/department and division leaders.
  • Total commitment to Quality and always maintaining a high standard of work, demonstrating highest levels of integrity and a strong work ethic.

Additional Information

  • The compensation range described below is the range of possible base pay compensation that the Company believes in good faith it will pay for this role at the time of this posting based on the job grade for this position. Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors including geographic location, and we may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future. ​
  • We offer a comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off (vacation, holidays, sick), medical/dental/vision insurance and 401(k) to eligible employees.​
  • This job is eligible to participate in our short-term incentive programs. ​

Note: No amount of pay is considered to be wages or compensation until such amount is earned, vested, and determinable. The amount and availability of any bonus, commission, incentive, benefits, or any other form of compensation and benefits that are allocable to a particular employee remains in the Company's sole and absolute discretion unless and until paid and may be modified at the Company’s sole and absolute discretion, consistent with applicable law. ​

title: Head of Communications
description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

At Roche, we believe care should start before disease takes hold. As the Head of Communications for Roche BeLux, you will serve as a strategic driver of our mission, championing a OneRoche approach by shaping our external image to ensure our groundbreaking science is understood, valued, and accessible to patients. Leading both internal and external communication strategies within the External Affairs department, you will proactively manage our corporate reputation, media relations, and crisis responses across Belgium and Luxembourg. By aligning our narratives, you will empower employees to act as authentic brand ambassadors who project our core values to the world.

Key responsibilities

  • Define and execute a cohesive internal and external communication strategy that proactively safeguards Roche’s social license to operate.

  • Engage proactively with health care and lay press media, acting as Roche’s primary media spokesperson.

  • Cultivate deep insights into the healthcare ecosystem to optimize business communication strategies, prioritize key corporate initiatives, and deliver consultative persuasion across complex healthcare networks.

  • Modernize communications by leading digital channel strategy, analyzing data analytics and engagement metrics, and proactively integrating generative AI tools into daily workflows and long-term strategic positioning.

  • Navigate a changing external environment and complex matrix structure with continuous resilience, fostering a OneRoche mindset to align communication efforts across divisions, while proactively solving problems, managing issues, and influencing without authority across industry task forces.

  • Partner closely with senior management on driving interactive dialogue through inspiring employee communications and town halls, and engage directly with the global Roche communications community.


Who You Are


You are a resilient, forward-thinking, and strategically-minded communication professional who thrives when translating complex scientific and business data into compelling storytelling. You bring an entrepreneurial, growth-oriented mindset, in line with the business priorities, and alongside a passion for navigating healthcare transformations.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Communication Sciences, Journalism, Linguistics, Social Sciences, or a related field.

  • 8+ years of corporate communications, public affairs, or journalism experience within a strongly regulated industry (ideally life sciences or healthcare) with a proven track record in high-stakes crisis and reputation management.

  • Trilingual proficiency with native or near-native command of Dutch, French, and English to effectively engage stakeholders across Belgium and Luxembourg.

  • Deep knowledge of the BeLux healthcare environment and media landscape, coupled with proficiency in media monitoring and the ability to drive unified "OneRoche" narrative strategies across diverse business functions.

  • Demonstrated proficiency in integrating AI solutions into corporate communication practices and strategy design.

Together, we’ll create a healthier, brighter future for all.

Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.


Let’s build a healthier future, together.

The Medical Office Specialist performs a variety of secretarial and administrative duties for the outpatient medical office relating to the organization and management of the department. The Medical Office Specialist is responsible for all front desk functions identified in the ambulatory setting. The role of the Medical Office Specialist is to provide optimal support to the team and to ensure patients receive the very best care, satisfaction and experience during the check-in, scheduling, registration, and check-out process while at the office, and continue to support our patients post visit for any appointment needs and concerns.

Depending on specialty, may include downloading specific health data into EMR; g. Provides assistance to patients as needed (e.g, e-check in, ipad, kiosks, etc).

Resolves routine matters that do not require the intervention of the department manager and escalates all others timely and appropriately.

Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required:

  • High School diploma, general equivalency diploma (GED), or GED equivalent programs and/or equivalent experience.

title: Product Lead
description:
"Day to day life has room for improvement."



That was our basic thinking when we founded simplehuman in 2000. Our mission is to bring high-performance innovation to basic but essential tasks in our daily routine. Through new technologies, meticulous engineering and an obsession for improvement, we find new and better ways to achieve basic but important daily tasks.



The Opportunity



As Product Lead, you'll drive the formulation and development of high-performance cleaning and household products that reflect simplehuman's standards for innovation and quality. You'll work closely with contract manufacturers, raw material suppliers, and internal teams to bring products from concept to launch-ready. This role focuses on technical execution, regulatory compliance, and manufacturing readiness, ensuring each product meets our standards before it goes to market. It's an opportunity to build and shape a growing category within a fast-paced, innovation-driven environment. This is an on-site position located in our Torrance, CA office. Some domestic travel is required.



What You'll Own



  • Lead end-to-end development of consumables—from concept through formulation and testing
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with industrial design, quality, creative, and supply chain to align product performance with brand and user experience
  • Develop and refine formulations, working closely with contract manufacturers and internal stakeholders
  • Ensure products meet regulatory requirements (EPA, FDA, California Prop 65, etc.)
  • Establish product specs and oversee performance, stability, safety, and claims testing
  • Identify new technologies, ingredients, and trends to keep our portfolio forward-thinking and effective
  • Source and evaluate potential partners (labs, co-mans, raw material suppliers)
  • Engage directly with new and prospective vendors—asking the right questions to understand their technology, capabilities, and innovation potential, and evaluating fit for our portfolio



What We're Looking For



  • 5–10 years of experience in product development within CPG, preferably in household cleaning, personal care, or similar categories
  • Strong background in formulation science, surfactants, and active ingredients
  • Deep knowledge of regulatory compliance (EPA, FDA, INCI, etc.)
  • Experience working with domestic and/or international contract manufacturers
  • Strong project management skills and ability to thrive in a fast-paced, design-driven environment
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to clearly align cross-functional teams and external partners
  • BS or MS in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or related field preferred



About Us



We're a mature company with the soul of a start-up. We value ingenuity, precise communications, fast iteration and scrappiness. Our teams are tight-knit with a work hard, play hard tradition – we take pride in individual and team success and push boundaries to make the best products. And we only build products we love to use ourselves. Great benefits, competitive compensation, and generous simplehuman product discounts.

title: Power System Planning & Operations Superintendent
description:
Shape Your World

At Alcoa, you will become an essential part of our purpose: to turn raw potential into real progress. The way we see it, every Alcoan is a work-shaper, team-shaper, idea-shaper & world-shaper.

We are seeking a skilled Power System Planning & Operations Superintendent to lead the daily management, planning, and coordination of APGI and Alcoa's high-voltage power systems and utility operations. In this role, you will oversee the safe, reliable, and compliant operation of our NERC-registered Bulk Electric System (BES), Rectifier Station, plant high-voltage distribution systems, and Long Sault/Alcoa Utilities water systems. You will play a key role in maintaining asset reliability, optimizing operational performance, supporting strategic capital investments, and ensuring regulatory compliance while leading a culture of safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

This position also provides critical support to plant operations through sound technical judgment, maintenance strategy, resource management, and data-driven decision making.

About the Role:

As the Power System Planning & Operations Superintendent, you will:

  • Lead the short-term planning, maintenance, and operation of the Bulk Electric System (BES), Rectifier Station, high-voltage plant systems, and Long Sault/Alcoa Utilities, maintaining a target of 99% equipment and operational reliability.

  • Utilize established work management systems, including Rex, to plan and schedule resources on a weekly basis, achieving an 80% planned work completion rate, week over week.

  • Develop and execute long-term, resource-loaded schedules supporting both operations and maintenance (O&M) activities as well as capital projects.

  • Create detailed job plans and technical maintenance procedures aligned with the reliability objectives of the Power Systems Department using established maintenance and operational practices.

  • Plan and coordinate work utilizing proven methods, policies, and procedures to ensure resources are deployed efficiently, minimizing delays, maximizing productivity, maintaining quality standards, and remaining within budget constraints.

  • Partner with the Power System Manager to provide day-to-day leadership and oversight of contractors, project teams, and support personnel.

  • Conduct internal audits of department standards, facilitate annual critical assessments for the Massena facility, and lead all aspects of Facility Ratings Assessments in compliance with FERC, NERC, and NPCC requirements.

  • Foster open communication and strong collaboration across hourly and salaried teams while building productive relationships with key stakeholders throughout the organization.

  • Support the growth and development of junior team members through coaching, mentoring, and technical guidance.

  • Champion Alcoa's commitment to safety by supporting Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) programs and initiatives, including Behavior-Based Safety programs, audits, Safety Council activities, and Safety Advisors.

Working Conditions:

This position operates primarily within an industrial manufacturing environment and requires close collaboration across operational and leadership teams. Key aspects include:

  • Onsite work within a dynamic industrial manufacturing facility.

  • Frequent interaction with both hourly and salaried employees working a variety of shifts.

  • Regular presence in production environments may include exposure to industrial equipment, elevated noise levels, and varying temperature conditions.

  • Supporting full compliance with all safety procedures, standards, and safe-work practices.

What you can bring to the role:

  • Minimum of 10 years of experience working with rectifier stations and industrial plant power systems.

  • Demonstrated technical leadership in power system operations and maintenance.

  • Advanced ability to read, interpret, and apply technical drawings, schematics, manuals, and documentation related to complex electrical, mechanical, and civil infrastructure.

  • Strong knowledge of power system safety standards and demonstrated ability to develop and deliver associated training programs.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and MS Schedule/Exchange.

  • Proven ability to provide leadership, solve complex problems, achieve measurable results, and successfully manage change.

  • Strong analytical and organizational skills, including the ability to logically evaluate challenges, identify essential requirements, and develop practical solutions that achieve project objectives.

Required Technical Knowledge

Successful candidates will possess demonstrated knowledge and experience in:

  • Electrical safety standards, including Alcoa Electrical Safety Standards 32.60 and 32.69.

  • OSHA Electrical Regulations (1910.269).

  • Project management and outage planning/execution.

  • Operation, coordination, maintenance, and reliability requirements associated with high-voltage power delivery systems.

What’s on Offer:

  • Competitive compensation packages, including pay-for-performance variable pay as well as recognition and rewards programs.

  • Flexible spending accounts and generous employer contribution to the HSA

  • 401(k), employer match up to 6%, additional employer retirement income contribution (no vesting period), and a non-qualified deferred compensation plan

  • 15 vacation days prorated in the 1st year based on hire date.

  • Alcoa has been chosen as one of America’s Greatest Workplaces 2023 by Newsweek

#LI-TL2

Base Salary: 111,800 - 167,400 USD annually

title: Student Success Coordinator
description:
Training Tomorrow's Technicians to Become Skilled, Employable and Essential.

About Us - Big Changes, Better Benefits - Join us today!

The Aviation Institute of Maintenance (AIM), established in 1969, is a premier institution dedicated to advancing the field of aviation maintenance through exceptional education and training. With 15 campuses nationwide, AIM is a cornerstone in the aviation industry, accounting for 20% of all students attending FAA-certified Airframe & Powerplant (A&P) schools across the country. Each year, AIM proudly contributes to the graduation of nearly one in four certified aircraft technicians in America.

At AIM, you'll become part of a dynamic team of educators and leaders, all united by a shared commitment to delivering top-notch training and ensuring student success. We are passionate about equipping the next generation of aircraft technicians with the skills and knowledge needed to excel in the aviation industry. If you are eager to make a meaningful impact and help shape the future of aviation maintenance, AIM offers a rewarding environment where your contributions will truly matter.

Location: 📍 2025 Satellite Pointe Duluth, GA 30096

Schedule:

  • Monday–Thursday: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM, with one scheduled late day each week from 10:00 AM – 7:00 PM
  • Friday: 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
  • Occasional evenings and weekends may be required to support student events, campus activities, and other business needs.

Compensation: $24 - $26 per hour

Are you someone who knows how to motivate others to follow through and succeed?

Do you enjoy building strong relationships while also holding people accountable to their goals?

Are you energized by helping students stay on track, complete certifications, and reach graduation?

If so, this role could be a great fit.

About the Role

The Student Success Coordinator plays a critical role in supporting students from onboarding through graduation, with a primary focus on retention, certification completion, and academic persistence.

This is not a passive student services role. You will “walk alongside” students—building trust while also pushing, motivating, and holding them accountable to complete certifications and stay on track. Success in this role is defined by your ability to engage students consistently, remove barriers, and drive measurable outcomes.

You’ll manage a caseload of students and work cross-functionally with academics, admissions, and student support teams in a metrics-driven, performance-focused environment.

Key Responsibilities

Performance & Accountability

  • Actively manage a student caseload and meet defined performance metrics, including:

    • Retention and persistence

    • Certification readiness and attainment

    • Graduation progression

  • Contribute to a performance-driven culture focused on measurable student outcomes

Student Engagement & Advocacy

  • Serve as a consistent point of contact and advocate for assigned students

  • Build strong relationships that foster trust, accountability, and follow-through

  • Proactively identify and address barriers to persistence and certification completion

  • Support students with attendance, academic standing, and program navigation

Retention & Certification Support

  • Drive certification outcomes through early intervention, consistent follow-up, and milestone tracking

  • Partner closely with Academic leadership and instructors to monitor student progress

  • Support students with resource referrals, accommodations, and escalation pathways as needed

Data, Documentation & Compliance

  • Accurately document all student interactions, engagement activities, and outcomes in CampusNexus and other systems

  • Participate in cohort tracking, G&E chart confirmation, and required audits

  • Contribute to weekly and monthly reporting tied to student success metrics

Events, Programming & Collaboration

  • Support and/or facilitate workshops, certification readiness initiatives, alumni events, and career fairs

  • Collaborate with Academic, Admissions, Financial Aid, and Employer Engagement teams to ensure coordinated student support

  • Participate in commencement and key student milestone events

What We’re Looking For

Education

  • High School Diploma or GED required

  • Associate or Bachelor’s degree preferred

Experience

  • 1–2+ years of experience in student services, advising, admissions, recruiting, workforce development, or a related role

  • Experience in a proprietary (for-profit), post-secondary education environment strongly preferred

  • Background in admissions or sales is highly beneficial

Skills & Mindset

  • Strong ability to motivate, influence, and hold students accountable

  • Excellent communication skills with a student-centered approach

  • Strong organizational and problem-solving abilities

  • Comfortable working in a metrics-driven, performance-focused environment

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, Outlook, Teams, etc.)

  • CampusNexus experience preferred

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • You are a natural motivator—you know how to push people in a supportive, effective way

  • You balance empathy with accountability and follow-through

  • You are persistent and don’t give up on students easily

  • You thrive in structured environments with clear goals and expectations

  • You are comfortable having tough conversations when needed

title: Associate AI Software Engineer
description:
Who we are

Over 600 employees strong, Asure sees Human Capital Management (HCM) through the lens of entrepreneurs and executives with an owner’s mentality. We help businesses develop their “Human Capital” to get to the next level, stay compliant, and allocate their time, money and technology toward growth. Our HCM platform empowers more than 100,000 clients to build great teams and better manage their people while staying compliant in an ever-changing HR legislative landscape. Asure’s HCM offering includes Payroll & Tax, HR, and Time & Attendance software and HR Services ranging from online compliance tools to a fully outsourced HR department.


How you will contribute

As an Associate AI Software Engineer, you will work alongside experienced engineers and AI practitioners to design, develop, test, and maintain AI-powered software that supports Asure's products and platform services. In this role you will primarily write Python and build features that integrate large language models (LLMs) and other AI services into real applications running in our AWS cloud environment.


This role is designed for early-career engineers who are eager to grow by learning modern AI software development practices and contributing to business-critical applications. You will gain hands-on experience integrating LLMs, building the APIs and data pipelines that support AI features, and applying solid software engineering fundamentals — all with the guidance and support of a senior team, and with room to grow your skills over time.


Much of this work supports Asure's agentic AI platform, which is designed to turn AI reasoning into reliable, real-world execution across payroll and HCM workflows — with human confirmation required before any sensitive action is committed. You will help build the tools and integrations that let AI systems take safe, well-scoped actions rather than simply generating text, working with modern agent architectures such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and human-in-the-loop patterns.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and other stakeholders to build AI-powered software features that meet business and customer needs.
  • Write clean, maintainable, well-tested Python code for applications, services, and APIs that leverage AI and LLM capabilities.
  • Integrate large language models (LLMs) and AI services into software applications and business workflows, primarily within our AWS environment.
  • Assist with prompt design, experimentation, evaluation, and validation of LLM-based features under the guidance of senior engineers.
  • Contribute to the data pipelines and retrieval components (e.g., embeddings and vector search) that support AI features.
  • Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback to improve software quality, AI solution effectiveness, and your own technical skills.
  • Assist with troubleshooting, debugging, monitoring, and resolving defects in AI-enabled applications and services.
  • Work with relational, NoSQL, and vector data stores to support AI-driven solutions.
  • Support the deployment and operation of AI applications and services in cloud (AWS) environments.
  • Participate in Agile development activities, including sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives.
  • Follow software engineering and responsible AI best practices, and continuously develop your knowledge across Python, AI/LLMs, and cloud technologies with a curiosity and growth mindset.


Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, or a related technical field.
  • Understanding of software development fundamentals, including object-oriented programming, data structures, algorithms, and software design principles.
  • Proficiency in Python — the primary language for this role — demonstrated through coursework, projects, internships, or personal development. Strong fundamentals in another modern language (e.g., C#, Java, or JavaScript/TypeScript) with the ability to ramp up quickly on Python are also welcome.
  • Foundational understanding of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or generative AI concepts, gained through coursework, certifications, projects, research, internships, or personal learning.
  • Understanding of large language models (LLMs) and basic prompt engineering concepts, and how they are applied in software applications.
  • Familiarity with APIs and web services.
  • Familiarity with at least one major cloud platform (AWS preferred; Azure or Google Cloud Platform also relevant).
  • Basic understanding of data management concepts, including relational and NoSQL databases.
  • Experience using Git or other version control systems.
  • Strong problem-solving, analytical, and communication skills.
  • Ability to learn quickly and collaborate effectively in a team-oriented environment.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience — through work, internships, co-ops, academic or personal projects, hackathons, or open-source contributions — building software that uses LLMs or other AI capabilities.
  • Experience building agentic AI features — including agent orchestration, tool/function calling, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) — or with related frameworks and patterns such as LangChain, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, and embeddings.
  • Exposure to LLM platforms and services such as Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or Google Gemini.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS, particularly its AI/ML and application services (e.g., Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, Lambda, DynamoDB).
  • Exposure to the Python data and ML ecosystem (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, and libraries such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Scikit-learn).
  • Familiarity with RESTful APIs, web services, and third-party or system integrations.
  • Understanding of AI model and prompt evaluation, monitoring, governance, security, and responsible AI principles.
  • Familiarity with Agile methodologies, DevOps practices, automated testing, or CI/CD pipelines.
  • Exposure to data engineering, ETL pipelines, or analytics platforms.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or similar.


Compensation

The salary range for this position is $80,000-$90,000 based on relevant experience, skills, and industry knowledge.


Benefits

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, HSA, FSA- All effective on day 1!
  • Company paid Basic Life Insurance, A+D, Long-Term Disability, and Short-Term Disability
  • 401K Program with 3% safe harbor contribution
  • Employee Stock Purchase Program
  • Fitness Reimbursement Program
  • Self-Managed PTO


Our Mission

To provide Human Capital Management (HCM) software and services that help companies grow, while nurturing a culture of growth around us.

  • Helping customers grow by getting the most from their human capital.
  • Helping our employees grow personally and professionally.
  • Growing relationships in our communities that inspire goodness.
  • Grow shareholder value


Our Vision

Be the most trusted Human Capital Management resource to entrepreneurs everywhere.


Our Values

Reflect who we are and what we stand for as a company.

  • Embrace Change
  • Lead with Integrity
  • Own the Outcome
  • Deliver Awesome
  • Be a Good Human


We are an equal opportunity employer. All candidates must be legally authorized to work in the US, as we are unable to sponsor or transfer Visas at this time.

The Site Controller – Laboratory Operations serves as the primary finance business partner for Abbott's Toxicology laboratory operations in Gretna, Louisiana. This role provides financial leadership and strategic support across the laboratory organization, partnering closely with site leadership to drive business performance, operational excellence, and sustainable growth.

The Site Controller is responsible for financial planning and analysis, cost accounting, forecasting, operational analytics, capital investment evaluation, and business decision support. The individual in this position will deliver timely and actionable financial insights that enable data-driven decision-making while ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and financial targets.

Working collaboratively with laboratory and site leadership teams, the Site Controller supports budgeting and forecasting processes, cost accounting governance, gross margin improvement initiatives, and capital investment planning. This role plays a critical part in identifying operational and financial opportunities, evaluating business risks, and developing strategies that enhance profitability and operational effectiveness.

The Site Controller will also ensure compliance with Abbott financial policies, accounting standards, internal controls, and applicable regulatory requirements. Working at Abbott

The Opportunity

This position is a field-based position based in Orange County, CA in the Cardiac Rhythm Management division. As a global leader in Cardiac Rhythm Technologies, we focus on innovative technologies that can improve the way doctors treat people with heart arrhythmias or irregular heartbeats.

What You’ll Work On

Under general direction, the CRM Product Support Specialist provides comprehensive engineering, sales, educational, and technical support.   • Must possess strong written and verbal communication skills, along with excellent interpersonal, presentation, analytical, and organizational abilities. Additionally, must be able to meet deadlines effectively.

title: Assistant Fashion Designer
description:
ABOUT US

Edgemine is a leading women’s fashion company based in Los Angeles, designing and manufacturing contemporary apparel for major retailers and brands. With a global production network and multiple brands under our umbrella, including Blu Pepper, The Workshop, and JOA, we operate at the intersection of creativity and operational excellence.


Enjoy standout, industry-leading benefits including company-covered health insurance, a 401(k) match, daily lunches, and early Friday afternoons. Be part of a fun, team-oriented culture with events, perks, and generous time off. Grow your career with hands-on industry experience and real opportunities for advancement.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring an Assistant Fashion Designer to join our design teams. This is a hands-on, production-heavy role that supports every stage of the design and development process — from trend research and sketching to fittings and photoshoot prep. The work is deadline-driven and detail-oriented, but it's what keeps the design calendar on track and the product consistent.

If you're focused, organized, and ready to build real experience in the wholesale apparel industry, this is your opportunity.

  • Research seasonal trends, colors, and fabrics aligned with the Blu Pepper brand direction

  • Enter and update style data in ERP and maintain internal style records



KEY QUALIFICATIONS

  • A strong eye for women's fashion, silhouette, and product development
  • Proficiency in Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop (or similar tools)
  • Organized, reliable, and detail-oriented, especially in process-based, repetitive tasks
  • A dependable team player with clear, professional communication
  • Familiarity with ERP systems like NetSuite is a plus
  • Prior internship or experience in wholesale or production environments preferred



BENEFITS & PERKS

  • Wellness: PPO health insurance (medical, dental, vision).
  • Financial Well-Being: 401(k) plan with 100% company match up to 4%.
  • Convenience: Daily lunch meals provided.
  • Time Off: Paid vacation, holidays, and sick days.
  • Culture: holiday parties, sample sales, and team-building events.
  • Alternative Schedule Available: 8:30AM-6PM Monday through Thursday, with half-days on Friday!
  • Travel: Paid expenses, food allowance, and the opportunity to explore new cities during free time.

Why Join Us? At Edgemine, we believe in investing in our employees. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We're looking for individuals who are authentic, accountable, and eager to learn and grow with us.

title: Research Laboratory Coordinator
description:
PRIMARY DETAIL

  • $102,136 - $112,741 (HEW Level 6), plus 17% superannuation and annual leave loading

  • 12 months fixed-term contract

  • Macquarie University, Wallumattagal Campus, North Ryde

Help power life-changing cancer research, coordinate the lab operations that keep our discoveries moving.

Cancer research is a key strategic priority for Macquarie University and our Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences, underpinned by a 2025 plan to grow an integrated cancer care and research program. Here, you'll play a pivotal operational role at the centre of a dynamic cancer research team led by Principal Investigator Professor Helen Rizos, working alongside postdoctoral fellows, research assistants and higher degree research students.

For us, dedicated operational support is essential to ensure continuity of research activity and the smooth day-to-day functioning of the laboratory and team. In this role you'll coordinate the technical, operational and administrative activities of the research laboratory, providing the reliable support that allows scientists to focus on what matters most which is delivering impactful cancer research.

If you enjoy variety, thrive on keeping things running smoothly, and want your work to contribute to meaningful health outcomes, this position offers a genuine chance to make a difference within a collegiate and purpose-driven environment.

About the Role

Reporting to our Deputy Dean, Research and Innovation, you will support the effective operation of the cancer research group by coordinating laboratory operations, research governance, financial administration and team communication. Working closely with research leadership, you will help implement priorities, streamline processes and ensure the smooth delivery of research activities. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Coordinating the technical and operational administration of the research laboratory, including hands-on operational and research support for the Principal Investigator and cancer research team.

  • Providing teaching support (such as demonstrations in tutorials and practicals) for junior staff and students as required.

  • Maintaining project documentation and version control, including protocols, SOPs and amendments.

  • Preparing research materials with team members, including ethics submissions, reporting, and assisting the PI with essential research documents, manuscripts, progress reports and acquittals.

  • Contributing to scientific outputs including research data preparation and collection, lab meetings, conference proceedings, grant applications and student projects.

  • Providing financial, purchasing, procurement and inventory support, and preparing financial reporting on expenditure against budget and project accounts.

  • Organising meetings and seminars, coordinating onboarding of new staff and students, and keeping the group informed on upcoming grants, conferences and opportunities.


About Us

The Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences has active research programs across biomedical, translational and health services domains, with areas of strength including neurosciences, cancer medicine and vascular science. The faculty hosts the Australian Institute of Health Innovation, an internationally acclaimed centre researching health systems, e-health and patient safety, and offers a distinctive suite of capability-based medical education programs and a unique three-year professional-entry Doctor of Physiotherapy degree. Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences | Macquarie University | Sydney

About You

You are a well-organised coordinator who enjoys balancing operational, administrative and scientific tasks, and who takes pride in enabling a research team to thrive. You bring sound problem-solving ability, sound communication skills, and a practical understanding of research laboratory environments.

Selection Criteria

  • Tertiary qualifications in an appropriate discipline and/or relevant experience in a related field.

  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills, with the capacity to work both autonomously and as part of a team while taking initiative on day-to-day operational matters.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the capacity to prioritise workload during busy periods.

  • Experience carrying out scientific experiments, conducting literature searches, and preparing literature reviews for further analysis.

  • Experience developing and working on research projects, including research protocols, experimental design, ethics submissions and grant applications.

  • Numeracy skills with experience managing income/expenditure for reconciliation and budget tracking, invoice payments and purchases.

  • A working understanding of WHS and safe laboratory practices applicable to the work environment.

How to Apply

To be considered, please apply online with your CV and a cover letter outlining how your experience aligns with the selection criteria (above).

Applications Close

Applications for this role will close on 19th August at 11 PM AEST.

Why Join Us?

Macquarie is a university engaged with the real and often complex problems and opportunities that define our lives. Since our foundation over 60 years ago, we have aspired to be a different type of university. Over the years, we have grown to become the centre of a vibrant local and global community. Connect with us today.

  • Onsite childcare facilities to support working parents

Your employment is conditional upon the completion and maintenance of all role-required pre-employment or background checks in terms satisfactory to the University.

Systems Analysts (Robotic Algorithms and Control) at Intuitive Surgical perform a central role in the design, development, and support of new products in the daVinci Surgery product line. Systems Analysts are primarily responsible for the tele-robotic motion control algorithms, robotic manipulator control and safety algorithms for new surgical robots and surgical instruments. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering where all the subsystems are integrated together. Systems Analysts strive to provide early design input, quickly prove out new designs, and seek out solutions to subtle and challenging problems in system integration and motion control. Responsibilities continue until the products are shipping to customers with the highest quality and reliability.

Essential Job Duties

  • Contribute to design of new surgical platforms and instruments through control system analysis and characterization of prototypes.

  • Implement motion control algorithms.

  • Apply control theory to the design and verification of mechatronic and tele-robotic systems.

  • Analyze complex electro-mechanical devices for dynamic safety and clinical risk.

  • Create safety monitoring algorithms based on sound physics.

  • Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.

  • Document and pursue intellectual property.

  • Communicate system performance to the organization as a whole.

  • Improve group work-flow through tool building and teaching others.

  • Support and track system performance as it moves from design to manufacturing.

title: Talent
description:
About Us

At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets.

We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.

We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel.

Read more about what we’re building here.

About the Role

We’re looking for someone to help build a robust Talent function at Axle.

In this role, you’ll own hiring end-to-end across both technical and commercial roles, ensuring we attract top talent while delivering an exceptional candidate experience. We’re aiming to make ~10 hires per quarter, so both quality and speed are equally important.

Axle’s success is built on the strength of our team, and you’ll play a critical role in shaping that as we scale.

What you will be doing

  • Own end-to-end hiring across technical and commercial roles and deliver exceptional candidate experience from first conversation through to offer.

  • Build proactive sourcing strategies and talent pipelines.

  • Coach interviewers on structured interviewing and best practice.

  • Continuously improve hiring processes, reporting and efficiency.

  • Strengthen Axle's employer brand through content and candidate engagement.

Benefits

A meaningful slice of equity in Axle, alongside a competitive salary, with total compensation ranging from £75k–£200k (base salary + equity).

We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation.

Enhanced parental leave to support you through life's meaningful moments.

Bi-annual retreats to strengthen team connection & shared purpose.

Hybrid working - We have a dog-friendly office around Farringdon. To maximize collaboration, we ask that you spend 2-3 days a week in the office.

The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.

We are extremely keen to build a diverse company, and we’re particularly eager to hear from candidates who don't fit the traditional role stereotypes. If you’re motivated by our mission, please do reach out, even if you feel you might not ‘check all the boxes’.

Interview process

  1. Initial interview

  2. Take-home exercise

  3. Final interview (in-person)

  4. Offer, references, and welcome to the team!

Compensation: £75K – £200K

  • • Total Compensation (salary + equity) £75K – £200K

Our 115,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

Working at Abbott

At Abbott, you can do work that matters, grow, and learn, care for yourself and your family, be your true self, and live a full life. You’ll also have access to:

In Abbott’s Electrophysiology (EP) business, we’re advancing the treatment of heart disease through breakthrough medical technologies in atrial fibrillation, allowing people to restore their health and get on with their lives.

Our location in St Paul, MN is looking for a Postmarket Surveillance Analyst.

title: People & workplace specialist
description:
🚀 About WRITER

WRITER is where the world's leading enterprises orchestrate AI-powered work. Our vision is to expand human capacity through superintelligence. And we're proving it's possible – through powerful, trustworthy AI that unites IT and business teams together to unlock enterprise-wide transformation. With WRITER's end-to-end platform, hundreds of companies like Mars, Marriott, Uber, and Vanguard are building and deploying AI agents that are grounded in their company's data and fueled by WRITER's enterprise-grade LLMs. Valued at $1.9B and backed by industry-leading investors including Premji Invest, Radical Ventures, and ICONIQ Growth, WRITER is rapidly cementing its position as the leader in enterprise generative AI.

Founded in 2020 with office hubs in San Francisco, New York City, Austin, Chicago, and London, our team thinks big and moves fast, and we're looking for smart, hardworking builders and scalers to join us on our journey to create a better future of work with AI.

📐 About the role

We are hiring for a people & workplace specialist in our London office, one of our three major global hubs. This role will be critical in supporting our EMEA team through continued growth. From the physical environment to internal and external events to daily HR tasks, you'll have a wide canvas to support and delight our London WRITER colleagues. This is a hands-on role where you'll own both the people operations and workplace experience for our London team, ensuring every employee feels supported, connected, and set up to do their best work.

You'll be the on-the-ground presence for the People team in London, managing everything from ticket queues and employee inquiries to onboarding, offboarding, and benefits administration across EMEA. At the same time, you'll own the daily workplace experience — keeping the office well-equipped, organized, and welcoming, planning events and team gatherings, and continuously improving how the space works for the people in it. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who loves building great employee experiences and wants to have a direct, visible impact on a growing team.

This role is office-based in our London office at the Parcels building, with 5 days in the office every week. This role reports to the head of people operations.

🦸🏻‍♀️ What you'll do

  • Own the People Ops ticket queue for the London office, triaging and responding to employee inquiries related to policies, benefits, onboarding, documentation, employment verifications, and general People Operations support, escalating or redirecting to other People Team members as appropriate

  • Act as the on-site liaison for all People Operations functions across EMEA, including onboarding, offboarding, benefits and compensation administration, and time off, while partnering with Talent to schedule interview loops and greet candidates in office

  • Create a welcoming and productive daily experience for our London WRITER employees and their guests, managing office inventory to ensure the space is well-equipped with snacks, beverages, and supplies

  • Organize and support internal and external company events and meetings, including the new hire onboarding program and global All Hands, ensuring every gathering runs smoothly and reflects WRITER's culture

  • Own space and capacity planning for the London office, continually enhancing the office layout and seating plan as the team grows, and managing mail, shipping, receiving, and other office logistics

  • Maintain the London office budget and manage relationships with property management and vendors for various services, repairs, and support, ensuring financial stewardship and high ROI for our spend

  • Create and iterate on office policies and processes that drive efficiency and better employee experiences across the London hub

⭐️ What you need

  • Experience in a Human Resources or People Operations role, preferably at a high-growth tech company where you've supported a scaling team through rapid change

  • A proactive problem solver who anticipates and resolves issues before they escalate, with a hospitality mindset that is friendly, approachable, and genuinely invested in creating delightful employee experiences

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills that demonstrate a high level of professionalism, with strong proactive communication habits both in sync and async settings

  • Exceptional prioritization and time management skills, with the ability to juggle many tasks and competing priorities without dropping the ball

  • Hands-on experience managing office operations, vendor relationships, and budgets, with a track record of making physical workspaces better for the people in them

  • A builder's mindset with genuine excitement about creating scalable processes and continuously improving how a People function operates day to day

  • A passion for workplace culture and employee experience, with the ability to bring WRITER's values to life in everything you do — Connect, Challenge, Own

🍩 Benefits & perks (UK full-time employees):

  • Generous PTO, plus company holidays

  • Comprehensive medical and dental insurance

  • Paid parental leave for all parents (16 weeks)

  • Fertility and family planning support

  • Early-detection cancer testing through Galleri

  • Competitive pension scheme and company contribution

  • Annual work-life stipends for:

    • Wellness stipend for gym, massage/chiropractor, personal training, etc.

    • Learning and development stipend

  • Company-wide off-sites and team off-sites

  • Competitive compensation and company stock options

title: Associate Director, Commercial Data Product Management
description:
We are the people who give possibilities purpose

BD is one of the largest global medical technology companies in the world. Advancing the world of health™ is our Purpose, and it’s no small feat. It takes the imagination and passion of all of us—from design and engineering to the manufacturing and marketing of our billions of MedTech products per year—to look at the impossible and find transformative solutions that turn dreams into possibilities.





Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Product Portfolio Strategy & Prioritization

  • Own the commercial data product portfolio and shape the strategic roadmap for assigned domains; make prioritization recommendations to ensure investments align with enterprise commercial priorities and strategic objectives.

  • Lead prioritization decisions across competing business needs, balancing Business Unit and Regional requirements with enterprise standardization goals.

  • Develop business cases, investment recommendations, value hypotheses, and success metrics for new products, enhancements, and strategic initiatives (including AI-enabled decision-making).

  • Recommend roadmap sequencing, deployment strategies, and resource allocation decisions to maximize business impact and organizational capacity.

  • Drive leadership alignment and secure cross-functional endorsement for product strategies, priorities, and investment decisions.

  • Represent assigned product portfolios within governance processes and executive review forums, effectively communicating recommendations, tradeoffs, risks, and opportunities.

  • Establish accountability frameworks that measure success through business outcomes, adoption, and value realization.

Product Model Cells & Value Validation

  • Design, lead, and evaluate Model Cell initiatives (e.g., MVPs, pilots, and proof-of-concept testing) that validate new commercial data and AI-enabled capabilities.

  • Define objectives, business hypotheses, success criteria, testing methodologies, and adoption metrics for pilot programs and scaled deployments.

  • Partner with business stakeholders, analytics teams, decision scientists, and technical teams to rigorously test solutions and measure business outcomes.

  • Track pilot performance, adoption trends, user engagement, and realized value to determine scalability and future investment priorities.

  • Continuously refine business cases and roadmap priorities based on measurable results, stakeholder feedback, and evolving commercial needs.

  • Lead successful capabilities through transition from pilot to enterprise-scale deployment, ensuring readiness for global adoption.

Product Management & Delivery Leadership

  • Lead the end-to-end lifecycle of assigned commercial data products from opportunity identification and discovery through deployment, adoption, optimization, and retirement.

  • Translate commercial strategies, business priorities, and workflow requirements into actionable product roadmaps and clearly defined product requirements.

  • Own product roadmap commitments and partner with Engineering, Analytics, and Technology teams to ensure successful delivery against strategic objectives.

  • Establish clear product success criteria and performance indicators to ensure products deliver measurable business value.

  • Ensure commercial data products are designed for scalability, sustainability, and adoption across global Business Units and Regions.

  • Maintain active feedback loops with stakeholders and end users to continuously improve product effectiveness and business impact.

  • Hold stakeholders and delivery partners accountable for executing agreed-upon plans, timelines, and outcomes.

Global Standards, Metrics & Semantic Consistency

  • Own metric definitions and business logic for assigned domains, ensuring consistent meaning across dashboards, reports, and models — so that “one metric” means the same thing in every region and business unit.

  • Partner with Analytics Engineering to ensure semantic definitions are accurately reflected in governed data layers and standardized consumption patterns.

  • Support the establishment and ongoing maintenance of the commercial business taxonomy (domains, entities, hierarchies) to drive alignment across functions and geographies.

  • Flag and resolve definition conflicts across BUs and Regions, escalating where enterprise-level decisions are required.

  • Contribute to governance processes that allow global standards to coexist with local flexibility — core metric standards plus permitted regional extensions.

Executive Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence

  • Influence senior leaders across Sales, Marketing, Commercial Operations, Finance, Analytics, and Technology organizations to align on priorities, investments, and strategic outcomes.

  • Develop executive-ready communications, business cases, roadmap reviews, and recommendations for leadership and governance forums.

  • Build consensus across diverse stakeholder groups while effectively managing competing priorities and organizational complexity.

  • Escalate strategic risks, investment decisions, and critical dependencies requiring executive intervention.

  • Contribute to the long-term vision and operating model for Commercial Data Products, helping shape future capabilities and organizational priorities.

Qualifications

  • 8–12 years of experience in product management, commercial analytics, commercial operations, strategy, data products, or related disciplines.

  • Demonstrated ownership of enterprise-scale product portfolios, strategic initiatives, or business capabilities with accountability for measurable outcomes.

  • Proven experience building business cases, influencing executive stakeholders, and driving strategic cross-functional decision-making.

  • Experience delivering data, analytics, digital, or AI-enabled products through the product lifecycle.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex global initiatives across teams.

  • Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and organizational influence skills.

  • Comfort working with data platforms, dashboards, and CRM systems (Salesforce experience a plus); ability to speak credibly with both business and technical audiences.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree required (Business, Economics, Engineering, Data/Analytics, or related). MBA/MS preferred.

Leadership Attributes

  • Business-first mindset: starts with the commercial problem and the behavior change needed, not the technical solution.

  • Global builder: designs products and standards that scale across BUs, regions, and markets — not just for one team or one market.

  • Outcome-oriented: measures success by adoption, impact, and revenue outcomes — not delivery milestones alone.

  • Strong collaborator: builds trust with both business stakeholders and technical teams.

  • Clear communicator: writes and speaks with precision; comfortable presenting to senior stakeholders and driving crisp alignment.

  • Resilient self-starter: thrives in fast-moving, cross-functional environments; builds structure and momentum without waiting for perfect conditions.

  • High integrity and a bias for action.

Minimum Requirement:

  • Degree level qualification; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

title: Production Planner
description:
Help grow a safer, cleaner, healthier future for everyone, every day.

Company description:

TeDan Surgical Innovations (TSI) designs and manufactures specialty surgical products for use in orthopedic, neuro, thoracic and spine surgeries. TSI was founded in 2006 with the goal to innovate and address evolving retraction techniques in spine surgery. We have successfully addressed the need for minimally invasive, posterior, lateral and anterior surgical approaches to the spine, and have introduced access instrumentation for neurological, orthopedic and cardiothoracic procedures. We commit to providing innovative, high-quality surgical access systems designed to optimize exposure and improve the surgeon experience.

Job Summary:

The Production Planner is responsible for translating demand into executable production plans that optimize capacity, inventory, and service levels across machining and assembly operations. This role serves as the central coordination point between Sales, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Production, ensuring alignment between demand, supply, and execution.

The Production Planner owns the integrity and execution of the production schedule, drives adherence to planning processes, and enables flow through data-driven decision making. This role is critical to implementing a structured Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (SIOP) process, improving schedule stability, and supporting Lean manufacturing principles in a high-mix, low-volume regulated environment.

Duties/Essential Job Functions:

  • Own the production schedule by translating demand, inventory, and capacity data into clear, executable plans for machining and assembly.
  • Analyze constraints, bottlenecks, and disruptions, then make timely adjustments to protect delivery, flow, and service levels.
  • Drive disciplined execution of daily, weekly, and monthly planning processes, including work order release, schedule adherence, and SIOP support.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Production, Supply Chain, Sales, Engineering, and NPI to align priorities, materials, and system data with operational needs.
  • Maintain high integrity of planning data, including BOMs, routings, cycle times, lead times, and ERP/MES signals, and resolve issues quickly.
  • Use strong analytical judgment to support capacity planning, inventory decisions, and scenario analysis such as overtime, outsourcing, and make-versus-buy tradeoffs.
  • Track key planning KPIs and lead continuous improvement efforts that increase schedule stability, reduce waste, and improve material flow.
  • Execute with a high level of ownership and accountability, clearly communicating risks, trade-offs, and required actions to leadership.

Required Education/Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 3–7 years of experience in production planning, scheduling, or supply chain roles within a manufacturing environment.
  • Demonstrated success in high-mix, low-volume operations, building executable schedules and managing shifting priorities with urgency and accuracy.
  • Strong command of ERP/MRP systems and planning data, with the ability to maintain high data integrity and translate information into decisions.
  • Advanced analytical capability, including strong Excel skills and comfort with data analysis or visualization tools such as Power BI.
  • Track record of disciplined execution, clear communication, and personal accountability in a fast-paced manufacturing setting.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with Syteline, Infor, Misys preferred.
  • APICS certification (CPIM, CSCP) preferred.
  • Experience supporting or leading SIOP processes.
  • Familiarity with MES systems and production data environments.

Physical Requirements:

Ability to stand for extended periods, lift up to 25 lbs occasionally, and work in a manufacturing environment.

Reasonable Accommodations

title: Head of Functional Genomics
description:
The opportunity

Substrate is building a network of fully autonomous wet labs, cloud-based data production facilities for AI biology, integrated with foundation models to become the critical infrastructure layer for AI-driven biological discovery. Our first node opens in King’s Cross, London, with several integrated workcells and two scientific verticals online by mid-2027. Our customers range from foundation model labs to global pharma.

We are hiring a Head of Functional Genomics to build and lead the functional genomics vertical from scratch. The vertical covers the full pipeline: cell line engineering, perturbation library design, screen execution, and bulk and single-cell sequencing readouts, with the resulting data feeding customer pipelines that include foundation model training for virtual cell models. This is the second scientific vertical we are bringing online: manual development is starting now, and full autonomous execution on workcells is targeted for mid-to-late 2027. You will own the screening menu, scope it against early customer demand, shape the workcells the screens will eventually run on, and build the team that operates the function at scale. You will be the senior functional genomics scientist in the company at hire.

About Substrate

Substrate is spinning out of Automata, the UK lab automation company that has built the workcell platform our labs run on. Our four co-founders are Mostafa ElSayed (CEO and founder of Automata), Oli Hoy (formerly VP Customer Experience at Automata), Alexey Morgunov (AI Scientist co-founder, leading the intelligence software product), and a Founding Biology Lead joining shortly. We are aiming to have ramped up to 32 people by the end of Q1 2027.

We are funded in parallel by a combination of venture funding and government grants. We are not a cloud lab and we are not a CRO. We are an autonomous lab platform with closed-loop integration available as one operating mode for foundation model partners.

The role

You will own functional genomics end-to-end. Day one priorities are the scientific pieces of standing up a vertical from scratch: scoping the priority screening menu against early customer demand, developing and validating those screens manually, setting quality thresholds, and hiring the Principal Scientists, Scientists, and Lab Technicians who will operate the function at scale. The vertical will eventually span cell line engineering across catalogue lines and iPSC-derived models, perturbation library design and production, pooled screen execution, and bulk and single-cell sequencing readouts; the day-1 wedge is one end-to-end workflow through these stages, scoped narrowly to a focused starting subset within each, and you decide what that scope looks like.

Two parts of the role are not standard, and they are why this role is so crucial to Substrate’s success. The first is that the functional genomics vertical is being built AI-first from day one. Every screen is designed from scratch for full AI-in-the-loop automation, not retrofitted onto a manual workflow. You do the work by hand first, exactly as you would in a high-end pharma research lab, and then work with Automata’s automation scientists to shape the workcells the screens will eventually run on. You will define the quality thresholds for each transition stage, decide which manual judgement calls have to be re-engineered out, and own the validation that proves equivalence at each step.

The second is closed-loop work with foundation model partners. Substrate’s distinctive operating mode is producing structured, machine-readable experimental data fast enough to feed directly into foundation model training. That changes how functional genomics screens get designed: cell line provenance, library composition, perturbation metadata, sequencing QC, and consistency across runs become first-class scientific constraints. You will work directly with model partners on screen co-design, and with our software and intelligence teams on how the resulting data flows back into customer pipelines and into Substrate’s own data factory.

You will also be the executive partner to the co-founders on anything functional-genomics related: the screening roadmap, the proprietary functional genomics dataset programme on the reserved fraction of lab capacity, and the customer conversations where functional genomics depth is decisive.

What you will do in your first twelve months

PHASE 0: NOW TO AUG 2026

  • Land in the lab. Set up workspace at our King’s Cross site and start manual screen development.

  • Scope the day-1 wedge against early customer demand: which cell line, which perturbation library, which sequencing readout, validated as one end-to-end workflow before the menu starts to expand.

  • Hire the first Principal Scientist and Lab Technician alongside you. Define the roles, run the processes, close the offers.

PHASE 1: SEP TO DEC 2026

  • Develop and validate the first screens manually. Set the reproducibility and quality thresholds that will serve as acceptance criteria for the moves to instrumented and to fully autonomous execution.

  • Co-design protocols with the software and automation engineering teams so that the manual versions you validate are automation-ready by design. Decide which manual judgement calls have to be engineered out before they hit a workcell.

  • Begin co-design conversations with the first commercial customers, including the foundation model partners coming online from mid-2027.

PHASE 2: JAN TO MAR 2027

  • Workcells arrive in the lab. Move the validated screens onto them, running with instrumentation and human intervention in the loop ahead of full autonomous operation later in 2027. Validate equivalence against the manual baselines.

  • Grow the team. Bring on the second Principal Scientist and the first scientists at the bench to support throughput as the screening menu opens to customers.

  • Ship the first revenue on the functional genomics vertical from manual and semi-automated services.

Who you are

You are an experienced functional genomics scientist who has built or led a screening function at a biotech, pharma R&D, or CRO. You are comfortable in the detail at the bench and you are comfortable setting direction for a team. The shape of the problem is what attracts you: a screening portfolio that has to be designed for autonomous execution from day one, in a business where the data the lab produces is itself part of the product.

You have hired and managed scientists, principal scientists, and technicians. You have set quality thresholds and held people to them. You have run screens that supported real customers, internal teams in pharma or biotech or external customers in a CRO setting, and you understand what enterprise-grade scientific operations look like.

You are pragmatic about being hands-on at the bench in the first six to nine months, and excited about the team you will build behind you. You enjoy interviewing, hiring, mentoring, and setting standards. You will be in the lab at our King’s Cross site at the cadence the science demands. That cadence will be heavy in the manual development phase and ease as the function grows and protocols move onto instrumentation. You are comfortable with that.

MUST HAVE

  • Seven or more years of experience in functional genomics or related disciplines (target validation, perturbation screening), with at least three in a senior or team-leading role at a biotech, pharma R&D, or CRO.

  • End-to-end hands-on experience in at least one screening modality (typically CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi knockdown), covering cell line preparation, library design, screen execution, and sequencing readout, with working familiarity across single-cell readouts and validation workflows.

  • Track record of leading a small scientific team end to end: hiring, setting quality standards, and managing performance against scientific outputs.

  • Customer-facing experience, either as a CRO scientific lead working with external customers, or as a pharma or biotech scientist embedded with internal customer teams.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Hands-on experience in cell line engineering, particularly iPSC differentiation or CRISPR-edited stable cell line generation.

  • Direct experience moving screens from manual workflows onto lab automation platforms.

  • Familiarity with structured experimental data capture, LIMS, ELN, or analogous data infrastructure.

  • Experience working with computational or AI/ML colleagues on closed-loop perturbation programmes.

  • Background at an AI-native biotech or foundation model company.

Why this is unusual

Most senior functional genomics roles in industry sit either inside a pharma R&D group (slow iteration, internal customers only), inside a CRO (external customers, faster iteration, but optimised for service throughput rather than scientific decisions about screen design), or inside an AI-native biotech (fast iteration, but a single internal customer in the company’s own pipeline). This is none of the three. You will be designing a screening menu that has to be automation-ready from the first manual experiment, working with foundation model labs on closed-loop programmes that do not have a precedent in any of those settings, and owning the proprietary dataset programme that turns the lab itself into a commercial asset.

It is also a functional genomics role with significant software and AI surface area. Your design decisions affect what the orchestrator has to do, what data flows back to model partners, and which manual judgements get re-engineered out of the workflow. Some scientists find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are.

Compensation and equity

We pay competitively against the London market for senior functional genomics scientists at venture-backed companies, calibrated to seniority and to the specific scope of this role. We will discuss numbers with serious candidates after first conversations.

Equity is meaningful, with vesting on the standard four-year schedule and a one-year cliff. We can talk through the philosophy and the maths in detail when we meet.

How we work

Working pattern is hybrid with a strong in-person bias dictated by the lab. In the manual development phase you will be at our King’s Cross site most days; this eases as the function grows, principal scientists are in seat, and protocols move onto instrumentation. Most of the founding team are in the office most days regardless. 30 days annual leave. A learning budget you can use for conferences, courses, books, and time. The founding team operates on a weekly cadence with a Monday planning meeting and a Friday close, and a quarterly offsite. We are direct with each other, we write things down, and we expect to be challenged.

The team you will join

You will initially report to Alexey Morgunov, our science and AI focused co-founder. We are recruiting a Founding Biology Lead, the co-founder who will own scientific operations across the verticals; once they join, your reporting line will likely move to them. You will work most closely with the Head of Protein Science, who is being hired alongside you, and with the software and automation engineering teams on the boundary between scientific protocols and autonomous execution.

You are the first protein-science hire. Substrate is currently three co-founders growing to roughly 32 people by the end of Q1 2027.

How to apply

Apply via Ashby with whatever you think shows your work best: a CV, a published paper or technical report you are proud of, an example of an assay you have taken from idea to validated workflow. We read everything that comes in.

Our process is three stages. An initial conversation with Alexey to understand what you want from the role and what we want from it. Followed by a technical session covering your. scientific track record, the assay menu you would build, and how you would build and lead the protein science team. Finally, an in-person founder-team session at our King’s Cross site covering scope, terms, and any final questions. We aim to move fast on candidates we are excited about; expect roughly two to three weeks end to end.

If you are not sure whether you are a fit, send a note anyway to ----- The most useful conversations we have had so far have been with people who were not sure.

Substrate is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background.
