title: Field Development Test Associate
description:
At Serve Robotics, we’re reimagining how things move in cities. Our personable sidewalk robot is our vision for the future. It’s designed to take deliveries away from congested streets, make deliveries available to more people, and benefit local businesses.

The Serve fleet has been delighting merchants, customers, and pedestrians along the way in Los Angeles, Miami, Dallas, Atlanta and Chicago while doing commercial deliveries. We’re looking for talented individuals who will grow robotic deliveries from surprising novelty to efficient ubiquity.

Who We Are

We are tech industry veterans in software, hardware, and design who are pooling our skills to build the future we want to live in. We are solving real-world problems leveraging robotics, machine learning and computer vision, among other disciplines, with a mindful eye towards the end-to-end user experience. Our team is agile, diverse, and driven. We believe that the best way to solve complicated dynamic problems is collaboratively and respectfully.

The Robotics Field Development Test Associate supports the testing, deployment, and operation of Serve's autonomous delivery robots in real-world environments. This role executes field testing, commercial deliveries, and operational activities that help validate robot performance, identify product improvements, and ensure safe, reliable operation across development and production fleets.

The Robotics Field Development Test Associate partners with Engineering, Product, and Operations teams by collecting test data, documenting issues, executing field procedures, and providing feedback that improves product quality and operational readiness.

Key Responsibilities

  • Execute field testing activities for autonomous delivery robots by following established test plans, procedures, and operational guidelines.

  • Deploy, monitor, recover, and operate robots in real-world environments while ensuring safe and reliable operation.

  • Perform commercial deliveries and represent Serve professionally when interacting with merchants, customers, and members of the public.

  • Identify, document, and reproduce software, hardware, and operational issues, providing clear information to support engineering investigations.

  • Collect test data, observations, and operational feedback to support product development and continuous improvement efforts.

  • Troubleshoot basic software and hardware issues in the field and escalate complex problems to engineering teams as appropriate.

  • Prepare robots for testing and deployment by performing routine inspections, charging, cleaning, and basic maintenance activities.

  • Follow established safety procedures, operational protocols, and testing standards during all field activities.

  • Maintain accurate testing records, issue documentation, and operational logs.

  • Collaborate with Engineering, Product, and Operations teams to support testing, deployments, demonstrations, and pilot programs.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related technical field preferred.

  • Interest in robotics, autonomous systems, field operations, logistics, quality assurance, or related technical disciplines.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately follow test procedures and document results.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work independently while following established processes and safety procedures.

  • Comfortable working outdoors and walking or biking several miles during a shift.

  • Ability to lift and move equipment consistent with the physical demands of the role.

  • Valid U.S. driver's license with a satisfactory driving record.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.

What Makes You Stand Out

  • Experience supporting field testing, robotics, autonomous vehicles, logistics, or technical operations.

  • Familiarity with issue tracking tools such as Jira.

  • Basic experience with scripting or programming languages such as Python or C++.

  • Experience using data visualization or monitoring tools such as Grafana or Looker.

  • Experience troubleshooting software or hardware systems.

  • Passion for robotics, automation, and emerging technologies.

Additional Information

  • This is a full-time, onsite position based in West Hollywood, California. The role requires regular work outdoors in varying weather conditions and involves standing, walking, biking, bending, and lifting throughout the workday. Occasional evening, weekend, or holiday work may be required to support testing, deployments, or operational needs.

title: Enterprise Knowledge Management Technical Lead
description:
Overview

DecisionPoint Corporation seeks a highly experienced Enterprise Knowledge Management Technical Lead to provide technical leadership for the implementation, integration, modernization, and continuous improvement of enterprise Knowledge Management (KM) capabilities supporting the United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM).

The Enterprise Knowledge Management Technical Lead serves as the contractor's senior technical lead responsible for designing, implementing, integrating, and sustaining enterprise Knowledge Management capabilities across Headquarters USSOCOM, Components, Theater Special Operations Commands (TSOCs), and mission partners. This position leads the technical implementation of enterprise collaboration technologies, information architecture, taxonomy, metadata, workflow automation, and knowledge-sharing capabilities that improve operational synchronization, decision superiority, and organizational effectiveness.

Working closely with Government Knowledge Management Officers (KMOs), the Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO), Special Operations Forces Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics (SOF AT&L), CIO/J6 organizations, cybersecurity personnel, records managers, and enterprise stakeholders, the Enterprise Knowledge Management Technical Lead ensures Knowledge Management capabilities integrate with existing enterprise services, governance frameworks, acquisition priorities, and approved collaboration environments while avoiding duplicate capabilities.

This role requires demonstrated experience implementing enterprise Knowledge Management solutions utilizing Microsoft 365, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Teams, Power Platform technologies, enterprise collaboration platforms, and modern information management practices supporting Combatant Command or Special Operations environments.

This position is located at MacDill Air Force Base, Tampa, Florida.

This position is contingent upon contract award.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive Government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical implementation, integration, and continuous improvement of enterprise Knowledge Management capabilities supporting USSOCOM.
  • Design, configure, implement, and optimize enterprise Knowledge Management solutions utilizing Microsoft 365, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Teams, Power Platform, and approved enterprise collaboration technologies.
  • Develop enterprise information architecture, metadata, taxonomy, content organization, and knowledge structures that improve information discoverability and operational effectiveness.
  • Lead implementation of workflow automation, digital modernization, and business process improvement initiatives supporting enterprise Knowledge Management operations.
  • Integrate Knowledge Management capabilities with existing enterprise collaboration platforms, records management systems, cybersecurity services, and other approved enterprise technologies.
  • Collaborate with Government Knowledge Management Officers (KMOs), CDAO, CIO/J6 organizations, cybersecurity personnel, records managers, and enterprise stakeholders to ensure successful implementation of Knowledge Management capabilities.
  • Develop and maintain technical standards, configuration documentation, governance artifacts, implementation guides, and standard operating procedures supporting enterprise collaboration technologies.
  • Support phased deployment and enterprise rollout of Knowledge Management capabilities across Headquarters USSOCOM, Components, Theater Special Operations Commands (TSOCs), and mission partners while accommodating mission-specific operational requirements.
  • Establish and enable Communities of Practice and enterprise collaboration capabilities that improve knowledge sharing, organizational learning, and operational synchronization.
  • Provide technical leadership supporting enterprise adoption of collaboration technologies through demonstrations, technical guidance, user enablement, and implementation support.
  • Assess existing Knowledge Management environments and recommend modernization, automation, and continuous improvement opportunities.
  • Support Agile software delivery, DevSecOps initiatives, and continuous modernization efforts supporting enterprise Knowledge Management capabilities.
  • Ensure compliance with cybersecurity requirements, records management policies, enterprise governance standards, and applicable Federal and DoD regulations.
  • Support implementation of enterprise Knowledge Management capabilities across classified and unclassified operational environments.

Qualifications

Clearance Requirement

Candidate must possess an active Top Secret (TS) clearance with SCI eligibility based on a Single Scope Background Investigation (SSBI).

Education (Required)

Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Knowledge Management, Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field. Master's degree preferred.

Experience (Required)

  • Minimum 10 years of experience supporting Department of Defense, Combatant Command, Joint, or Special Operations enterprise Knowledge Management, collaboration, or information management environments.
  • Experience supporting a Combatant Command, Joint organization, or Special Operations organization.
  • Experience serving as a Knowledge Management Lead, SharePoint Architect, Enterprise Collaboration Lead, or Microsoft 365 Technical Lead supporting mission-critical operations.
  • Experience designing, implementing, configuring, and sustaining enterprise collaboration environments utilizing Microsoft SharePoint Online, SharePoint Server, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365, and Microsoft Power Platform technologies.
  • Experience developing enterprise information architecture, taxonomy, metadata, knowledge organization, records integration, and content management capabilities.
  • Experience implementing workflow automation, digital modernization, and business process improvement initiatives supporting enterprise Knowledge Management environments.
  • Experience integrating enterprise Knowledge Management capabilities with existing collaboration platforms, records management systems, cybersecurity services, and enterprise technologies.
  • Experience supporting phased deployment, implementation, adoption, and sustainment of enterprise Knowledge Management capabilities across geographically dispersed organizations.
  • Experience supporting Agile software delivery, enterprise modernization, and DevSecOps initiatives.
  • Experience supporting classified and unclassified collaboration environments.
  • Experience developing technical documentation, implementation guides, governance artifacts, standard operating procedures, and user training materials supporting enterprise collaboration technologies.

Technical Knowledge (Required)

  • Enterprise Knowledge Management principles and implementation methodologies.
  • Microsoft 365.
  • SharePoint Online.
  • SharePoint Server.
  • Microsoft Teams.
  • Microsoft Power Platform.
  • Power Apps.
  • Power Automate.
  • Power BI.
  • Enterprise Search.
  • Information Architecture.
  • Metadata and Taxonomy.
  • Records Management integration.
  • Enterprise Collaboration technologies.
  • Workflow Automation.
  • Agile software delivery methodologies.
  • DevSecOps concepts.
  • ITIL principles and service management.
  • Microsoft Office Suite.

Certifications Required

Candidate must possess one or more of the following active certifications at the time of hire:

  • Certified Knowledge Manager (CKM); or
  • Joint Enterprise Communications Capability (JECC) Knowledge Management Practitioner; or
  • Project Management Professional (PMP).
  • Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Power Platform, or other Microsoft collaboration platform certifications are highly desired.

Skills

  • Extensive enterprise Knowledge Management implementation and technical leadership expertise.
  • Strong understanding of Microsoft 365, SharePoint, enterprise collaboration technologies, and information architecture.
  • Demonstrated ability to design, integrate, and modernize enterprise Knowledge Management capabilities supporting complex operational environments.
  • Excellent communication and executive briefing skills.
  • Strong collaboration, facilitation, and stakeholder engagement abilities.
  • Ability to lead enterprise Knowledge Management implementation and modernization initiatives across geographically dispersed organizations.
  • Strong understanding of knowledge governance, records management integration, and organizational knowledge-sharing practices.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to support dynamic mission requirements within high-tempo Special Operations environments.
  • Ability to foster enterprise collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement across the USSOCOM Knowledge Management environment.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

  • EEO and Affirmative Action Policy: DecisionPoint Corporation is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.
  • Pay Transparency Policy: In accordance with Presidential Executive Order 13665, DecisionPoint Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.
  • Authorization to Share Resume and Personal Information: By expressing your interest and submitting your resume for this position, you authorize DecisionPoint Corporation to share your resume, as well as personal information included on the resume, with its subsidiaries, affiliates and teaming partners for the purpose of considering you for this position and other available positions requiring comparable skills, education and experience. Should DecisionPoint Corporation. or its affiliates and teaming partners wish to initiate pre-employment discussions, you will be asked to complete an employment application and related employment documents.

title: Services Lead, Volleyball and Sitting Volleyball
description:
LA28 is the independent, non-profit, privately funded organizing committee for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. We are on a singular mission to create an Olympic and Paralympic Games that celebrate all that this city and country have to offer, delivering an unparalleled experience for athletes, fans, partners and our community.

The 2028 Games mark the return of the Summer Games to the U.S. for the first time in 32 years and Los Angeles’ third time hosting an Olympic Games and first time welcoming the Paralympic Games. This presents the unique and exciting opportunity to celebrate our legacy with the Games and push the Olympic and Paralympic Movements forward, writing a new chapter of Games history in Los Angeles.

Putting on an Olympic and Paralympic Games is a team sport. To build a Games unlike any the world has seen before, we need the best team in place–a team full of perspectives, experiences and expertise. We are guided by the following set of values and behaviors–optimism, integrity, excellence, inclusion, co-creation and boldness–and look forward to hearing about how your past experiences align with them.

Services Lead, Volleyball and Sitting Volleyball

Position Summary

Within this division, LA28 is looking for a Volleyball/Sitting Volleyball Services Lead. Under the authority of the Volleyball/ Sitting Volleyball Sport Manager, the Sport Services Lead is responsible for the planning, organization, coordination, and management of the administrative functions of Volleyball/Sitting Volleyball events at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

The Sport Services Lead will need to relay and facilitate critical services for key stakeholder groups, such as athletes, International Federations and technical officials. They will also coordinate sports information with the various divisions of LA28, participate in the planning and operations of test events, coordinate the recruitment of sports staff, as well as the recruitment and training of volunteers needed for competitions in their sport.

Key Responsibilities

Pre Games Responsibilities

  • Plan, coordinate, and be the dedicated sport contact person in organizing visits from the International Federation in coordination with the IF Services Team and Head of Competition Management.

  • Act as the dedicated sports contact for coordinating services-related matters with the International Federation, including accommodation, transportation, accreditation, and hospitality.

  • Advocate for and coordinate all sport stakeholders’ services including Athletes, Technical Officials, IF Staff and IF guests.

  • Create and ensure organized follow-up of the sharing of databases related to key topics of the Sport Delivery Plan between the International Federation and the various departments of LA28

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for NOC/NPC services teams to establish an effective communication channel in preparation for their visits and information requests.

  • Support the Sport Manager to ensure that all operational procedures and processes of LA28 are understood and followed.

  • Work closely with the Sport Manager, the technical operations lead, the National Federation, and the LA28 Workforce team to recruit, train, and ensure the operational management of sport-specific volunteers.

  • Collaborate with the Sport Manager and the technical operations lead to recruit, train, and deploy the team responsible for delivering the competitions.

  • Work closely with the Sport Manager, the International Federation, and the National Federation for the selection and training of the National Technical Officials (NTOs) required for the Olympic and Paralympic Games.

  • Manage all other tasks and projects related to the delivery of competitions as requested by the Sport Manager.

  • Collaborate with the IF Services and Relations Manager to ensure sharing of information and tools with the services team and other stakeholders.

Games Time Responsibilities

  • Coordinate the following matters within the sport during the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games:

  • Services for athletes

  • Services for the International Federation

  • Services for international and national officials

  • Sport Information

  • Volunteers

  • Manage a team of full-time employees including scheduling, task delegation, training and on-site management

  • Manage a team of Sport Specific Volunteers including recruitment, retention, training, scheduling, recognition and task delegation

  • Act as point of contact with LA28 Functional areas to solve Games Time issues

  • Act as point of contact with the International Federation team to identify and solve Games Time issues.

Background and Requirements

  • Experience collaborating with National and International Federations and knowledge of their structure and functioning during national and international events.

  • Ability to demonstrate an understanding and knowledge of the operational elements required for organizing major sports events/competitions.

  • Experience in international sporting events.

  • Experience in working with an International Federation and knowledge of their structure and operation is an advantage

  • Experience of working with a National Sport Federation and knowledge of its structure and operation at domestic and international events is an advantage

  • Experience managing a team (staff and volunteers) at major events.

  • Good understanding and knowledge of project management, including planning and producing tracking documents.

  • Ability to manage multiple projects involving numerous stakeholders.

  • Skills in report writing and presentation materials.

  • Knowledge of the Olympic and Paralympic Games as well as the specific sport’s technical requirements is an advantage.

  • Proficiency in the Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, as well as Outlook, Teams, SharePoint).

  • Excellent level of English, both written and spoken, is essential for this position.

  • Long-term interest and involvement in Olympic and Paralympic sports.

Physical Requirements and Working Conditions

  • Available to work onsite in our Downtown Los Angeles-based office.

  • The majority of work will be conducted in an office setting, requiring extended periods of time using computers, phones, and other office equipment.

  • The LA28 office is an open floorplan working environment; employees must be able to work efficiently in an open cubicle environment.

  • Hours of work may vary, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, especially during peak event periods.

  • Perform other duties as required; the role will evolve over time and may include operational responsibilities during the Olympic and Paralympic Games.

  • Ability to be outdoors in the elements for long periods of time including sun, wind, rain, etc.

Expectations

  • Understanding and ability to use project management tools is a must.

  • Rigor and very good organizational skills.

  • Strong communication skills.

  • Strong level of commitment to achieve objectives.

  • Willingness to work in a team spirit.

  • Autonomous and proactive.

  • Curiosity and enthusiasm to continuously develop knowledge and skills.

  • Flexible and open-minded in a dynamic environment.

  • Very good interpersonal skills and great adaptability.

  • Knows how to manage time, meet deadlines, and approach projects in a structured manner.

  • Enthusiastic about sport and about the Olympic and Paralympic Movement.

  • Understands and is committed to LA28’s vision, mission, and values.

  • Seeks ways to continuously improve the way things are done.

  • Willing to assist and work with other sport managers/sports.

  • Proficient in excel, word, PDF Power point

Education / Training / Certifications

The annual base salary range for this position is $73,000 - $98,000. The pay scale provided is the range that LA28 reasonably expects to pay as starting base compensation for this role. title: Structural Analyst (Raptor Combustion Devices)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

STRUCTURAL ANALYST (RAPTOR COMBUSTION DEVICES)

The Propulsion Structural Analyst role is responsible for ensuring the structural reliability of Raptor Combustion Devices components subject to extreme pressures, temperatures, vibrations, and accelerations from liftoff to landing. These engineers possess an affinity for physics, structural mechanics, advanced computing, and unraveling intricate challenges associated with complex, high-performance hardware. You will drive analysis, design, manufacturing, and development of hardware for the world’s most advanced rocket engine powering Starship, the largest launch vehicle in history.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Conduct, document, and present static, thermal, thermo-mechanical, dynamic, and durability (fatigue/fracture) analyses on Raptor Combustion Devices hardware through FEA and first principles to inform design decisions and ensure reliability, performance, and reuse requirements are met
  • Collaborate with engineers and technicians across a range of disciplines including design, production, development test, launch, reliability and more to develop hardware that meets high-level engine and vehicle objectives
  • Take a practical, hands-on approach to model validation/verification, ensuring that model predictions are representative of design criteria and tied firmly to test data
  • Support ongoing design, manufacturing and reliability improvements to the engine, and ensure changes and new designs are properly analyzed and qualified

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline, or physics
  • 1+ years of academic or professional experience related to structural analysis (extracurricular and internship experience qualifies)
  • Experience with Finite Element Analysis (FEA) software and post-processing

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Master’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, or materials engineering, or physics
  • 1+ years of academic or professional experience related to combustion devices or rocket engine/motor development
  • Proficient in statics, mechanics of materials, fatigue, dynamics, and heat transfer
  • Hands-on experience with rocket engines/motors, automotive engine design, dynamic or complex static fluid systems
  • Able to perform hand calculations to validate and improve models
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
  • Professional experience using Siemens NX (Unigraphics) and GD&T
  • Experience with manufacturing processes such as CNC mill/lathe, welding, castings, additive, etc. Proficient with the fundamentals of Design for Manufacturing/Assembly (DFMA)

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willingness to travel on occasion in support of testing
  • Willingness to work extended hours and weekends as needed to resolve critical technical issues

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $100,000.00 - $130,000.00
Level 2: $115,000.00 - $160,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. About the job…

As an integral member of our team, you will play a pivotal role in supporting our service business by preparing accurate cost quotations for service and parts orders. You will gather and validate cost inputs, working closely with internal teams to ensure quotes are complete, accurate, and ready for Sales to present to customers.   • Obtain internal approvals and review information in customer portals as required.

The role leads end-to-end audit engagements covering IT infrastructure, AI systems, data flows, cybersecurity controls, and operating procedures in accordance with established professional standards for efficiency, accuracy, security, and risk mitigation. Working with limited supervision, this position applies deep industry, technical, and regulatory expertise to assess information systems, platforms, emerging technologies (including artificial intelligence), and IT operating processes and procedures, while serving as a subject matter resource across the team.

  • Oversees delivery of IT and AI audit engagements against budgets, timelines, and quality expectations, while guiding staff auditors on workload management.

  • Serves as the primary point of contact for technology and AI audit clients, clearly communicating IT and AI risk and control strengths and concerns to peers, supervisors, and clients.

· Maintains process efficiency by keeping all logs and information needed for production reporting current.
· Performs daily mold cleanings as instructed in the Process Binders.
· Performs shut-down and close-out activities.
· Submits close-out/re-start data to Quality.
· Works with Production Control to maintain RTC calendar.
· Executes all RTC events utilizing the RTC Checklist.
· Enhances team efficiency by training and directing the training of less experienced personnel as designated by the Molding Team Leader.
· Improves working conditions by providing supervision of workplace environment with particular emphasis on safety.
· Eliminates down time by writing and processing work orders for/on damaged equipment requiring repair.
· May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

· Industry/product knowledge
· Communication skills
· Detail-oriented

· Teamwork
· Analytical

STARLINK GROWTH LEAD, US WEST

Starlink is a revolutionary satellite constellation delivering low-latency broadband internet around the world—bringing an unprecedented opportunity to significantly impact communities, businesses, and governments worldwide. In the United States, Starlink is rapidly expanding access to high-speed internet for rural, suburban, and underserved communities.

The Growth Team is seeking a Starlink Growth Lead to own consumer subscriber acquisition and growth across the states of Colorado and New Mexico. This role will be responsible for building and executing local growth strategies through local partnerships, sales, affiliates, field marketing, events, and other awareness/growth initiatives. This person will serve as Starlink’s on-the-ground growth owner for the state, accountable for scaling adoption and expanding broadband access to households and communities.

The ideal candidate is an execution-focused, highly motivated operator with experience in business development, partnerships, growth, and/or sales within consumer technology, telecommunications, or subscription-based services. This role requires strong hustle, creativity, and the ability to operate independently while building scalable growth engines for Starlink within the region.

This is a unique opportunity to own an entire state market end-to-end and directly drive Starlink’s expansion.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own Starlink’s consumer subscriber growth strategy and execution for Colorado and New Mexico, fully responsible for achieving ambitious growth targets within the states
  • Serve as Starlink’s local market owner, accountable for awareness, acquisition, partnerships, and performance
  • Execute business development strategies to expand Starlink’s consumer presence across the states
  • Identify, evaluate, and build new customer acquisition channels including with internet service providers, affiliates, utilities, retailers, installers, real estate partners, community organizations, and local governments
  • Drive deal execution from opportunity identification through commercial agreements and partner launch
  • Represent Starlink in external discussions with prospective commercial partners and community stakeholders
  • Lead local marketing and awareness initiatives including field marketing, community events, trade shows, retail activations, and grassroots campaigns
  • Build Starlink’s brand presence and visibility throughout the states
  • Collect and synthesize customer and partner feedback to influence product offerings, pricing strategies, and go-to-market approaches
  • Track and report on subscriber acquisition performance, partner productivity, and campaign / growth initiative ROI
  • Collaborate with sales, product, marketing, operations, engineering, and finance teams to execute scalable growth programs
  • Develop and execute pilots and growth experiments to identify high-performing acquisition channels

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

title: Associate AI Software Engineer
description:
Who we are

Over 600 employees strong, Asure sees Human Capital Management (HCM) through the lens of entrepreneurs and executives with an owner’s mentality. We help businesses develop their “Human Capital” to get to the next level, stay compliant, and allocate their time, money and technology toward growth. Our HCM platform empowers more than 100,000 clients to build great teams and better manage their people while staying compliant in an ever-changing HR legislative landscape. Asure’s HCM offering includes Payroll & Tax, HR, and Time & Attendance software and HR Services ranging from online compliance tools to a fully outsourced HR department.


How you will contribute

As an Associate AI Software Engineer, you will work alongside experienced engineers and AI practitioners to design, develop, test, and maintain AI-powered software that supports Asure's products and platform services. In this role you will primarily write Python and build features that integrate large language models (LLMs) and other AI services into real applications running in our AWS cloud environment.


This role is designed for early-career engineers who are eager to grow by learning modern AI software development practices and contributing to business-critical applications. You will gain hands-on experience integrating LLMs, building the APIs and data pipelines that support AI features, and applying solid software engineering fundamentals — all with the guidance and support of a senior team, and with room to grow your skills over time.


Much of this work supports Asure's agentic AI platform, which is designed to turn AI reasoning into reliable, real-world execution across payroll and HCM workflows — with human confirmation required before any sensitive action is committed. You will help build the tools and integrations that let AI systems take safe, well-scoped actions rather than simply generating text, working with modern agent architectures such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and human-in-the-loop patterns.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and other stakeholders to build AI-powered software features that meet business and customer needs.
  • Write clean, maintainable, well-tested Python code for applications, services, and APIs that leverage AI and LLM capabilities.
  • Integrate large language models (LLMs) and AI services into software applications and business workflows, primarily within our AWS environment.
  • Assist with prompt design, experimentation, evaluation, and validation of LLM-based features under the guidance of senior engineers.
  • Contribute to the data pipelines and retrieval components (e.g., embeddings and vector search) that support AI features.
  • Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback to improve software quality, AI solution effectiveness, and your own technical skills.
  • Assist with troubleshooting, debugging, monitoring, and resolving defects in AI-enabled applications and services.
  • Work with relational, NoSQL, and vector data stores to support AI-driven solutions.
  • Support the deployment and operation of AI applications and services in cloud (AWS) environments.
  • Participate in Agile development activities, including sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives.
  • Follow software engineering and responsible AI best practices, and continuously develop your knowledge across Python, AI/LLMs, and cloud technologies with a curiosity and growth mindset.


Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, or a related technical field.
  • Understanding of software development fundamentals, including object-oriented programming, data structures, algorithms, and software design principles.
  • Proficiency in Python — the primary language for this role — demonstrated through coursework, projects, internships, or personal development. Strong fundamentals in another modern language (e.g., C#, Java, or JavaScript/TypeScript) with the ability to ramp up quickly on Python are also welcome.
  • Foundational understanding of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or generative AI concepts, gained through coursework, certifications, projects, research, internships, or personal learning.
  • Understanding of large language models (LLMs) and basic prompt engineering concepts, and how they are applied in software applications.
  • Familiarity with APIs and web services.
  • Familiarity with at least one major cloud platform (AWS preferred; Azure or Google Cloud Platform also relevant).
  • Basic understanding of data management concepts, including relational and NoSQL databases.
  • Experience using Git or other version control systems.
  • Strong problem-solving, analytical, and communication skills.
  • Ability to learn quickly and collaborate effectively in a team-oriented environment.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience — through work, internships, co-ops, academic or personal projects, hackathons, or open-source contributions — building software that uses LLMs or other AI capabilities.
  • Experience building agentic AI features — including agent orchestration, tool/function calling, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) — or with related frameworks and patterns such as LangChain, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, and embeddings.
  • Exposure to LLM platforms and services such as Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or Google Gemini.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS, particularly its AI/ML and application services (e.g., Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, Lambda, DynamoDB).
  • Exposure to the Python data and ML ecosystem (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, and libraries such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Scikit-learn).
  • Familiarity with RESTful APIs, web services, and third-party or system integrations.
  • Understanding of AI model and prompt evaluation, monitoring, governance, security, and responsible AI principles.
  • Familiarity with Agile methodologies, DevOps practices, automated testing, or CI/CD pipelines.
  • Exposure to data engineering, ETL pipelines, or analytics platforms.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or similar.


Compensation

The starting salary for this position is $80,000 based on relevant experience, skills, and industry knowledge.


Benefits

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, HSA, FSA- All effective on day 1!
  • Company paid Basic Life Insurance, A+D, Long-Term Disability, and Short-Term Disability
  • 401K Program with 3% safe harbor contribution
  • Employee Stock Purchase Program
  • Fitness Reimbursement Program
  • Self-Managed PTO


Our Mission

To provide Human Capital Management (HCM) software and services that help companies grow, while nurturing a culture of growth around us.

  • Helping customers grow by getting the most from their human capital.
  • Helping our employees grow personally and professionally.
  • Growing relationships in our communities that inspire goodness.
  • Grow shareholder value


Our Vision

Be the most trusted Human Capital Management resource to entrepreneurs everywhere.


Our Values

Reflect who we are and what we stand for as a company.

  • Embrace Change
  • Lead with Integrity
  • Own the Outcome
  • Deliver Awesome
  • Be a Good Human


We are an equal opportunity employer. All candidates must be legally authorized to work in the US, as we are unable to sponsor or transfer Visas at this time.


NO AGENCIES PLEASE

Any unsolicited resumes sent to Asure Software from a third party, such as an Agency, including unsolicited resumes sent to Asure’s mailing address, fax machine or email address, directly to employees or hiring managers will be considered Asure property. Asure will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume.

About Advocate Health

Advocate Health is the third-largest nonprofit, integrated health system in the United States, created from the combination of Advocate Aurora Health and Atrium Health. Providing care under the names Advocate Health Care in Illinois; Atrium Health in the Carolinas, Georgia and Alabama; and Aurora Health Care in Wisconsin, Advocate Health is a national leader in clinical innovation, health outcomes, consumer experience and value-based care. About the Role:

IMAX is seeking a Service Inventory Specialist to support the efficient distribution of service parts across our global theatre network. Working closely with Logistics, Procurement, Shipping, and Technical Services teams, the Service Inventory Specialist plays a critical role in supporting field operations through inventory management, parts distribution, shipment coordination, and SAP transactions. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where responsiveness and accuracy are essential to maintaining exceptional customer service.

Inventory & Parts Operations

  • Process service part requests accurately and ensure timely fulfillment

  • Maintain inventory accuracy through SAP inventory transactions and system updates

  • Create and process intra-company orders within SAP

  • Monitor inventory levels and support replenishment activities to maintain adequate stock availability

  • Support parts depot operations and return center activities to improve inventory efficiency

Logistics & Distribution

  • Coordinate domestic and international shipments with Logistics and Shipping teams

  • Monitor deliveries to depots and ensure shipment transactions are completed accurately in SAP

  • Track shipments and provide delivery updates to internal stakeholders

  • Support shipping accuracy, delivery performance, and return cycle time objectives

  • Assist with job costing and logistics documentation as required

Operational Support

  • Prioritize service orders based on operational requirements and business needs

  • Collaborate with Procurement, Logistics, and Technical Services teams to resolve inventory and shipment issues

  • Identify opportunities to improve inventory processes, shipping efficiency, and overall service performance

  • Maintain accurate records while ensuring compliance with company policies and operational procedures

Qualifications

  • 1–2 years of experience in inventory management, warehouse operations, logistics, or supply chain

  • Broad understanding of inventory operations and logistics processes

  • Experience working with ERP systems; SAP experience preferred

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Word

  • Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail and accuracy

  • Excellent problem-solving skills with the ability to prioritize competing demands

  • Strong interpersonal and customer service skills

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Ability to work effectively under time-sensitive deadlines in a fast-paced environment

Nice to Haves

  • Experience supporting technical service or aftermarket operations

  • Knowledge of warehouse and inventory best practices

title: Waiheke Bus Drivers (Summer - full-time / fixed term)
description:
We're gearing up for our busiest period with summer around the corner and will be employing Bus Drivers on a fixed term, full-time basis. Ideally you'll be able to start September and work through till approximately the end of April 2027.


About us

Through a reliable network and a passionate team, Fullers360 ferries nearly 6 million people every year, getting commuters to work and visitors to play. We are in an exciting phase of growing our tourism market, restless to elevate the experience we deliver to every single one of our customers.


About the role

Are you passionate about delivering exceptional service and exploring beautiful destinations? Waiheke Bus Company needs you! We’re seeking fixed-term Bus Drivers that can work 30+ hours a week to join our team and create memorable experiences for our visitors.


Every day will be an opportunity to deliver fantastic customer service and share a unique and safe experience for our passengers, driving urban or tour coaches and experience the stunning views from your ‘office’ that is Waiheke Island.

Our bus drivers are everyday people. They enjoy working with customers (commuters and tourists visitors), love driving through Waiheke's challenging and spectacular roads and take pride in their job. Dealing with so many different people every day requires you to communicate clearly (written and oral), but also be flexible and patient enough to understand those who are not English speakers. Caring about their safety is a must.

Skills and Experience:

  • YOU MUST hold a class 2 or 4 licence and your P endorsement to be eligible for this position
  • You must have the right to work in NZ to be considered for the role
  • Strong communication skills and a friendly demeanor
  • Excellent driving record and adherence to safety regulations
  • Previous tour driving experience
  • WBC is a 7-day operation – you will be rostered 5 out of 7 days, including weekends and public holidays
  • You will need to pass our pre-employment screening and background checks
  • You must live on Waiheke Island OR be willing to commute to and from our depot in Ostend, Waiheke Island


      Summer crew overview

      • Starting early October
      • Fixed term contract at 40+ hours per week until April 2027
      • Starting and ending your shifts at the Waiheke Bus Company located on Ostend Road
      • Need to be able and willing to work over the Christmas and New Year’s period
      • Need to be available to work 40+ hours a week

      Hours of work: (we operate between 5am - 1am, Monday to Sunday)

      • Average of 9-hour days starting as rostered

      Salary and perks:

      • Training / Induction rate $27.85 per hour, once signed off hourly rate of $32.89 per hour, paid weekly
      • Free ferry travel for our employees for work and leisure
      • Free bus travel on island (for the employee)


      *Candidates must have the right to work in NZ to be considered for this role.


      Please note: Any information you provide will be used to evaluate your suitability to this position. We will hold onto your details for any future opportunities unless asked otherwise.

title: Trading & Value Chain Optimization Advisory Consultant
description:
Consultant - Trading & VCO Advisory - Enterprise Operations & Risk

Deloitte's Regulatory, Risk & Forensic team helps clients turn complex risks and evolving regulations into defensible actions that strengthen, protect, and transform their organizations. Join us to apply advanced data, AI, emerging technologies, and industry insights to bring clarity to complexity and accelerate value creation.

Work you'll do

As a Trading & VCO Advisory Consultant on the Enterprise Operations & Risk team, you will be responsible for:
  • Support analysis across the commodity trade lifecycle (e.g., deal capture, scheduling/nomination, pricing, settlements) to help identify data, process, or control improvement opportunities within trading and risk operations
  • Support the design, implementation, and ongoing improvement of value chain optimization programs for Commodity Trading companies in Oil & Gas, Power & Utilities, Agriculture and other adjacent commodity sectors.
  • Analyze commercial and operational data to identify optimization opportunities, quantify value, and support recommendations for margin improvement
  • Collaborate with client stakeholders and Deloitte teams to align optimization initiatives with business objectives, timelines, and delivery requirements
  • Contribute to the development of solution materials, client presentations, and sales support assets used in pursuit and delivery efforts
  • Support project workstreams across refining, shipping, storage, marketing, and commodity trading operations while helping track performance against defined key performance indicators

A successful candidate would possess these skills:
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The team

Our Enterprise Operations & Risk offering enables clients to achieve profitable growth and competitive advantage by optimizing "heart of the business" operations. We leverage deep domain expertise to extend enterprise resilience, agility and remediation. Our professionals address client needs which span the organization and impact strategy, operations, performance and reputation.

Qualifications

Required:
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related field
  • 4+ years of experience in value chain, operations, supply chain management, or consulting
  • Experience supporting work across downstream oil & gas functions, including refining, shipping, storage, marketing, and commodity trading operations
  • Foundational understanding of the commodities trade lifecycle and related risk concepts (e.g., deal capture, confirmations, scheduling, settlements, market/credit risk exposures)
  • Experience supporting commercial or operational optimization programs and tracking performance against key performance indicators
  • Experience creating client-ready analyses, presentations, or financial models to quantify business value
  • Ability to travel 75%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve
  • Limited immigration sponsorship may be available.

Preferred:
  • Experience with financial modeling to quantify value and business benefits
  • Experience using data, analytics, or artificial intelligence in commercial or operational optimization
  • Exposure to CTRM/ETRM platforms (e.g., ION Endur/Openlink, Allegro, RightAngle, Eka, TriplePoint, SAP Commodity Management, or similar)
  • Familiarity with one or more commodity markets (e.g., power, natural gas, crude/refined products, LNG, metals, agriculture)
  • Basic understanding of risk and analytics concepts such as mark-to-market, valuation, or scenario analysis
  • Experience working in a consulting or advisory environment

title: Staff Inbound Product Manager
description:
Knowledge is the connective tissue of employee self-service, and the quality of that knowledge influences how well AI systems perform. Bad articles don't just frustrate employees; they produce assured wrong answers from AI agents. This role exists to close that gap.

As a Staff Technical Product Manager on the AI Experiences & Platform Products team, you will own the product strategy and delivery for ServiceNow's enterprise employee-facing Knowledge Management product, built on ServiceNow Knowledge Center. You will drive governance frameworks, article lifecycle tooling, content quality standards, and the AI-readiness of the knowledge base that powers Now Assist, Moveworks and Employee Works across the enterprise. You will also serve as the internal customer zero for ServiceNow KM capabilities, validating features and representing production experience in customer-facing forums.

What you get to do in this role

Product ownership & roadmap

  • Own the technical product vision and roadmap for the enterprise employee-facing Knowledge Management product, including article authoring experience, lifecycle management, governance tooling, and AI readiness capabilities
  • Define, prioritize, and refine requirements; document epics and stories with clear acceptance criteria; drive end-to-end feature delivery in partnership with engineering, UX, and platform teams
  • Make trade-off choices between what's possible, desirable, and viable and communicate the reasoning clearly to stakeholders across DT and the business domains.

Knowledge governance

  • Guide the enterprise Knowledge Governance model: ownership structure, champion accountability, pillar coverage, and scaled governance across all employee-facing knowledge domains
  • Build and maintain the knowledge lifecycle framework, authoring, republishing, expiry, and retirement with policies and operational workflows that work at enterprise scale without constant intervention
  • Define and operationalize the Knowledge Health Score and standards that connect article quality to AI system performance across the enterprise

AI-readiness & content quality

  • Own the product definition for AI-facing knowledge quality: structural requirements, quality standards, and gap identification across the enterprise knowledge base
  • Partner with IT Service Management Team (AI Agents), Search & Conversational Interfaces (Now Assist and Moveworks) teams to understand how knowledge quality affects AI confidence and answer accuracy and build the feedback loop into governance
  • Surface and prioritize knowledge gaps that cause AI failures or broken self-service experiences before they reach employees

Customer zero

  • Serve as ServiceNow's internal customer zero for ServiceNow Knowledge Center and Now Assist authoring capabilities.
  • Validate features, surface issues early, and provide structured product feedback that influences the ServiceNow KM product roadmap
  • Represent production experience in Now-on-Now customer engagements and executive briefing centers; translate internal results into credible customer-facing narratives

Success measurement

  • Define adoption, quality, and AI-performance metrics across the enterprise KM product; instrument them and establish baselines
  • Examine usage data and knowledge telemetry to inform prioritization; validate impact post-launch
  • Run retrospectives; use what the data says to drive iteration

To be successful in this role you have:

  • 7+ years of Technical Product Management experience, with demonstrated ownership of knowledge management, content platforms, or enterprise self-service products at scale
  • Fluency in AI:
  • Experience using AI in your own work processes such as drafting requirements, reviewing data, automating workflows, not just awareness of AI trends
  • Delivered at least one AI-powered product or AI-consuming capability with measurable outcomes
  • Day-to-day fluency in tools like Claude, Copilot, as part of how you work, not an occasional experiment
  • Governance instincts: you can design accountability structures that hold, build standards people didn't ask for, and get buy-in without a mandate
  • Strong technical judgment - you can scope a feature, write testable acceptance criteria, and hold a credible conversation with an engineer about implementation trade-offs
  • Clear communicator across audiences: you can translate content quality problems into business risk for a VP, and translate product strategy into actionable requirements for a scrum team
  • Demonstrated ability to turn ambiguous problems into a structured, prioritized roadmap

Preferred qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with ServiceNow Knowledge Management, Knowledge Center, or Now Assist and/or Moveworks.
  • Familiarity with how AI retrieval works and how knowledge structure affects AI answer quality
  • Experience working with knowledge taxonomy, metadata standards, or content structure in a context where AI or search performance depended on it
  • Prior experience in customer zero, as design partner, or internal beta capacity for an enterprise SaaS product

Work Personas

We approach our distributed world of work with flexibility and trust. Work personas (flexible, remote, or required in office) are categories that are assigned to ServiceNow employees depending on the nature of their work and their assigned work location. Learn more here. To determine eligibility for a work persona, ServiceNow may confirm the distance between your primary residence and the closest ServiceNow office using a third-party service.

ServiceNow is an equal opportunity employer. In addition, all qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with legal requirements.

We strive to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application process, or are unable to use this online application and need an alternative method to apply, please contact globaltalentss@servicenow.com for assistance.

title: Lead Solutions Architect
description:
Become a part of our caring community

Job Description Summary
The Lead Solutions Architect provides architecture leadership for CenterWell Home Health programs and platforms, shaping conceptual and reference architectures, governing solution designs, and aligning delivery teams to cloud and data strategies. The scope includes high-priority initiatives as well as interoperability and provider-data integrations that span CenterWell and Humana Insurance.

As Lead Solution Architect, you'll be the senior individual contributor on a team with broad accountability across CenterWell's dispensing pharmacy portfolio — mail order, specialty, retail, and associated platforms. You'll own the architectural vision for complex, multi-system initiatives, shape how technology decisions get made, and act as a connective force between business strategy, engineering execution, and enterprise standards.

You will operate within CenterWell IT – Cross-CenterWell Architecture. You will collaborate with product, engineering, EA Activation, security, data, and operations. You will engage governance forums to enable Integrated Health across CenterWell and Humana Insurance.

Key Activities

  • Quickly conduct structured knowledge transfer with existing architects and relevant stakeholders to capture critical in-flight designs and decisions.
  • Review current initiatives and establish an architectural roadmap aligned with organizational priorities.
  • Develop or refine reference architectures and design patterns for core platforms and solutions.
  • Collaborate with governance and compliance teams to validate designs against enterprise standards and regulatory requirements.
  • Define integration strategies and solution blueprints for key systems and data flows.
  • Establish architecture review processes and decision forums to support delivery readiness and quality assurance.

Demonstrated depth in:

  • Agent orchestration (tools/function calling, planning, memory, multi-agent collaboration)
  • Enterprise guardrails (security, compliance, responsible AI)
  • Robust MLOps/LLMOps practices for observability, evaluation, and cost/performance optimization
  • Proven ability to integrate AI systems with event-driven microservices, vector databases/feature stores, and CI/CD pipelines, while leading reference architectures and cross-cloud patterns that scale reliably.
  • Executive-level communication and stakeholder management across product, engineering, and enterprise functions.

Core Responsibilities

  • Architectural Leadership: Own end-to-end solution architecture for Home Health initiatives, translating business outcomes into composable designs across systems of experience, operations, and insight.
  • Reference Architectures & Patterns: Author and maintain reference architectures for data platform, clinical documents NLP, RPA/automation, and interoperability patterns; steward pattern reuse across CenterWell when applicable.
  • Governance & Compliance: Lead architecture checkpoints and risk reviews; ensure designs conform to enterprise guardrails and privacy/security requirements. Participate in governance forums (e.g., ARB, TRB, MOR).
  • Delivery Enablement: Partner with product and engineering to convert conceptual designs into executable architectural runways; de-risk delivery with measurable non-functional requirements (NFRs).
  • Data & Integration Strategy: Define integration contracts and domain boundaries for provider data, EMR, and Snowflake/Databricks/Azure data platforms; ensure observability, lineage, and data protection.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborate with CenterWell leaders, EA Activation, security, and segment CIO teams; communicate decisions clearly to executives and delivery teams.


Use your skills to make an impact

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or a related field.
  • 8 years of progressive information technology experience directly related to architecture/engineering, information security, or other specialized technology field.
  • 5+ years of solution architecture experience with healthcare delivery or payer/provider ecosystems; proven delivery within regulated environments (HIPAA/PHI).
  • Hands-on architecture across Azure services and Snowflake/Databricks (data lake/data platform patterns, data sharing, identity & access, vault/secrets management).
  • Demonstrated leadership producing reference architectures and governing solution designs across multiple teams.
  • Strong competency in APIs/event-driven integration, security models, and NFRs (availability, performance, resilience).
  • Generative & Agentic AI, Multi-Cloud is a specialty of a seasoned Solutions Architect. This expert has hands-on experience delivering generative and agentic AI on Google Cloud, Azure, and AWS. They leverage services like Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, and Amazon Bedrock. Their expertise includes implementing production-grade capabilities, such as RAG, fine-tuning, prompt/knowledge management, and secure data integrations.

Preferred Qualifications — Core Home Health

  • Experience with clinical document NLP pipelines and automation/RPA in Home Health workflows (eligibility, authorization).
  • Familiarity with Home Healthcare solutions conceptual architecture and operating models and artifacts; ability to evolve them with measurable outcomes.
  • Knowledge of enterprise identity/access management flows and Azure group governance within tenants.
  • Experience participating in portfolio governance and activation forums (e.g., ARB, TRB, MOR) and translating those decisions into architectural runways.

Preferred Qualifications — Agentic AI Skills

  • Agent orchestration: planning, tool/function calling
  • Long/short-term memory and context management
  • Multi-agent collaboration and role assignment
  • Human-in-the-loop review and overrides workflow
  • Safety guardrails, policy enforcement, governance
  • Telemetry: tracing, evaluation, A/B testing
  • Reliability: retries, fallbacks, deterministic handoffs
  • Tool ecosystem integration (APIs, MCPs)

Additional Information

Work-At-Home Requirements

  • Must have the ability to provide a high-speed DSL or cable modem for a home office. Associates or contractors who live and work from home in the state of California will be provided payment for their internet expense.
  • A minimum standard speed for optimal performance of 25×10 (25 Mbps download × 10 Mbps upload) is required.
  • Satellite and Wireless Internet service is NOT allowed for this role.
  • A dedicated space lacking ongoing interruptions to protect member PHI / HIPAA information

In certain roles, the minimum recommended internet speed required by Humana may not be sufficient for business needs. Humana reserves the right to require associates to upgrade their internet service if necessary. Work from a dedicated space lacking ongoing interruptions to protect member PHI / HIPAA information.

Travel: While this is a remote position, occasional travel to Humana's offices for training or meetings may be required.

Scheduled Weekly Hours

40

This job is eligible for a bonus incentive plan. This incentive opportunity is based upon company and/or individual performance.

title: Test Engineer, Vehicle Integration
description:
About Harbinger

Harbinger is an American commercial electric vehicle (EV) company on a mission to transform an industry starving for innovation. Harbinger’s best-in-class team of EV, battery, and drivetrain experts have pooled their deep experience to bring a first-of-its-kind EV platform to support the growing demand for medium-duty EVs and Hybrids. Harbinger: Familiar Form, Revolutionary Foundation.

Job Overview

Harbinger is seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Vehicle Test Engineer to join their team. You will be responsible for planning, executing, and analyzing vehicle testing activities to ensure the quality, performance, and safety of their vehicles. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to identify and resolve issues, contributing to the successful development and launch of new commercial electric vehicles.

What You'll Do:

title: Founding Finance Lead
description:
The Opportunity

Substrate is building the critical infrastructure layer between AI and biology: an AI-native automated lab that produces biological data at scale. Biological foundation models can predict but cannot experiment, and the high-quality data they need does not exist at the scale required. Substrate generates it, with quality and provenance built in. Our first lab opens in London in 2026, with protein characterisation coming online first and functional genomics following through 2027. Our customers range from foundation model labs to global pharma.

We are hiring a founding finance leader to build the finance function from the ground up. Substrate is an unusual finance problem: significant capital expenditure on automated workcells and lab infrastructure, funding through both equity and debt, and a usage-priced commercial model that turns physical lab capacity into customer cost. You will own how we account for it, how we fund it, how we price it, and how we explain all of it to investors and lenders.

About Substrate

Substrate is an AI-native automated lab. Our four co-founders are Mostafa ElSayed (co-founder and CEO, and founder and CEO of Automata), Oli Hoy (co-founder, leading infrastructure, software and operations), Alexey Morgunov (co-founder, leading intelligence software and the science roadmap), and Anna Huyghues-Despointes (co-founder, leading commercial and partnerships). The automated lab runs on Automata's workcell platform.

We are funded by a combination of equity and debt. We are not a CRO and we are not a cloud lab. We are the infrastructure that generates large-scale, high-quality, AI-ready biological data.

The Role

You will own the finance function end to end. The day-one priorities are the operational pieces of a fast-growing company: month-end close, management accounts, payroll, statutory accounts, the first audit, and the cap table.

Three parts of this role go well beyond standard controllership, and they are why it matters so much to Substrate.

Planning, analysis and corporate finance. You own the financial model, scenario planning, and the numbers that go to the co-founders and investors, and you are the finance partner in the room when commercial and fundraising decisions are made. You run the cap table through SAFE conversion and into the priced rounds that follow.

Capital intensity and the debt that funds it. Substrate runs a CAPEX-heavy operating model: automated workcells, lab fit-out and instrumentation, each with its own contracting, depreciation and treatment. You account for that spend, structure and manage the venture and infrastructure debt that funds it, and sequence drawdown so the cash position stays clear. Some of the build is part-funded by government grants, which fold into the same picture.

Pricing. We sell access to our platform on a usage basis, priced on a model that maps the physical inputs of a run (instrument time, materials, compute, complexity) onto a cleaner customer-facing unit of value. We have a working hypothesis. You will stress-test it, build the underlying cost model, set the incentive structure, take it to early customers, and operationalise it as the commercial pricing system, connected to real billing and revenue recognition. This is finance work and product work at once, and it is the single highest-impact piece of finance work in the company.

You will build a finance function that is augmented by AI from the start; you are as interested in designing the systems that run the close and the numbers as in running them yourself. You will be pragmatic about doing the work directly through the early months, and you will build the team underneath you as Substrate grows.

Your First 90 Days

By day 30

  • Take ownership of the books, payroll and the close, and decide what stays in house and what is outsourced.

  • Sit down with each co-founder and take ownership of the financial model.

  • Get a grip on the cap table and the funding mechanics.

By day 60

  • Stand up the management accounts and a clear monthly rhythm. Make Substrate a company whose finances can be explained in five minutes.

  • Get into the pricing problem: build the underlying cost model and stress-test the current hypothesis.

  • Map the CAPEX programme against funding drawdown and the debt facility.

By day 90

  • Take a refined usage-based pricing structure to early customers and incorporate their feedback.

  • Have the first audit and the R&D tax position planned and underway.

  • Position the finance function for the next raise: clean numbers and defensible unit economics that investors, lenders and customers all understand.

Who You Are

You are an experienced finance leader who has built or rebuilt a finance function in a capital-intensive, usage-priced business. The shape of the problem is what attracts you: significant CAPEX, debt-funded infrastructure, complex revenue mechanics, and a cost model with many physical variables. You are equally strong in planning and analysis and in controllership, and you are comfortable owning corporate finance: the cap table, the debt, and the fundraise.

You have done this in an adjacent infrastructure business: compute, cloud, data centres, energy, telecoms, manufacturing, or somewhere similar that builds physical capacity and sells it on a usage basis. You can carry those lessons across without needing the company to look exactly like the last one. You do not need a background in biology or life sciences, and we will not test you on the science; what matters is the structure of the operating model.

You write clearly for investors, and you can take a complicated set of numbers and make it simple. You can build a financial model from scratch and defend its assumptions in a room of sceptical investors. You enjoy pricing as a problem and you have an opinion on it. You are equally at home in the detail (a bank reconciliation, a deferred revenue schedule) and in the strategy (where the next tranche of capital comes from, and what it costs us to take it).

Substrate's early roles are deliberately amorphous, and you are comfortable in that. When something outside the obvious finance remit needs owning in the early months (supplier management or procurement as the lab kits out, for example), you pick it up and do it well rather than wait for someone else. We do not hire people into boxes.

You are London-based, or willing to be, and happy to spend regular time in person at the lab as we build.

Must have

  • A track record of building or rebuilding a finance function end to end: the team, the cadence, the close, and the working relationship with founders or an executive team. Typically six or more years of progressive finance experience, including a senior finance role at a venture-backed or capital-intensive growth company.

  • Strong FP&A ownership: building and owning the financial model, scenario planning, investor updates, and partnering with the executive team on commercial and fundraising decisions.

  • Direct experience of CAPEX-heavy operating models: depreciation policy, asset accounting, vendor contracting, and the cash dynamics of significant up-front spend.

  • Corporate finance and debt: cap table mechanics, SAFE conversion, and structuring or managing venture or infrastructure debt against a capital programme.

  • Direct experience of usage-priced commercial models: cost-to-serve modelling, pricing design, revenue recognition under usage rules, and the operational link between billing and product.

  • A background in a capital-intensive, usage- or capacity-priced infrastructure business (compute, cloud, data centres, energy, telecoms, or similar).

Nice to have

  • Experience with government grant or other non-dilutive funding.

  • The Series A and Series B fundraise cycle: SAFE conversion, cap table mechanics, investor materials and diligence.

  • Designing or operationalising token-based, unit-based, or otherwise usage-quantified pricing.

  • Comfort building AI- and agent-augmented finance workflows.

Why This Is Unusual

Most finance leadership roles at venture-backed companies are either pure SaaS finance (clean ARR, clean margin, clean billing) or operational finance at a more mature stage. This is neither. You will design a finance function for a capital-intensive infrastructure business with a usage-priced commercial model, debt-funded CAPEX, and a live funding round, and you will be the person who decides how the pricing model actually works.

It is also a finance role with real product surface area. The pricing model is one of the most important commercial decisions Substrate will make, and you will own it. Some finance leaders find that energising and some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are.

How We Work

We are London-based and we work in a hybrid way. The founding team is spread across London, New York and Europe and travels often, so we lean on writing things down and working asynchronously. Finance, payroll and audit work goes better with regular time together, so we will value your presence at our London lab, especially through the early build.

We work to a weekly cadence, with a Monday planning meeting and a Friday close, and a quarterly offsite. We are direct with each other, and we expect to be challenged.

Our UK benefits include:

  • 30 days annual leave, plus your birthday off

  • A salary-sacrifice pension with a 10% employer contribution

  • Private medical insurance

  • Income protection, life cover and critical illness

  • A personal financial coach and annual financial planning

The Team You Will Join

You will report to Oli Hoy, co-founder, who leads infrastructure, software and operations and currently carries finance until you take it on. You will work most closely with Mostafa ElSayed, co-founder and CEO, on commercial and fundraising matters, and with Anna Huyghues-Despointes, co-founder, and the wider co-founder team on the financial model and the numbers.

You are the first dedicated finance hire, joining four co-founders and a fast-growing team.

Our Process

We move quickly on people we are excited about. The process has four stages: an initial screen; a behavioural and values conversation; a technical session on the finance and commercial substance of the role (FP&A, the debt and CAPEX picture, and how you think about usage-based pricing); and references. Expect roughly two to three weeks end to end.

If you are not sure whether you are a fit, apply anyway. The most useful conversations we have had have been with people who were not sure.

Substrate is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background.
