title: Principle Power Control/SW Engineer
description:
At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe.

Principle Power Control/SW Engineer

Build your career with Jabil! We challenge and empower you to make the most of your talents while working with outstanding colleagues from diverse backgrounds who share your drive and passion to make Jabil grow!

Job Summary

The lead power control / SW engineer will lead control software, embedded firmware, and system integration for Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) products, including PCS/inverter controls, EMS/BMS interfaces, SCADA integration, protection logic, diagnostics, and critical power operating modes. This role translates system and customer requirements into reliable software architecture, control requirements, communication interfaces, validation plans, and release criteria to support safe, efficient, and compliant BESS operation. The engineer will work with power electronics, system architecture, battery engineering, test, manufacturing, quality, suppliers, and customers to deliver high-performance BESS platforms for commercial, industrial, utility-scale, microgrid, and critical power applications.

Location:

This role will be based at Jabil's Huangpu office in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, China.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead BESS power control and software activities, including PCS/inverter controls, EMS/BMS interfaces, SCADA integration, protection logic, diagnostics, and critical power operating modes.
  • Define control requirements for charge/discharge operation, grid-following and grid-forming behavior, reactive power, frequency response, black start readiness, fault ride-through, anti-islanding, safe shutdown, and system recovery.
  • Develop and review software architecture, state machines, control sequences, communication mapping, alarms, diagnostics, cybersecurity requirements, configuration management, and release readiness criteria.
  • Establish critical coding expectations, including modular design, coding standards, traceability, version control, code review, unit testing, static analysis, integration testing, HIL/SIL validation, cybersecurity review, and release control.
  • Integrate BESS software with PCS, BMS, EMS, SCADA, site controllers, meters, protection relays, HVAC, fire safety interfaces, and customer or utility control systems.
  • Plan and support software verification and validation, including requirements-based testing, regression testing, HIL/SIL testing, FAT/SAT, commissioning support, grid compliance testing, and field issue troubleshooting.
  • Partner with suppliers, customers, test labs, and cross-functional teams to improve system performance, reliability, and launch readiness.
  • May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Job Qualifications

Technical Knowledge & Skills

  • Strong understanding of BESS control architecture, including PCS/inverter controls, EMS/BMS coordination, SCADA integration, site controllers, protection logic, grid services, and critical power operating modes.
  • Solid experiences developing or specifying embedded software, firmware, PLC logic, EMS logic, or supervisory control software for power electronics, energy storage, UPS, microgrid, renewable energy, or industrial automation systems.
  • Hands-on knowledge of critical software practices, including C/C++, Python, IEC 61131-3 PLC languages, MATLAB/Simulink model-based design, modular architecture, version control, requirements traceability, code review, unit testing, static analysis, regression testing, and release control.
  • Familiar with software quality and safety practices such as MISRA C awareness, secure coding, cybersecurity review, functional safety concepts, FMEA/DFMEA support, configuration management, defect tracking, and requirements-based verification.
  • Knowledge of industrial communication protocols such as CAN, Modbus TCP/RTU, IEC 61850, DNP3, MQTT, OPC UA, Ethernet/IP, RS-485, TCP/IP, and PCS/BMS/EMS/SCADA interfaces.
  • Strong understanding of control functions for charge/discharge scheduling, active/reactive power control, frequency response, voltage support, ramp-rate control, peak shaving, islanding, black start readiness, fault ride-through, alarms, diagnostics, and fail-safe operation.
  • Experience with simulation, test, and development tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS, PSIM, PSCAD, Python, Git, Jira, requirements management tools, HIL platforms, and protocol analyzers.
  • Working knowledge of BESS and grid-related requirements, including UL 9540, UL 1741, IEEE 1547, IEC 61850, IEC 62477, IEC 61000, NEC awareness, NERC CIP awareness, and regional grid interconnection requirements.

Non-Technical Knowledge & Skills

  • Worked as part of a global team.
  • Strong English communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively across global teams.
  • Build trusted relationships and effectively influence others and share best practices.
  • Assess a project and articulate risk while developing project milestones.
  • Develop projects in a stage-gate process (PLCM).
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities, meet commitments, and communicate risks, assumptions, and dependencies proactively.
  • Ability to adapt quickly to changing customer, technical, and business requirements while effectively managing complexity and ambiguity.
  • Demonstrates ownership and accountability in overcoming challenges and delivering results under pressure.
  • Mentor less experienced engineers.

Education & experience requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Control Engineering, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Power Electronics, Power Systems, Automation, or a related technical field is required.
  • Master’s degree or Ph.D. in a relevant engineering discipline is preferred, especially with emphasis on control systems, embedded software, power electronics controls, power systems, grid-connected converters, automation, or energy storage systems.
  • Typically requires 5+ years of hands-on experience in embedded software, firmware, controls engineering, EMS/SCADA integration, inverter controls, PLC programming, BESS integration, critical power systems, or related engineering roles.
  • Experience in Battery Energy Storage Systems, PCS/inverter controls, UPS, microgrids, renewable energy, solar plus storage, EV charging, industrial automation, data center power, or utility-scale energy systems is strongly preferred.

title: Field Safety Specialist - Utility Line Clearance - Clarksville
description:
About us:

The Halter Group (The Halter Group) - Established in 1982, The Halter Group has continued to grow in the Utility Line clearance arena in the area, providing comprehensive services to our clients. We pride ourselves on providing the best possible service to our customers, contractors and value our employees through honesty and integrity.


We are currently seeking a full-time Field Safety Specialist who is passionate about safety and ensuring the safety of others, responsible, self-motived and managed, leads by example and reliable to join our team. This position reports directly to the Safety Director. A clear, valid driver's license is required and a CDL A or B is preferred. Bilingual (English/Spanish) is highly desired.


This will position will service the greater KY, TN, GA areas. Travel is required.


JOB DESCRIPTION

Responsible for providing field support services and assisting the Safety Director, Safety Administrator, Regional Managers, Supervisors, and team members with the implementation and enforcement of Halter and client safety and health policies, procedures, and requirements. This position provides day-to-day compliance support, conducts routine compliance inspections and observations, delivers and develops safety-related training, investigates incidents, and maintains recordkeeping.


SCOPE

The Field Safety Specialist plays a critical role in supporting field operations by directly applying and enforcing safety policies, regulatory standards, and company and client expectations. This position is primarily field-based and is responsible for ensuring that crews operate safely and in compliance with internal procedures and external regulations. The Field Safety Specialist serves as a visible presence on job sites — proactively identifying hazards, conducting safety training, performing targeted and broad-scope inspections, and reinforcing a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. The role requires daily interaction with field crews, as well as supervision and management, to align safe work expectations with operational goals.


KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Collaborate with key stakeholders to ensure effective implementation of safety programs in accordance with management system elements.
  • Conduct training as necessary to ensure applicable rules, procedures, and expectations are understood.
  • Conduct engagements and observations with employees and contract partners, providing immediate coaching on safe and unsafe conditions observed.
  • Conduct joint compliance walks and site reviews with utility and client representatives, serving as Halter's field safety point of contact.
  • Conduct field and site inspections, document deficiencies, and develop sustainable solutions to prevent repeat findings.
  • Participate in the incident investigation process, including root cause analysis and identification of corrective actions.
  • Reinforce safe work expectations in accordance with applicable laws, rules, procedures, and standards.
  • Review safety-related data and metrics to identify trends and recommend corrective actions to address issues identified.
  • Exercise stop-work authority whenever an unsafe condition is present.
  • Make recommendations to management concerning disciplinary action when safety violations occur.
  • Conduct new-hire safety orientation.
  • Identify, evaluate, and coordinate the implementation of new methods and approaches to accelerate safety improvement.


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

  • Work collaboratively in a team environment and contribute to group projects.
  • Deliver group presentations and training sessions.
  • Perform and prioritize tasks under time constraints with accuracy.
  • Interpret and apply OSHA, ANSI Z133, DOT, and other applicable regulatory standards.
  • Document field observations, incident findings, and corrective actions thoroughly and accurately.
  • Travel to job sites with the flexibility to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision while aligning with the direction of the Safety Director and Safety Administrator.
  • Deliver effective safety training, briefings, and orientations to field and management personnel.
  • Use technology (e.g., tablets, laptop, safety applications, GPS, Microsoft Office) to support safety reporting and communication.


QUALIFICATIONS


Experience

  • 1–3 years of experience in utility vegetation management, line clearance, or arboriculture.
  • Prior experience as a field general foreman, crew foreman, or trainer is a plus.


Education

  • Associate's degree in occupational safety, safety management, or a related field preferred; or an equivalent combination of education and relevant industry experience.


Certifications & Licenses

  • Valid driver's license with an acceptable motor vehicle record that meets company and insurance standards (required).
  • Current First Aid/CPR certification, or the ability to obtain within 90 days of hire.
  • OSHA 30-Hour (General Industry or Construction) preferred.

title: Chemistry Principal Scientist
description:
The opportunity

Substrate is building a network of fully autonomous wet labs, cloud-based data production facilities for AI biology, integrated with foundation models to become the critical infrastructure layer for AI-driven biological discovery. Our first node opens in King’s Cross, London, with several integrated workcells and two scientific verticals, protein science and functional genomics, online by mid-2027. Our customers range from foundation model labs to global pharma.

We are hiring a Chemistry Principal Scientist to develop the strategy for chemistry at Substrate. This is a deliberately exploratory hire. Your job is to figure out what shape a chemistry vertical should take, whether the case for it holds, and what the day-1 architecture should look like if it does. Depending on what you find, the role evolves: you may grow into the Chemistry Lead position, a Head of Chemistry may be recruited above you, or your chemistry expertise folds into the protein science and functional genomics verticals where it is needed regardless. All three paths are real.

About Substrate

Substrate is spinning out of Automata, the UK lab automation company that has built the workcell platform our labs run on. Our four co-founders are Mostafa ElSayed (CEO and founder of Automata), Oli Hoy (formerly VP Customer Experience at Automata), Alexey Morgunov (AI Scientist co-founder, leading the intelligence software product), and a Founding Biology Lead joining shortly. We are aiming to have ramped up to 32 people by the end of Q1 2027.

We are funded in parallel by a combination of venture funding and government grants. We are not a cloud lab and we are not a CRO. We are an autonomous lab platform with closed-loop integration available as one operating mode for foundation model partners.

The role

You will own the chemistry strategy at Substrate. If we build the vertical, it will mirror our protein science vertical but for small molecule therapeutic candidates: making the molecules through some combination of on-site synthesis, pre-sourced precursors with on-site coupling, and external procurement, and testing them through a portfolio of characterisation assays designed for closed-loop work with generative AI. The use case we are most interested in is a model asking for a large set of candidate molecules and Substrate making and testing what is possible quickly, in a tighter cycle than current CROs can deliver.

Your job is to develop the strategy for this space: the right architecture for the make/buy/precursor decision tree given the molecule classes our customers most need, the day-1 assay portfolio that sits on top of these candidates, where the gaps are in what existing automated chemistry platforms can do, and where the customer demand signal sits between foundation model labs and pharma R&D.

You will spend significant time with Alexey as a weekly thought partner; otherwise the work is autonomous and self-directed. You will write up the strategy iteratively and present a clear recommendation to the co-founders by roughly month nine to twelve. If the recommendation is to build, you may grow into the Chemistry Lead position, or a Head of Chemistry may be recruited above you. If the recommendation is to hold, the role evolves into chemistry support across the protein science and functional genomics verticals (conjugation work, small molecule perturbations, related supply-chain decisions) rather than ending.

What you will do in your first twelve months

FIST 90 DAYS:

  • Land in the team. Set up workspace at our King’s Cross site and start the strategy scan in two directions: the foundation-model landscape for generative chemistry, and the chemistry-automation industry.

  • Map the chemical-space coverage problems the model builders are prioritising. Map the gaps in what existing automated chemistry platforms can do today, especially where customer quality requirements sit above the line.

  • Begin customer conversations alongside Mostafa with foundation model labs and pharma R&D contacts. Learn what they find painful when working with CROs today, and what is already commodity for them.

MONTHS 4 TO 8

  • Sharpen the strategy. For each candidate molecule class and assay readout, assess what Substrate could realistically operate at quality, what mix of on-site synthesis and external procurement makes sense, and what the customer demand signal looks like.

  • Continue tracking the foundation-model landscape as it evolves. Which generative-chemistry directions are converging on something Substrate’s autonomous chemistry could become the execution layer for, and which are still purely model-side work.

  • Draft the strategy document iteratively. If trending toward greenlight, begin sketching the day-1 chemistry assay portfolio, the make/buy/precursor architecture, and the workcell shape that would carry them.

MONTHS 9 TO 12

  • Close the strategy. Present a clear recommendation to the co-founders: build a standalone chemistry vertical, hold the bet and fold chemistry into the existing verticals, or some variant in between.

  • If the recommendation is greenlight: transition into Chemistry Lead build-out work, or into first-hire-under-Head-of-Chemistry mode, depending on which path the co-founders take.

  • If the recommendation is hold: transition into chemistry support across the protein science and functional genomics verticals.

Who you are

You are a chemist who is excited about an open scoping mandate rather than a defined assay portfolio. You enjoy research-mode work as much as hands-on bench work. You write good assessments and can hold a value-proposition argument together while you go gather the evidence to test it.

You have deep chemistry training and a working sense of the chemistry-automation industry: what existing platforms can do, where their gaps are, and where customer quality requirements sit above what current instrumentation delivers. You can have a credible conversation with a pharma R&D chemist about what they actually use, or with a foundation-model researcher about the chemical-space coverage their model needs.

You are comfortable working largely autonomously, with Alexey as your weekly thought partner and otherwise self-directed. You are comfortable with the three-fork future of this role and would rather know all three paths are real than have one of them sold to you.

MUST HAVE

  • PhD in synthetic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, or a closely adjacent discipline.

  • A couple of years of post-PhD industrial experience (pharma R&D, biotech, or a chemistry-flavoured CRO) where small molecule therapeutic candidate generation and characterisation were part of the day job.

  • Working familiarity with the small molecule therapeutic assay landscape: binding, biophysical, ADMET, cell-based characterisation, or analogous readouts.

  • Working knowledge of automated, flow, and high-throughput chemistry, and where the existing chemistry-automation industry can and cannot reach today.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Direct experience working with or alongside customers (pharma partners, foundation model labs, or AI-native biotech) on assay or workflow design.

  • Published work on automated, flow, or high-throughput chemistry, or on closed-loop generative chemistry workflows.

  • Background near AI / ML, computational chemistry, or scientific computing.

  • Experience working at the boundary between chemistry and other scientific disciplines (biology, screening, ADMET).

Why this is unusual

Most senior chemistry roles at venture-backed companies sit either inside an established platform that has already committed to chemistry, or inside a pharma R&D group running an internal chemistry pipeline. This is neither. You will be the person who decides whether Substrate commits to chemistry as a standalone vertical, by doing the work to figure out what shape that vertical should take and whether the case for it holds.

Some chemists find that openness energising: the chance to scope a strategic bet, shape it from the ground up, and either lead the build-out or hand it off to a more senior Head of Chemistry. If the standalone bet does not greenlight, chemistry expertise is still needed across our other verticals, so the work continues, just inside a different scope. Worth knowing in advance whether this kind of openness fits how you want to work.

Compensation and equity

We pay competitively against the London market for PhD-level chemists at venture-backed companies, calibrated to seniority and to the specific scope of this role. We will discuss numbers with serious candidates after first conversations.

Options on the standard four-year vest with a one-year cliff. The specific quantum reflects the scoping nature of the hire and will be discussed with serious candidates.

How we work

Working pattern is hybrid with an in-person bias dictated by the team. You will be at our King’s Cross site most days, particularly during the research-mode phase where the work benefits from being close to Alexey and the rest of the founding team. If and when the chemistry vertical greenlights and bench work begins, the cadence shifts to lab-based.

30 days annual leave. A learning budget you can use for conferences, courses, books, and time. The founding team operates on a weekly cadence with a Monday planning meeting and a Friday close, and a quarterly offsite. We are direct with each other, we write things down, and we expect to be challenged.

The team you will join

You will report to Alexey Morgunov, our science and AI focused co-founder. Alexey is your weekly thought partner on the strategy and your direction-setter through the scoping phase. You will work alongside Mostafa on customer conversations, with foundation model labs primarily and with pharma R&D contacts secondarily, and with the Heads of Protein Science and Functional Genomics on a peer-to-peer basis.

You are the first and currently only chemistry hire. Substrate is currently three co-founders growing to roughly 32 people by the end of Q1 2027.

How to apply

Apply via Ashby with whatever you think shows your work best: a CV, a published paper or thesis chapter you are proud of, a piece of writing on a chemistry-or-adjacent topic, a value-proposition argument you have made for an idea you thought was worth pursuing. We read everything that comes in.

Our process is three stages. An initial conversation with Alexey to understand what you want from the role and what we want from it. Followed by a technical session covering your chemistry background, your read on the chemistry-automation industry and the foundation-model landscape, and how you would shape the strategy. Finally, an in-person founder-team session at our King’s Cross site covering scope, terms, the conditional nature of the role, and any final questions. We aim to move fast on candidates we are excited about; expect roughly two to three weeks end to end.

If you are not sure whether you are a fit, send a note anyway. The most useful conversations we have had so far have been with people who were not sure.

Substrate is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background.

title: Analyst Lead, Cybersecurity
description:
Are you curious, motivated and forward-thinking? At FIS, you will have the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging and relevant issues in financial services and technology. Our talented people empower us, and we believe in being part of a team that is open, collaborative, entrepreneurial, passionate and above all fun.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Cybersecurity Analyst Senior to support strategic cybersecurity, risk and governance activities for a significant banking client. This is a varied role that blends business analysis, project delivery, cybersecurity governance and client-facing assurance. You will work closely with client stakeholders, product teams, technology teams and security SMEs to translate cybersecurity requirements into practical, trackable outcomes.

The role will help define, maintain and improve the way product and service solutions are assessed, governed and delivered against cybersecurity requirements. It is well suited to someone who can operate across business and technical stakeholders, understands cyber risk and control expectations, and can bring structure, clarity and momentum to complex initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead requirements gathering and analysis for cybersecurity requirements across applications, infrastructure, network services, controls and operational processes.

  • Perform business analysis of client needs and internal requirements, identifying solutions for non-standard tasks, control gaps and risk-based queries.

  • Collaborate with senior client stakeholders, product managers, delivery teams and technical architects to shape secure business architecture and implementation outcomes.

  • Review functional designs, business process designs and solution artefacts to identify cybersecurity risks, missing requirements, control gaps or implementation dependencies.

  • Track security requirements, risks, vulnerabilities, exceptions and remediation actions through to accountable ownership and closure.

  • Prepare governance reporting for internal and external stakeholders, including incident, risk, vulnerability, exception, control gap and remediation reporting.

  • Support client assurance activities by contributing to clear responses, evidence gathering and status updates against cybersecurity obligations and agreed commitments.

  • Work along with the team to help drive consistent cyber risk management practices across stakeholders by improving documentation, issue tracking, reporting cadence and decision visibility.

What You Will Need:

  • Strong experience in business analysis, project coordination or project management, ideally within a PMO, technology delivery or cybersecurity governance environment.

  • Demonstrated exposure to cybersecurity, technology risk, systems governance, control frameworks and operational reporting.

  • Ability to engage confidently with senior stakeholders, clients, product teams, technical architects and delivery teams.

  • Strong written communication skills, with the ability to produce concise governance updates, risk summaries, meeting outputs and client-ready documentation.

  • Practical understanding of risk, vulnerability, incident, control gap or remediation management processes.

  • Ability to translate technical and cybersecurity requirements into business actions, ownership, milestones and measurable outcomes.

  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Business Analysis, Project Management or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

Bonus If You Have:

  • Knowledge of industry standards and assurance frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, or similar regulatory and control frameworks.

  • Experience working with banking, financial services, fintech or highly regulated client environments.

  • Experience with governance, risk and compliance tooling, vulnerability management processes, risk acceptance workflows or audit evidence management.

  • Familiarity with cloud, infrastructure, network security, application security or operational resilience concepts.

  • Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, PMP, PRINCE2, or business analysis certifications.

What We Offer You:

A career at FIS is more than just a job. It is a chance to shape the future of fintech. At FIS, we offer you:

  • Always-on learning and development.

  • A flexible, hybrid work environment.

  • Competitive salary and benefits, including medical insurance and an employee share scheme.

title: Insight & Analytics Strategist
description:
Who We Are

Digible is a privately owned and operated digital marketing company founded in 2017 with a mission to bring cutting-edge solutions to the multifamily industry. We offer a full suite of digital services, alongside Fiona, our predictive analytics platform, the first of its kind.

At Digible, we take pride in our collaborative, transparent, and authentic culture. Since 2021, we've been recognized as a Top Workplace in Colorado and secured the #8 spot in the Best Places to Work Multifamily rankings. From our hiring process to our All Hands meetings and Town Halls, our values are at the core of everything we do.

We believe diversity fuels innovation, and we strive to create an inclusive environment where everyone can bring their authentic selves to work. If you're ready to do the best work of your career, we'd love to have you on the team!

Core Values

  • Authenticity. The commitment to be steadfast and genuine with our actions and communication toward everyone we touch.
  • Curiosity. The belief that a deep and fundamental curiosity (the "why") in our work is vital to company innovation and evolution.
  • Focus. The collective will to remain completely devoted and ultimately accountable to our deliverables.
  • Humility. The recognition and daily practice that "we" is always greater than "I".
  • Happiness. The decision to prioritize passion and love for what we do above everything else.

The Role

Digible is looking for an Insights & Analytics Strategist to join our Data team.

Our Data team owns the governed semantic layer, the Silver and Gold data models, and the trusted metric definitions that the rest of Digible builds on. This role sits next to that foundation but faces outward. It closes the gap between the data we already collect and the decisions our agency teams make every day for our roughly 1,000 multifamily clients.

You'll dig into data sources that aren't being used well today, turn them into client and business insight, and work directly with our Agency Solutions team to put that insight into action on real client accounts. This isn't a dashboard-building role, and it isn't a pure data engineering role either. Think of it as the connective tissue between the two: you take the semantic layer's trusted foundation, add in data nobody has operationalized yet, and put both to work alongside the agency. We'll measure your success by the decisions and outcomes you influence on client accounts, not just the reports you hand off.

You'll report to our Director of Data and partner most closely with our Director of Agency Solutions, sitting within a roughly 20-person technology department. You'll also work with Analytics Engineering on data foundations and Data Science when a question needs deeper modeling.

You'll Love This Job If You:

  • Embrace Digible's core values: authenticity, curiosity, focus, humility, and happiness
  • Enjoy turning a pile of underused data (call recordings, CRM activity, client financials) into a clear, defensible insight
  • Care as much about driving action as about being right. You're not satisfied until the insight changes what someone does
  • Like being embedded with a business team, understanding their goals well enough to see their next question coming
  • Move easily between analysis, storytelling, and stakeholder conversations
  • Don't mind taking a manual, one-off analysis and turning it into a repeatable pipeline or report
  • Already use AI tools as a normal part of how you explore, synthesize, and communicate
  • Are comfortable in ambiguity and don't need someone else to define your scope for you
  • Bring a customer-first mentality and genuine curiosity to your work
  • Want the impact of your work to show up in a client outcome, not just a delivered report

What You'll Do:

  • Operationalize Customer Analytics data. Build the pipeline and analysis to turn call and meeting intelligence into structured signal the agency can act on, closing today's biggest analytical blind spot
  • Deliver client and account insight that goes beyond financial performance: client segmentation, health signals, and account-level narrative that support client dossiers and QBR prep
  • Work embedded in agency workflows, close enough to Agency Solutions and account teams to understand their open questions, turning ad hoc requests into recurring, trustworthy analysis
  • Turn insight into action. Don't stop at the finding; work with agency partners to define the recommended action, track whether it was taken, and follow up on the outcome
  • Build analytics products that give account teams and clients a shared view of account health
  • Be a bridge to the governed semantic layer by pulling from and helping extend the Analytics Engineering team's trusted metric definitions, rather than building parallel, ungoverned ones. Flag gaps back to that team instead of working around them
  • Prove out ROI early. As a new, cross-functional role, you'll need a track record of concrete, attributable wins that justify continued investment

How Success Will Be Measured:

  • First 90 days: A subset of customer analytics data operationalized into at least one repeatable analysis, and a first client insight delivered and acted on by the agency team
  • Days 90 to 180: A small portfolio of insight-to-action wins tied to specific client accounts, with outcomes tracked, and clear handoff patterns established with Analytics Engineering for anything that should graduate into the governed semantic layer
  • Ongoing: A growing, attributable track record of insights that changed what the agency did on a client account, not just insights that were delivered

What You Should Have:

  • 4+ years of experience in an analytics, insights, or analytics-engineering role, ideally with direct exposure to a client-facing or agency/consulting environment
  • Strong SQL skills and comfort querying a modern cloud warehouse (we use Snowflake) to go from raw data to insight on your own
  • Experience turning unstructured or semi-structured data (call transcripts, CRM notes, support tickets) into structured, analyzable signal
  • A track record of working directly with non-technical stakeholders: shaping a question, delivering an answer, and following through to action
  • Comfort with BI and reporting tools for both client-facing and internal analysis

title: Director, Supplier Quality
description:
Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Director of Supplier Quality to join the Global Operations team and lead our global quality management efforts across technical hardgoods and softgoods. This position will be responsible for establishing and executing a comprehensive quality strategy that spans global teams, including product management, R&D, manufacturing facilities, and external suppliers. Your leadership will ensure that we not only meet rigorous quality standards but also maintain a competitive edge in a fast-paced global marketplace. This role demands a strategic thinker with a proven track record in leading cross-functional teams, managing complex global product creation processes, and driving continuous quality improvements at every stage of the product lifecycle. This senior leadership role will oversee all aspects of Total Quality Management (TQM), driving excellence in both product creation and operational processes to meet and exceed customer expectations.

This position reports to the Vice President of Strategic Sourcing, Procurement and Supplier Quality and is based out of Irvine, CA.

As the Director of Supplier Quality, you will have an opportunity to:

  • Lead Global Quality Strategy: Develop and execute a global quality management strategy that aligns with Revelyst’s business goals across three primary platforms: Adventure Sports, Outdoor Performance, and Precision Sports. Define and communicate quality objectives, priorities, and key results across regions and product categories.

  • Quality Transformation & Customer Experience: Lead the ongoing transformation of Revelyst's global quality organization from a reactive inspection-based model to a prevention-based quality culture. Drive enterprise-wide focus on customer experience, defect prevention, quality ownership, and continuous improvement through people, process, systems, and supplier partnerships.

  • Global Quality Assurance and Control: Lead the design and implementation of QA/QC processes that ensure the highest standards for all products, from design through production. Partner with internal teams and external suppliers to ensure that all technical hardgoods and softgoods meet functional, safety, and aesthetic standards. Assess production operations at a global scale to ensure compliance with quality standards.

  • Compliance & Regulatory Oversight: Ensure that Revelyst products meet all relevant industry standards, legal requirements, and environmental regulations globally. Stay current with changes in quality standards and regulations, and work closely with compliance teams to ensure ongoing alignment.

  • Continuous Improvement & Innovation: Lead initiatives to identify and implement process improvements that enhance product quality, reduce waste, and drive cost efficiencies. Introduce innovative quality management practices that align with best-in-class industry standards.

  • Team Leadership & Development: Inspire and lead a diverse, globally dispersed team of quality professionals. Oversee hiring, training, and professional development efforts to build a high-performing, collaborative team that is equipped to meet evolving challenges. Foster a culture of accountability, continuous learning, and quality excellence.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with senior management, R&D, product management, and operations teams to integrate quality into the product development lifecycle from concept to consumer. Collaborate with Global Sourcing, Procurement, Manufacturing and Supply Chain teams to align supplier quality expectations, scorecards, and escalation protocols. Provide expert guidance on quality-related decision-making at every stage of product creation.

  • Supplier Quality Management: Develop and implement a global supplier quality strategy that ensures consistent standards across all regions. Lead supplier audits, qualification, and performance monitoring programs to ensure compliance with quality expectations and continuous improvement.

  • Vendor Quality Risk Mitigation: Establish proactive risk assessment and mitigation strategies for supplier quality issues, including contingency planning and corrective action protocols.

  • Supplier Development & Engagement: Partner with Procurement and Sourcing teams to drive supplier development initiatives, including training, capability assessments, and joint improvement plans.

  • Executive Reporting: Provide regular updates and executive-level reports on quality performance, compliance, continuous improvement initiatives, and key performance metrics. Highlight trends and emerging issues and ensure that leadership is informed about quality-related risks and opportunities.

  • Global Quality Systems & Metrics: Standardize quality processes, documentation, and KPIs across all regions and supplier tiers to ensure consistency and transparency. Implement and maintain a global Quality Management System (QMS) that supports real-time visibility in supplier performance and product quality. Define and track key quality metrics (e.g., PPM, OTIF, NCRs, CAPAs) and drive accountability through regular reviews and dashboards.

You have:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field (Master's preferred).

  • 10+ years of experience in quality management roles within a global, consumer products environment, including leadership roles in quality assurance, quality control, or Total Quality Management (TQM).

  • Demonstrated quality leadership experience supporting global product categories like those within Revelyst's Adventure Sports platform, including technical apparel, helmets, protective equipment, hydration systems, packs, softgoods, and engineered hardgoods. Proven success managing quality throughout the product lifecycle, from design validation and supplier qualification through mass production and post-market performance.

  • Proven track record in managing global product creation processes, ideally in both hardgoods and softgoods categories within the sports or outdoor industry.

  • Strong expertise in implementing and leading global quality management systems (QMS), including familiarity with ISO standards, and Helmet Certification Standards - ASTM, CPSC, ECE, DOT, FIM etc.

  • Exceptional leadership and team-building skills, with the ability to inspire, motivate, and drive performance across geographically dispersed teams.

  • Strong strategic thinking capabilities, with the ability to align quality initiatives with business objectives and improve overall product quality and operational efficiency.

  • Expertise in data analysis and trend identification to inform decision-making and identify areas for improvement.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across all levels of the organization, including senior leadership, product teams, and external stakeholders.

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, changing environment and manage multiple priorities effectively.

  • Global travel flexibility is needed to support our international operations and quality initiatives.

title: Clinical Specialist, Joint Replacement - Columbia, MO
description:
Overview

As a Clinical Specialist at Stryker, you will help improve orthopedic surgeries around the world and play a direct role in our mission of making healthcare better. In this role, you will build deep clinical and technical expertise across both robotic (Mako SmartRobotics™) and manual orthopedic procedures. You will support surgeons in the operating room by assisting with pre-operative planning, case preparation, system setup, and real-time procedural workflows to ensure safe, accurate, and efficient outcomes.

You will gain hands-on experience working with Mako technology—including CT-based planning, implant sizing, registration, and intra-operative support—while also developing strong competency in manual procedures, instrumentation, and OR protocols. Through shadowing experienced team members, supporting product demonstrations, and participating in labs and education programs, you will learn the systems, processes, and best practices that define world-class clinical support.

This role requires adaptability, steady composure, and strong problem-solving in a fast-paced surgical environment. Because patients’ needs don’t follow business hours, you will also participate in on-call coverage, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, to ensure uninterrupted support for urgent cases and time-sensitive customer needs.

What You Will Do

  • Gain competency in solo case coverage for manual and robotic procedures through hands-on training.

  • Troubleshoot technical issues confidently and efficiently in the operating room.

  • Learn and support workflow for daily account coordination, including inventory management and logistics.

  • Shadow experienced teammates to understand territory dynamics and surgeon preferences.

  • Participate in product demonstrations, cadaver labs, education programs, and customer training events.

  • Build and maintain strong, trust-based relationships with surgeons, OR staff, and cross-functional partners.

Preferred:

title: Volunteer & Community Engagement Coordinator
description:

We're looking for a highly organized, relationship-driven Volunteer & Community Engagement Coordinator who enjoys bringing people together, creating exceptional volunteer experiences, and supporting the behind-the-scenes operations that help our mission thrive.


In this role, you'll welcome and lead volunteer groups, build relationships with community partners, help recruit volunteers, and ensure every volunteer leaves feeling valued and inspired. You'll also support inventory, purchasing, and production planning to ensure volunteer events have the materials needed to succeed.


This is an ideal opportunity for someone who is passionate about nonprofit work, community engagement, volunteer management, and creating meaningful experiences while balancing people-focused work with operational excellence.


Location: San Jose, California (Regular on-site work required)

Why You'll Love Working at RAFT


At RAFT, your work directly supports students, educators, and communities.You'll have the opportunity to:

  • Make a meaningful impact through a mission-driven nonprofit organization.
  • Create memorable volunteer experiences for individuals, schools, and corporate teams.
  • Collaborate with a creative, passionate, and supportive team.
  • See the direct impact of your work on thousands of students each year.

We also offer:

  • Competitive salary
  • Comprehensive health benefits
  • 403(b) retirement plan with employer match
  • Performance bonuses
  • Three weeks of vacation
  • One week of paid sick leave
  • Paid holidays and holiday shutdown


What You'll Do

Volunteer & Community Engagement

  • Recruit new volunteers through community outreach, nonprofit partnerships, local organizations, and online platforms.
  • Build relationships that encourage volunteers to return and become long-term supporters of RAFT.
  • Set up and break down volunteer workstations while ensuring projects and materials are ready for each event.
  • Coordinate materials needed for volunteer kit production.

Help ensure our volunteer events and STEAM kit production run smoothly by:

  • Supporting purchasing, inventory management, and production planning using NetSuite.

  • Preparing purchase orders and working with suppliers.

  • Performing kit builds and inventory transactions in NetSuite.
  • Supporting retail operations by processing Point of Sale transactions when needed.


What We’re Looking For

We're excited to meet someone who has:

  • Two or more years of experience in volunteer management, nonprofit organizations, community engagement, education, event coordination, or a related field.
  • A passion for serving others and creating meaningful volunteer experiences.
  • Outstanding interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Experience coordinating events, volunteer programs, or community activities.
  • Comfort learning technology, inventory systems, or ERP platforms such as NetSuite.

title: Industrial Hygienist
description:
At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Industrial Hygienist

Location: any of the US manufacturing sites listed, or Remote US with 50% travel

Department: EHS
Reports To: Global EHS Manager

Jabil is seeking an experienced Industrial Hygienist to identify, evaluate, and control occupational health hazards within manufacturing environments. This role will focus on chemical safety, exposure assessments, industrial hygiene monitoring, regulatory compliance, and implementation of effective risk reduction strategies.

What can you expect to do?

  • Assist in the development, training and roll-out of assessment program for chemical exposures.
  • Conduct qualitative and quantitative exposure assessments for chemical, physical, and biological hazards.
  • Manage risks associated with specialty chemicals, electronic manufacturing including adhesives, solvents, conformal coatings, lasers, x-rays, hydrofluoric acid (HF), and other hazardous materials.
  • Assist in the design and implementation of industrial hygiene programs, including air monitoring, noise monitoring, and chemical exposure assessments.
  • May perform personal and area air sampling using pumps, badges, and direct-reading instruments.
  • Evaluate engineering controls, such as local exhaust ventilation (LEV) systems, fume hoods, cleanroom laminar flow systems and containment systems such as isolators and glove boxes, using airflow measurement equipment and surrogate monitoring.
  • Conduct workplace hazard assessments and recommend engineering, administrative, and PPE controls.
  • Provide employee training on occupational health and chemical safety topics.
  • Interpret and apply OSHA, NIOSH, ACGIH, and other applicable regulations.
  • Prepare technical reports, maintain monitoring records, and communicate findings to management.
  • Partner with Engineering, Facilities, Operations, and Maintenance teams to implement effective exposure controls.
  • Provide support to Regional EHS team and sites for implementation and technical assistance, upon request.
  • May join global assessment program as auditor/SME upon request.
  • May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

What is the experience needed to be successful in this role?

  • Bachelor's degree in Industrial Hygiene, Occupational Health, Environmental Health & Safety, Chemistry, Engineering, or related field.
  • 3-5 years of industrial hygiene experience in manufacturing, semiconductor, pharmaceutical, electronics, or related industries.
  • Experience with exposure monitoring, risk assessments, ventilation evaluations, and chemical safety programs.
  • Strong knowledge of occupational health regulations and exposure limits.

Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 115,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

About Abbott

Abbott is a global healthcare leader, creating breakthrough science to improve people’s health. We’re always looking towards the future, anticipating changes in medical science and technology.

Our diagnostic solutions are used in hospitals, laboratories, and clinics around the globe. The crucial information derived from our tests, instruments and informatics systems are often the first step in patient care decision making for hundreds of health conditions from heart attacks to blood disorders to infectious diseases and cancers.

Working at Abbott

At Abbott, you can do work that matters, grow, and learn, care for yourself and family, be your true self and live a full life. You’ll also have access to:

  • Career development with an international company where you can grow the career you dream of.

  • Employees can qualify for free medical coverage in our Health Investment Plan (HIP) PPO medical plan in the next calendar year.

  • An excellent retirement savings plan with high employer contribution

  • Tuition reimbursement, the Freedom 2 Save student debt program and FreeU education benefit - an affordable and convenient path to getting a bachelor’s degree.

  • A company recognized as a great place to work in dozens of countries around the world and named one of the most admired companies in the world by Fortune.

  • A company that is recognized as one of the best big companies to work for as well as a best place to work for diversity, working mothers, female executives, and scientists.

The Opportunity

  • This position is field based remote.

  • Territory: Greenville, NC. The incumbent can live in the area.

  • Travel up to 20%.

  • Must have a Valid Driver’s License.

We’re hiring a Field Service Engineer within our Diagnostics Division. This is a field-based, remote role that covers Greenville, NC.

As a Field Service Engineer II, you’ll support customers as a trusted technical expert, responsible for installing, maintaining, and troubleshooting diagnostic instruments while ensuring compliance and customer satisfaction. You’ll manage your territory, resolve complex issues, and partner cross-functionally to deliver exceptional service and achieve business goals. Your work ensures reliable diagnostics that directly impact patient care.

title: Director of Development
description:
Scope of Work: The Director of Development is responsible for all aspects of fund development, with a focus on major gifts and planned giving. In partnership with the CEO, the Director of Development leads and is responsible for ensuring that SAAF meets or exceeds fundraising goals. Functions as a leader, peer, support, and resource for Development Team in the areas of donor and community relationships, volunteerism, public relations, branding, marketing, budget management and external communications.

Primary Job Duties:

  • Develops and leads SAAF’s overall revenue development strategies in consultation and partnership with the CEO, in alignment with the organization’s strategic direction.

title: Part-time Mammography Tech
location: Advocate Condell Medical Center - 801 S Milwaukee Ave
description:
Department:

36324 Advocate Condell Medical Center - Mammography

Status:

Part time

Benefits Eligible:

Yes

Hours Per Week:

20

Schedule Details/Additional Information:

Day Shift 7:30-4, Saturday rotation

Pay Range:

$35.50 - $53.25

Major Responsibilities:
Performs screening and diagnostic mammograms and bone density testing on physician referred patients according to established clinical protocols and MQSA Quality Guidelines.
1)Delivers patient care in accordance with department/hospital standards; changes to adapt to customer/department needs.

2)Uses proper telephone scripting at all times.

3)Accurately documents patient images electronically.

4)Positions the breast to obtain the appropriate standard and alternative views.

5)Adjusts positioning and technique for thorough quality exam based on patient's anatomy and condition.

6)Keeps patient informed and encourages patient to ask questions regarding own care.

7)Applies radiation protection to patient in accordance with accepted radiation protection standards for mammography.

8)Documents patient history and other pertinent clinical information in RIS or Penrad computer database,when available, designed for this purpose.

9)Selects technical factors to ensure appropriate capture of digital images.

Prepares and processes patient clinical and demographic information, using RIS or Penrad, when available, and ensures the accuracy of historic and current information.
1)Secures or otherwise makes arrangements for mammography films performed elsewhere to be sent to the Advocate Condell Breast Imaging Center.

2)Obtains current personal and family history of breast disease using computer databases, i.e. Penrad to record information.

3)Secures patient consent forms as may be required; these consents include Pregnancy Consent and Verification, Authorization Form to Release Medical Information and Consent for Interventional Procedures.

4)Documents the presence of a physical lump, moles or other skin lesions with BB Markers and draws or labels breast diagrams in Penrad, indicationg location of anatomical scars, pervious surgical sites or other abnormalities.

5)Documents procedure information in RIS or Penrad, when available.

6)Acknowleges patient exam completion in RIS.

Prepares mammographic images, scans documentation and determines when radiographic exam adheres to department standard for interpretation by the Radiologist.
1)Procures historical images and prepares these images for review by the Radiologist.

2)Ensures the presence of any previous diagnostic or pathology reports.

3)Prepares current images for dictation by ensuring proper image identification and scanning orders into PACs.

4)Ensures all paperwork, forms and diagrams are complete and accurate and merged into PACs therefore ready for use by the supervising Radiologist.

5)Provides accurate notes detailing any comments, unique circumstances or observation in Medical Record or Penrad, when available that will aid the Radiologist in dictating the mammographic report.

6)Processes and sends to the appropriate areas, procedure requisitons, history forms, consents and other documentation as it may be generated.

Provides pre-procedure, procedure and post-procedure education and instruction to the patient appropriate to the patient's needs and requirements.
1)Participates in advanced mammographic procedures such as needle localizations, galactograms, Stereotactic biopsy and specimen radiographs.

2)On a pre-procedure basis, establishes patient comfort by familiarizing the patient with the equipment and aspects of the procedure to be performed.

3)Demonstration of how the equipment operates, the use of compression and address any questions the patient may have on a procedural basis, the technologist must be able to identify the anxious and fearful patient and be able to modify both the mammographic routine and their communication style in order to reduce the patient's anxiety and complete the study.

4)On a post-procedure basis, the mammography technologist must be able to describe in sufficient detail the process by which the images will be processed and read by the Radiologists and how the diagnostic reports are communicated to the referring physician and how layman report is sent to patient's home.

5)Maintains patient modesty and confidentiality throughout the entire patient visit.

6)The technologist must be viewed as being helpful to the patient by facilitating or directing the patient to other resources in the patient's quest to seek additional information or address other issues outside the scope of the mammography service; the technologist must offer to assist this patient in this effort.

7)Properly labels and identifies specimens to go to lab.

Performs mammography equipment quality control and quality assurance tests established to meet MQSA Quality Control/Quality Assurance Standards and equipment manufacturer's recommendations.
1)Performs start-up and shut-down procedures according to established procedures.

2)Performs equipment warm-up and calibration tests according to manufacturer's recommended frequency.

3)Cleans illuminator panels and surfaces as needed to remove sources of dirt, contamination and artifacts.

4)Cleans and disinfects equipment surfaces that come into direct contact with the patient's skin.

Delivery of Patient Care in accordance with departmental standards of continued quality improvement.
1)Follows Accrediting Organization requirements regarding safety and protection of patients and staff.

2)Must promote patient safety by reporting of issues through established channels and participating as requested in saftey initiatives.

3)Demonstrates excellent communication skills by answering questions from all customers in an appropriate and respectful manner.

4)Takes an active role in making sure the general appearance of the department is clean, uncluttered and calm.

5)Maintains positive customer relations following prescribed department policies.

6)Participates in team problem solving issues that would improve patient care, department operations, image quality, interdepartmental relationships and employee satisfaction.

Ensure a secure and safe patient and work environment by maintaining continued awareness of safety hazards.
1)Adheres to safety practices and provides a safe work environment for self and others.

2)Must promote patient safey by reporting of issues through established channels and participate as requested in safety initiatives.

Education/Experience Required:
- Graduate of AMA Approved Program in Radiologic Technology - 1 - 2 years experience as Radiologic Technologist or sonographer - 40 hours of specialized training and continuing education in mammography - Knowledge of breast anatomy - Need to recognize patients experiencing fear or anxiety - Needs to be able to recognize needs and behaviors of a variety of age groups of patients treated, i.e. understand the differences of female growth and development, and look for signs of normal aging; degree of under- standing and physical limitation related to age

Licensure, Registration and/or Certification Required:

- Registered Radiologic Technologist/ARRT - IDNS License

  • Basic Life Support (BLS) for Healthcare Providers certification issued by the American Heart Association (AHA).


Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Required:
- Good verbal and written communication skills - Ability to handle anxious and fearful patients - Demonstrated technical skills as a radiographer -Knowledge of mammography positioning.

Physical Requirements and Working Conditions:
- Position best performed by a female who enjoys working with women in health related issues - Must understand and take serious the social and psychological issues associated with mammography and breast cancer. - Must keep informed of changes in regulatory requirements, including FDA, IEMA, ACR, and MQSA - Must engage in continuous learning and review of new and emerging technologies - Must be flexible and be able to adapt to a rapidly changing environment and growing patient volume - Must demonstrate confidence in one’s own ability and have a calming effect on patients and others
If position has direct patient care or direct patient contact the following lifting requirement supersedes any previous lifting requirement effective 06/01/2015. Ability to lift up to 35 pounds without assistance. For patient lifts of over 35 pounds, or when patient is unable to assist with the lift, patient handling equipment is expected to be used, with at least one other associate, when available. Unique patient lifting/movement situations will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.
